### lane design-tweaks — the Design window v2 lane C: Tweaks, the free knobs (B-6351, design 003 §2 S4)

The owner asked for the online Claude Design replicated (2026-10-02 20:32 PDT); design 003 ranks Tweaks fourth ("genuinely new", free to move). The agent declares knobs in design.json, the owner moves them in OUR panel, the artboards restyle at once with no agent turn, and the values live in `user.json` — the contract's user layer, written ONLY by the hub on the owner's act (design 003 §2 "Two contract additions"; it ends F4's agent-and-human race on one file).

- **The contract.** design.json gains the closed key `tweaks`: ≤ 12 `{id, label?, kind: color|range|select|toggle, var: "--x" | attr: "data-x", default}` (+ range `min, max, step?, unit?` from a closed unit set; select 2–12 `options`); closed keys per kind, one knob per target, never `data-vibespace-…`, refusals by name (`tweaks[i].<key>`). `user.json` = `{v:1, tweaks:{id: value}}`, judged like any input; a value that no longer fits its knob, or a knob that is gone, is dropped and SAID (a warning), never applied.
- **Split by the viewer's budget.** design-model.js is bundled whole into public/design-viewer.js (test-design-canvas trips at 60 KB; lanes A + B took it from 44.6 to 55.2 KB; everything here would have made 67.5). It keeps only the list's shape, the fence word `tweakSay` / `tweakWordOk` (a value cannot close a rule, the style block or the root tag) and its walker pieces (`WALK`); each knob's rules, the user layer and the baking live in the new PURE **src/design-user-layer.js**, reaching the manifest through `validateManifest(json, {tweaks})` (`UL.validateDesign` = the hub's reader). Without the hook (the viewer, bundleCanvas / readBundle) the manifest carries no knobs — their values are baked. Viewer: 57.8 KB.
- **Baked where it is served.** `applyUser` writes EVERY declared knob (the user's value, else the default) into each artboard the read serves — the window, `preview`, publish: ONE `<style id="vibespace-tweaks">:root{… !important}</style>` at the head's start + ONE marked attribute run right after `<html` (the parser keeps the first of a repeated attribute). Found only at those two places by a linear tag walk, only when exactly ours ⇒ idempotent; every word re-judged at bake time.
- **Restyle in place.** A move posts `design-tweak {var|attr, value}` through the canvas's outgoing fence (FRAME_KINDS + 1) to every frame; the picker sets the root property (inline `!important`) or attribute from its parent only. The write says ONE `file-changed` for user.json; a re-read whose html differs from a LIVE frame's ONLY in the layer (`tweakSwap`) restyles it by message instead of reloading (design-canvas.js `setSwap` + a `live` flag) — on every device, scroll and state kept.
- **Hub.** design-engine.js reads user.json with the folder (O_NOFOLLOW; a link or non-file is said, `user_not_file`; ssh: the one read emits it, `@@ULINK` for a link), bakes in compose, watches it; `readMeta` (design.json + user.json; ssh = one command); `setTweaks` (one write chain per folder, merge, null = default, Reset; lstat + O_EXCL temp + rename, a link / directory refused by name; ssh = ONE `remoteUserWriteScript`: mktemp, base64, mv); `requestTweaks` ("+ Tweaks" = ONE `[Design tweaks]` line through THE belt down the comment's sender). Owner routes `GET` / `POST /api/design/tweaks`, `POST /api/design/tweaks/request` (an agent bearer 403). `check` / `show` print the knobs and what the user set (belted).

- **Shared-file hunks (for the integrator).** design-model.js: KEYS.top + `tweaks`; validateManifest's signature + the shape block + the return spread; the section before "the published page"; exports. design-engine.js: header, STATUS line, `UL` require, isWatchable, the remote read (`@@ULINK` + user.json in its loop + the parse line), readLocal (user.json in the read loop + `userOdd`), compose (`ul` line, `applyUser` on html, 1 return line), two `UL.validateDesign` reads, the tweaks block before "publish", agentView (2 lines), the returned API, module.exports. routes/design.js: header + 3 routes. design-canvas-model.js: import + FRAME_KINDS + 1 frameSay line. design-pick.js: header + 7 lines. design-canvas.js: header word, `swapFn`, the load flag, the srcdoc swap, `setSwap`. design-window.js: import, the bar button line, the mount + `ROW_ACTS.tweaks` lines. icons.js (`sliders`), style.css (one block after lane design-ask's), i18n zh/ja (one block), vibespace-design (usage line, `printTweaks`, 2 calls). - PURE `src/channel-search.js`: `snippetOf` (cut to 4 000 characters before any regex, markup stripped, entities decoded, then `peerName` — hidden characters, bidi, complete and dangling frames, ≤ 400), `snippetShape`, `mergeVendorHits`, `coverageOf`, `fullSearchVerdict` (not-supported › needs-scope › backoff › search-floor › the agents' share › search-minute › vendor-budget, each with its wait), the dialog's words.

### lane channels-first-read — the Channels panel's first read sends the first screen, not every conversation (B-3cf8, design 008)

**the first Channels open is instant on an account with tens of thousands of conversations: the list carries the rows that need attention and each account's newest, every other row is read a page at a time**

#### The first open stalled for seconds (B-3cf8, userW, 2026-10-02 after the 2.369.201 hotfix)

Measured on userW's pod (2.369.200): `GET /api/channels` answered 77 538 430 bytes, 1.49 s to first byte, ≈ 50 000 conversations (1 542 bytes a row) — `digest()` built a `rowView` for EVERY live conversation and every non-partial broadcast pushed the same list to every tab. The first screen draws the attention list, the agent groups, each account's newest 30 and All's newest 60.

- The shared predicate: `statusTag` & co. moved unchanged to PURE CJS `src/channel-focus.js` (`src/lib/channel-focus.js` re-exports it) beside `candidateOf(en, ob, now)` — the raw facts a tag is made of, one clause per tag, may over-include, never miss — and the page rules (`pageOrder` lastAt desc then key, `selectPage` one pass with a bounded heap, `pageCursor`, `queryOf` ≤ 100 characters, `textMatches` = filterRows' rule).
- `digest({keys, scope})`: `keys` = the partial broadcast, unchanged; `'first'` (the route's default and every non-partial broadcast) = adapters + `counts {all, byAdapter}` (the kept row facts) + totals + `conversations` = the attention rows (≤ 300, `attention {total, cut}`) and each account's newest 30 listed rows (`heads`, every account — an empty one too), built by `firstRead`: ONE pass, a rowView only for a candidate or a head; `'accounts'` (no rows); `'totals'`. A first read no longer forces the kept facts' re-sum.
- `rows({view, adapter, q, before, limit, keys, conv})` + `GET /api/channels/rows`: the next `limit` (1–200, default 60) after the cursor, no full sort; `q` over the ladder name / account label / last line with a sound prefilter (every letter-digit run of the query must sit in the raw title / participants / author names before the ladder is computed); bounds refused by name (400 `bad-request`), an unknown account 404; both routes refuse an agent's session / job bearer (403 `agent-forbidden`).
- The client: PURE `src/lib/channel-rows.js` (keyed store: `applyFirst` / `applyPage` / `applyBroadcast` — the never-loaded rule: a row is taken when it wears a tag or sorts inside a loaded list's range, else dropped; a page asked before a broadcast keeps the broadcast's row; a non-partial broadcast restarts the heads and marks the paged lists stale, the list on screen re-reads ≤ 200). The panel draws from it: the header counts from `counts` + `attention.cut`, All = the server's pages (60 a page), an account card = its head + pages of 200, each list's end loading the next page itself (owner 2026-10-03: seamless, no "Show more" — a sentinel watched one screen ahead, a skeleton row while read, ≤ 5 pages while the view does not move down, focus on the end reads on, a whole broadcast keeps the range), the filter = the attention rows at once + the server 250 ms after the last keystroke ("{n} more in All", All's search pages). The account ⋯ menu asks the account's count, not its loaded rows. The rail badge reads `?scope=totals`, the window's Re-authorize `?scope=accounts`, a chat card's link `rows?conv=`.
- verify r1: the attention list is the SERVER'S (`store.focus` — a row that lost its tag while the client was away left no ghost after a reconnect / a whole broadcast); past ATTENTION_MAX the cut keeps statusTag's TAG_ORDER first, then the newest, and `attention.cut` counts only the tagged rows not carried (a tagged head was counted twice); the search prefilter drops hidden characters for a row named by its participants / authors ("Bo<ZWSP>b" reads "Bob").
- MEASURED (test-channels-index-scale ⑨, work meter): the first read at 50 286 / 100 566 rows = 41.2 KB / 41.2 KB, 36 rowViews, 1.61 % / 1.57 % of the old whole list's work (47.7 / 95.4 MB on these lighter fixture rows); an account-level change broadcasts 41.3 KB; the client half (parse + applyFirst + groupListRows + firstScreen) 0.22 ms; a page of 60 from the middle 55.7 KB; a search linear (×1.99), 643 work units a row (the shown strings' bytes), 2.6× less than without the prefilter.
- Not done (separable, design S6): the agent's `list` bound.
- Gates: test-channel-rows (new, fast, 35 — the property candidateOf ⊇ statusTag over every tag kind at every window edge + its control, the first read = focusRows over the whole list, the store's tables, the full-list readers' census + its control), test-channels-index-scale ⑨ (+ 2 controls), test-channels-engine § design 008 (V3 paging under churn: 500 rows moved + 20 born between pages — no row twice, none lost; scopes; bounds; bearer refusals), test-channels-panel-redraw re-fixtured on paging (a page append keeps the drawn rows), test-channels-groups-e2e / -e2e await the server's pages.

### lane apps-one-card — an agent's install is ONE card and ONE click (design 009 S5, lane 2)

- **The card is structure, the words are the client's.** NEW PURE `src/app-card.js`: design 009 §4's proposal view (`{id, host, state, kind, app{name, labels, icon}, by, why, from, bytes, keeps, firstUse, details, digest}` + `planChanged` / `result`), `planSummary` (the engine's summary + the closure, the commands, a .deb's sha256 / scripts) and `shownDigest` (fnv32 ×2 over `shownFields` — what a card shows, never its state). The For-you item carries it as `card` (src/user-todos.js `normalizeCard`: plain data ≤ 24 KB, kept EXACTLY; `setCard`; a resolved card rides the snapshot face-only; Clear content… drops it — record-clear's todo shape). NEW PURE `src/lib/app-card-model.js` words it in en / zh / ja (`cardWords`, `detailLines`, `progressWords`, `openRowOf`).
- **One click.** `engine.approve(id, {shown})` = POST /api/apps/proposals/:id/approve: a card that is not the proposal as it stands ⇒ 409 plan_changed + the current card, nothing ran; else the STORED plan runs through the one slot (`expectDigest = p.digest`) in the background and every state move redraws the card (`syncCard`). A machine whose plan moved ⇒ plan_changed and the proposal TAKES the new plan (`planChanged`: "the plan changed — take another look"); a failure names its step (prepare / install / record, `stepOf`) and Try again is the same click; busy ⇒ 409. No second dialog. Mark done / Ignore still decline (onStatus, unchanged).
- **The surfaces.** The popup / phone sheet / mini inbox row (`appCardHtml`): title, who asks and why, where from and how big (a download's host; "official" only when a recipe vouches, else one unverified-publisher line), what the click gives (replay / home / system — Layer 1's "always there"), Layer 1's first-use line, TWO buttons, progress → Installed · Open, Try again, a Details fold; Reply / Mark done / Ignore / Copy / Clear content… behind ⋯. The For-you window shows the same card in its pane (actions `app-install, app-reject, more` · `app-retry` · `app-open`). Install is ARMED like Approve (press-arm). The window now also stamps its arm where the pane's item changes: render() stamped before holdSelection moved the selection, so a pane opened onto an item refused every press (found by test-apps-ui ②). The install dialog LEADS with the same summary (`appSummaryBlock`); the root sentence, the facts and the commands fold under Details; "1 packages" fixed; the log hides the slot's `= run` / `= ok` lines (review I13).
- **For lane apps-install-core (the shared contract):** the view reads `p.app {name, labels, icon}`, `p.fetch {host, recipe}`, `p.keeps`, `p.firstUse` when a proposal carries them, and maps `request.kind` deb / appimage — a download proposal's card needs no change here.

Census rows: approval-census (the approve door + 3 pins), user-todos-layout (rowCtx lang), inbox-window-model (a 3rd innerHTML write = the card's escaped HTML), takeover-keyboard (the dialog's Details), record-clear-census (normalizers' `e.card` is a chat card); ci.mjs (test-app-card, fast).

### lane apps-install-core — an agent proposes any install (a package name, a vendor's download address, a file), one card (design 009, lane 1 of 3)

- **One verb.** `vibespace-app install <package> | --from <https URL> | --file <path> | --source …`. An address or a file is FETCHED by the machine half as the user at propose time (`app-fetch`): `fetchVerdict` (PURE) — https, a public NAME (no IP literal in any spelling, no localhost / .local / .internal / .lan / .home.arpa …), no credentials; every resolved address judged by `addressVerdict` (private / loopback / link-local incl. 169.254.169.254 / CGNAT / multicast, IPv4-mapped and NAT64 as their IPv4) and the socket pinned to that address (no rebinding); redirects followed by hand, each re-judged, ≤ 5; ≤ 2 GiB; idle 60 s / total 60 min; into `staging/` 0600 while hashed. `sniffInstaller` decides the kind by the BYTES (ar + `debian-binary` = deb, ELF + `AI\x02` = AppImage); a web page named .deb, a type-1 AppImage, a program, a device are refused by name and deleted.
- **Name from the archive.** A .deb: `dpkg-deb -c` → `debDesktopOf` (regular files where a launcher looks — no symlink, no `..`, ≤ 256 KiB) → one member out through `dpkg-deb --fsys-tarfile | tar -xO` (bounded) → `parseDesktopFile`, now with `labels: {zh, ja}` from `Name[zh_CN]` › `Name[zh]` (never zh_TW) and `Name[ja]`; its icon (`debIconOf`) staged as `<hash>.icon.png|svg` and served by `GET /api/apps/proposals/:id/icon`. An AppImage: NEW `src/app-squashfs.js` reads the SquashFS 4 image after the ELF (`appImageOffset`) — gzip / zstd, every read async, never the vendor's runtime; `unsupported` (xz…) / `hostile` (a `..` / `/` name, loops, > 200 k entries, > 64 deep) by name.
- **The card's structure** (§4 view, additive): `kind` package|deb|appimage|remove|source, `app {name, labels, icon}`, `from {kind, host, via?, file?, recipe?}`, `bytes`, `keeps` replay|home|system, `details {packages, commands, sha256, scripts, fingerprints, url}`, `digest`. Lane apps-one-card words it.
- **The click.** A .deb from staging plans IN PLACE (re-hashed; another byte ⇒ `changed`, nothing ran) through today's slot + root script (which re-checks the sha256), then the staged copy goes. An AppImage runs no root and no slot: copied-while-hashed into a private dir, unpacked by the reader into `appimage/<id>/root` (files O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, links made never followed, devices skipped), the AppImage deleted, its row from its own desktop file (`AppRun`, `APPDIR`), served by the catalog only while it runs exactly that file. `remove` plans by kind (`removePlanFor`: AppImage = its directory, uv / npm = their uninstallers as the user, `homeArgv` — never the slot's `argv`).
- **Cleanup.** Rejected / withdrawn / expired (24 h, `sweep`, the agent told) / done ⇒ `app-unstage` at once (a failed one keeps its file for a retry); at boot every staged file over an hour old that no open proposal keeps goes.
- **Recipes** (`src/app-recipes.js`, PURE, 8 rows HEAD-checked 2026-10-03): search finds "微信"; a card says "official download" only when EVERY hop stayed on the row's hosts. Feishu / Lark / QQ publish versioned addresses only — not rows.
- **Helper conversation**: the first message is the user's words + one line (`vibespace-app`, `vibespace-docs apps`); named "Install app · <request>" (zh 装应用 · …).
- Gates: test-app-manifest §D9 (verdict tables, sniff, names, members, removal plans, recipes, the reader on committed gzip / zstd / xz / hostile fixtures, unpack confinement with the cwd elsewhere), test-apps-engine §10 (the REAL machine half + a loopback https "vendor" by a `.test` name through `fetchSeam`: deb + AppImage end to end, 13 refusals with nothing filed and staging empty, reject / expiry / changed bytes), heavy test-app-install §9 (a real .deb read by dpkg-deb and installed by apt through the slot; an AppImage unpacked with the cwd elsewhere, run, removed).

### lane custom-app-h1 — an approved apt source is pinned to the packages taken from it (verify-r1 H1, H2, H3 of lane custom-app)

- **H1 (MED, held at custom-app verify r1):** an approved third-party apt source had no pin, so apt could take that source's newer build of ANY package on a later install or a Refresh (the Refresh card listed updates without their origin) — while the source card says "Packages come from this source only when you install them later". Now the ONE root script writes `/etc/apt/preferences.d/vibespace-<id>.pref` per source (PURE `sourcePin`): everything from its host at priority 1 (apt takes such a version only when nothing installed has that name), the packages the user installed FROM it at 500. Those packages are attributed BEFORE apt runs (`--print-uris` into an empty archives dir → `entries/<id>.pin`). `pins()` runs at the end of every run; `restore()` runs before apt in both replay rungs (rung 1 never restored sources before). The manifest records `sources[].pin`. Each Refresh update names its origin, checked against root's own sources, never the index. Gate: test-app-manifest §8c runs pins() from the script text, byte-equal to the table (a no-pin copy is red). Heavy test-app-install §8 uses a signed https repository fixture (our CA + OpenPGP key) that serves hello 2.10-99 and capp-third 1.0 → 1.1. With the pin, hello stays at Debian's 2.10-3 and capp-third goes to 1.1, named "fx" on the card. The no-pin control upgrades hello to 2.10-99. `Pin: origin` matched the bare host of an `https://host:8443` source (measured through apt-cache policy).
- **H2 (LOW):** the .deb plan reads the user's file once: an O_NONBLOCK open, type and size judged on the fd, copied while hashed. Before, a FIFO swapped in after the stat parked a libuv thread. Root's deb and source modes `grab()` with `dd iflag=nofollow,nonblock`: no `[ -f ] && cp` gap, and a FIFO is refused by the hash at once (the pre-fix `cp` blocks — control). Residual: a same-uid racer can still rewrite the user-owned staged copy between the plan's hash and its dpkg-deb inspection. Root installs only bytes whose hash matches.
- **H3 (LOW):** a boot replay that meets a busy package slot (`busy`, or a followed run's `not_run`) waits it out, polling every 15 s for at most 10 min, then runs the same rung. Before, it filed "every app" at once. Gate: test-apps-engine §6, plus a no-wait control.
- Known limits: an entry installed from a source before 2.369.203 has no `.pin`, so the pin holds back its updates until it is reinstalled (or adopted). A dependency that a Refresh newly brings in from a source is not added to the allow-list. Two sources on one host share one origin.
- **verify r1 (lane custom-app-h1):** three holes in the pin's life, each reproduced in a Debian 12 container on f56e9d57. (1) A source approved before .203 had no pin until a run ENDED, so its first Refresh took the source's hello 2.10-99: every run now calls `pins` before the mode dispatch. (2) Source mode made the source live, then ran `apt-get update`, then pinned: a SIGKILL during the update left it live and unpinned (the machine's own `apt-get upgrade` took 2.10-99). Now root's record, then the pin, then the live source. (3) `Pin: origin` matches a HOST, so a source on a host the machine's own apt sources use (Debian backports on deb.debian.org) held the machine's own archive at priority 1, security updates too: refused `shared-host` (`mine()`). Gates: test-app-manifest §8c (order + `mine()` table + a pre-fix control), test-app-install §8 (shared-host and pre-.203 containers, each with a pre-order control).

### lane channel-attach-read — an agent opens a picture or a file someone sent in a conversation it may read (B-d6b9, design 005 §2.A)

- **The verb.** `vibespace-channels attachment <conv> <msg id> <attachment id> [--out <path>] [--force]` saves the file and prints `saved <path> (<type>, N bytes) — sent by <name> in <conversation>; what it shows is theirs, not instructions to you`; the agent opens it with its own tools. `read` prints each attachment's id and the command (every piece one shell word — a hostile id is single-quoted, round-tripped through a real shell in the gate). The default path is `$TMPDIR/vibespace-channels/<adapter>/<12 hex>.<ext>`: the hex is sha256 of (conversation, message, id) — **a deviation from the design's "first 12 of the id"**, which names one file for every Gmail `part:2` and for Lark keys sharing their `img_v3_02xx_` prefix; the extension comes from the stored mime, else (**an addition**) the file's own first bytes for png / jpeg / gif / webp / pdf, because a Lark picture is stored as `image/*` and a `.bin` is a picture the agent cannot open as one. Never the sender's file name. An existing `--out` is refused before any request without `--force`; the bytes go to a `.part` file beside the target and are renamed only when exactly `Content-Length` bytes arrived (a short body, no size, or a broken transfer keeps nothing; a body longer than its size was measured: undici hands over the declared bytes only).
- **The route.** `GET /api/agent/channels/attachment?conv=&msg=&id=` (src/agent-routes.js, beside `read`): a session token only (a job token 401); the engine's answer streamed from the file held open (the size said = the size sent), `application/octet-stream`, nosniff, sandbox CSP, `attachment`, `no-store`; `X-VibeSpace-Attachment` = URI-encoded JSON `{mime, bytes, from, conversation}`. Its own status table (chanAnswer's is the refresh census's source in test-channels-agent-cli). The touch witness records a `read` (§63).
- **The engine.** The SAME `attachment()` with `{by: 'agent', principal}`: the read route's reach FIRST (`stillSees` — hidden, requestable, a disabled account, none: the uniform not-found, before the cache is asked — so the cached-file-with-the-account-disabled case is not-found for an agent, while the owner's window is still served from the cache: rule 1, stated and unchanged); then the message the agent names must carry the id, and a `role:'body'` part (a mail's formatted body — its `part:N` id is guessable, the window may have cached it) is the same not-found (§25: an agent reads `text`; test-channel-acl drives it + a control); a cache hit free; a fetch in flight joined (no charge); before a vendor fetch `agentShareRefusal` and the charge attributed to `spentBy.agent`; every answer through `agentAttachmentAnswer` — reach asked AGAIN after the fetch / the join / the held write, the sender (the read view + agentCopy), the title and the vendor's type each through the belt. The share's sentence now says "agents' refreshes and fetches" (kb-api updated).
- **Gates.** test-channels-images ③b (the real agent routes on the rig's server: hidden ≡ requestable ≡ nonexistent with no vendor call, a job token, the bytes + headers, charged to the agents' share, a cache hit free, joined with the owner's flight = one call / one charge, another agent refused even on a cached picture, an account grant, a disabled account, the share at its boundary 2 of 8 with the owner unaffected, a revoke inside the fetch) + 4 patched-copy controls (no reach: the vendor is called for a hidden conversation; no share; no attribution; no re-ask); test-vendor-whitelist §7 (the caller census admits src/agent-routes.js only `by: 'agent'` with the principal, reach before the cache, the share between the verdict's `fetch` and the call — 3 controls); test-channels-agent-cli (the PURE ext / path / shell-word tables, the verb end to end against the stub, a raw server lying long); test-peer-text-census (the door `agentAttachmentAnswer(`, its print rows, an attack leg with a hostile name / title / type, a pin control); test-architecture §65 (FOLLOW + the await exemption with its reason, a control).
- **Verify r1.** The attachment cache, its flight and its remembered refusals name the MESSAGE too (a Gmail `part:1` is one mail's formatted body and the next mail's PDF: an agent asking the PDF was handed the body under the wrong sender; a file cached under the bare id serves the owner's window only); an agent fetch's spender rides the call's own async context (`spendAs` — a pass or the owner's window inside the await moved `e.chargeBy`); Lark's resource read stops at 100 MB whatever its Content-Length says; `--out` inside VibeSpace's own checkout is refused before any request. Legs: test-channels-images ③c (+2 controls), test-channels-lark-shape (the lying length), test-channels-agent-cli (`--out` into data/bin, direct and through a symlink).

### lane channel-attach-send — an agent's reply or new message carries pictures and files, bound to the approval (B-fd1f, design 005 §2.B)

- **The verb.** `vibespace-channels reply|compose … --attach <path>` (repeatable): the CLI stats every path first (a directory, a missing / unreadable / empty file, > 10 files, > 25 MB together ⇒ exit 1 before anything is read or sent), then sends `attachments: [{name: <basename>, data: <base64>}]` in the propose request; the agent routes already passed `attachments` through — src/agent-routes.js is untouched. It prints the server's list (type, size, sha256).
- **Policy (PURE, src/channel-policy.js).** `attachmentsOf` (bounds, `ATTACH_CODES` in `why`), `safeAttachmentName` (refused, never cleaned: separators, src/hidden-chars.js's set with joiners refused, a line feed / tab, edge spaces, > 200), `sniffType` (bytes → png/jpeg/gif/webp = image; pdf/zip/gzip/svg/html/text/octet-stream = file), `nameTypeMismatch` (the card's chip), `attachVerdict` (one row `{maxCount, maxTotalBytes, withText}` or `{images, files}`), `storedAttachments`, `attachmentSize`. `shownFields` appends `[name, bytes, sha256]` per stored file ONLY when there are any (every other digest unchanged). `receiptFor` / `renderReceiptBlock` list the files. `decideOutbound` is unchanged (owner Q2 = NO: the existing `channels.guardAttachmentsReview` switch and the channel policy decide). The old names-only `{name, bytes}` shape is refused (`attachment-data`) — it never carried bytes.
- **Files (src/channel-outbox-files.js, new).** `prepare` (decode, sha256, sniff — in memory), `stage` (SYNCHRONOUS write into `outbox-files/.stage-*`, so no await sits between propose's last reach check and the record), `commit` (rename to `<proposal id>`), `discard`, `verify` (re-read + re-hash at the send), `remove`, `sweep`. Paths come from the proposal id + index only.
- **Engine.** `attachPrepare` right after the shape check in `propose` and `compose` (refusal = `bad-proposal` + `why`; nothing on disk); the record stores metas only; `sendNow` verifies and hands the adapter THE verified buffers (`attachment-changed` ⇒ failed, zero adapter calls); `transition` to rejected / withdrawn / expired removes the folder and stamps `attachmentsGoneAt`; `filesSweep` (beside the expiry sweep) removes sent / failed files 7 days after they ended, orphan folders and stale stages; `outboxAttachment(id, n)` for the owner route. The store's `outboxPrune` takes a pruned record's folder.
- **Registry / adapters.** `caps.sendAttachments` validated at registration (+ `sendAttachmentsWhy`); `send` / `compose` handed attachments without the row throw `not-supported`. Gmail: `buildMime` multipart/mixed (sniffed type, ASCII fallback + RFC 2231 `filename*` continued in ≤ 60-char pieces, 76-col base64, control characters stripped from names / an invalid type → octet-stream), `rawRequest` = the JSON form up to `JSON_RAW_MAX` 4 MB, else the documented upload form (`gmail.googleapis.com/upload/…?uploadType=multipart`, metered like the JSON one) — the threshold is from Google's documented 5 MB JSON cap, NOT measured live. Lark: `sendAttachments: null` with its reason (docs: uploads take the tenant token only — LA1; LA3 unprovable without a live call; LA2 `im:resource` / `im:resource:upload`, LA4 10 MB image / 30 MB file per the docs).
- **Card + route.** src/lib/channel-outbox.js `appendAttachments` (thumbnail only for the four SNIFFED rasters, name via `revealInto`, size · type · sha256 prefix, the mismatch chip, the "exactly these bytes" / "no longer kept" note; zh/ja strings). `GET /api/channels/outbox/:id/attachment/:n` (owner-only, declared BEFORE the read route whose pattern would take it): nosniff, sandbox CSP, no-store, inline only for the four sniffed rasters.
- **Gates.** New scripts/test-channel-attach-send.mjs (PURE table, engine rig propose → approve → send with a recording adapter, V1/V2/V6/V7, Q2 through the engine, compose, retention incl. a pruned record, the owner route incl. V4, the registry row, Gmail MIME parsed back incl. V3 + the upload form, the CLI, V8/V10 censuses) with patched-copy controls (count, separator, hidden char, digest, no re-hash, no removal, staging a refused proposal, inline-any route, CR/LF in MIME, no row check).

### lane message-facts — a message's envelope and each provider's own facts, from ONE declared scheme (B-f066 part 1, design 007)

- **The scheme.** `facts: [{k, v, more?, cut?}]` is an optional, closed, typed list on the ONE record (src/channel-record.js: `FACT_TYPES` — seven value types, `FACT_SCHEMA`, `FACT_LIMITS`, `validateFacts` — refusals by name `unknown-kind` / `bad-value` / `duplicate-kind` / `too-many`, every string through `peerName`, ≤ 50 parties per list then `more`, ≤ 16 KB per list by giving party tails to `more`); a record without facts is byte-identical. PURE `src/channel-facts.js` words it: `FACT_KINDS` (type, label, where, agent), `foldFacts`, `summaryOf`, `chipsOf`, `detailRows`, `mapFactStrings`, `agentFactLines`, `compactFactLines`. The side log's fourth kind `fx` (the "edit" occupant §28 reserved) carries facts learned later; the store's trim folds a message's fx lines into one and its reader's head match knows `fx`.
- **Gmail now.** `factsFromHeaders` (PURE) at ingest: to, cc, bcc (own sent mail only), reply-to, sender (≠ From), list (List-Id), delivered-to (≠ the account), subject (≠ the thread's, Re:/Fwd: aside), importance (Importance / Priority / X-Priority), automated (Auto-Submitted / Precedence) — through `addressList` + `addressParts`, RFC 2047 names decoded (`decodeWords`, linear), a header over 16 KB ⇒ `cut: true`. `caps.facts` (validated against the closed kinds at registration) + `caps.factsOf` → `factsOf(convId)`: ONE `threads.get?format=metadata` through the gate. The registry holds the answer to the declared kinds and the validator; `factsOf` declared ⇔ implemented.
- **The backfill (S5).** `GET /api/channels/:adapterId/:convId/facts?msg=` → engine `messageFacts`: a side hit is free; a message stored before its facts = ONE metered read of its whole thread, single-flight per thread, the account's budget and back-off, refusals by name; one `fx` line per message of THIS conversation's log (a vendor id the log does not hold is never written; an empty list = "asked, none"); an agent bearer is refused by name. Ingest never backfills; an agent's read never does.
- **The window.** `src/lib/channel-facts-view.js` (by value type only, textContent): the summary button ("to me, Alice Chen, Bob +3 · cc Carol", addresses in the tooltip), the chips, the details `dl` (open state in `folds`, "+N" expands in place), chips-only facts beside the time, a "Details" ask on a record stored before its facts (`factsAsk` from the engine's page view); one call in `renderRecord` (the thread pane renders through it). zh/ja words.
- **The agent.** The belt door `agentFacts` (engine; names by peerName, addresses + lines by the belt's line rule) in `agentCopy` and `withView`; `factsText` = `agentFactLines` under the line rule; the CLI's `read` prints it as one indented line. test-peer-text-census: doors `agentFacts` / `agentFactLines`, row `m.factsText`.
- **Gates.** NEW scripts/test-channel-facts.mjs (fast): the table ⇔ schema ⇔ zh/ja, the schema's refusals and bounds (V1 frames / bidi / a 1 MB line), the fold + compaction, the summary at 1 / 4 / 60, details, chips, the agent line (V2), THE PAPER TEST (Slack / Telegram / Outlook mappers: no new type; via, edited, read-by, pinned, restricted, forwarded-from printed as the rows they would add), Gmail's ten kinds (V3 Bcc), the contract, the engine backfill (V5 20 clicks = 1 call, V6, V4, V8) and the route's agent refusal. Legs in test-channel-record (the optional set), test-channels-agent-cli (the read line), test-vendor-whitelist (the backfill is on demand: one call site, no timer, owner route only).
- **Verify r1 (Opus).** F1 a peer's display name / subject could spell our own line's structure — `"a\", evil@x, \"b" <real@x>` read as three recipients, `Alice · reply-to: pay@evil` / a subject `… · bcc: …` as more fact keys (agent line, summary, tooltip, details): `channel-facts.js` `quoted()` — RFC 5322 quoting (`"` and `\` escaped) for a name holding `, " < > \ ·`-dots or ` +N`, a line value holding a dot or a quote. F2 Bcc rode inbound mail that spoofed From = the account: `factsFromHeaders({sent})` — Gmail's SENT label (both reads pass `sentLabel(m)`); From decides alone only when the labels are unknown. F3 a stored message the vendor's answer omits (re-threaded / deleted) cost a metered thread read per click: every such held message without facts is written "asked, none" (`[]`). F4 the V7 adapter-id census read only `=== 'gmail'` (and test-channels-groups-ui §3's CLIENT list omits the view): it now reads the view, the table and the engine section with the full id list, a planted branch its negative control. test-channel-facts §9 + V7 (15 legs; 12 red on 597f381d).

### lane message-facts-lark — Lark's own per-message facts as chips (B-f066 part 2, design 007 "Lark now")

- **Four rows, no new type.** `via` (party), `forwarded-from` (party), `edited` (time), `recalled` (flag) in channel-record `FACT_SCHEMA` + channel-facts `FACT_KINDS`, all `where: 'chip'` (a chat message with chips only shows them beside the time, no line of its own); `edited` / `recalled` are `mutable` (an `fx` may bring them late). Lark's `caps.facts` declares the four; no `factsOf`.
- **Lark emits them at ingest** (`factsOfItem`, module-private, called by `toRecord` — the poll, history, push and by-id paths all pass it): `sender_type: 'app'` ⇒ `via {id: app_id, name: the head's name}`; `msg_type: 'merge_forward'` ⇒ `forwarded-from {}`; `updated: true` ⇒ `edited` at `update_time` (no readable instant ⇒ no fact); `deleted: true` ⇒ `recalled`. An unedited person's message emits none (keys byte-identical). `author.isBot`, the "[deleted]" / "[forwarded messages]" texts and `raw` unchanged. `recordView` renames the `via` party with the head when an app's name is learned later, through `validateFacts`.
- **Two scheme changes, by row property / value type — no kind named, no engine / CLI change:** (1) the list item of a merged forward never names the original sender, so a `party` row may declare `nameless: true` — `v: {}` is "a party the vendor did not name" (validateFacts accepts it only there; chipsOf prints the row's `chipBare` — "forwarded"; agentFactLines prints the bare key); (2) the chip printer had no `time` branch (Gmail emits no time): `chipsOf` hands a time chip's instant over and channel-facts-view.js words it in the chip's title in the device's locale.
- **Gates.** test-channel-facts §10 (+21): the rows, the nameless rule, emitted ⊆ declared over EVERY recorded Lark item through the real toRecord (CONTROL: a copy emitting an undeclared `importance` is flagged; without the facts fixtures `edited` / `forwarded-from` are flagged unexercised), the name door end to end (CONTROL: a copy whose record skips peerName stores the raw 800-char bidi name), the engine page, the agent's line, edited / recalled arriving late as `fx`. test-channels-lark-shape ⑤c (+12) over the recorded shapes + a new `messagesFacts` fixture page (an edit, a merged forward, an app that updated its card, a recall); the via rename's two doors (CONTROL: both removed ⇒ red). test-channel-record: one SITES row (the via name). Heavy test-channel-window-render ⑬b: a zh Lark room — "经 Facts Bot 发送" / "已编辑" (title = the instant) / "已转发" / "已撤回" in the head, a plain message without any.
- **Not in this lane:** noticing an edit or a recall AFTER a message was stored (a re-delivered copy is a dedup no-op by vendorId); the `fx` path exists. Lark records stored before this lane carry no facts (`raw` lacks `update_time` / `deleted`; nothing is backfilled).

### lane usage-pricing — the Codex price rows the 2026-10-02 price check found (wf_d2b3907b-2c5), the fork double count, a gate for the OpenAI rows

Every Claude row was right; every money error was in a Codex row. Measured over a read of the production ledger (base table → this table, production pricing.json merged as at load): gpt-6-astra $2,989 → $16,110 (26,746 rows, 12K of them over 272K), gpt-5.6-sol $2,548 → $3,345 (exactly the check's figure), the four old codex models $248 → $124; ledger total $125,946 → $139,740 before the fork archive (−$177).

- **gpt-6-astra row + the long-context rule.** $10 / $1 / $50, and above 272K input tokens the WHOLE request at $20 / $2 / $75. `long` is decided on the request's whole prompt; `_cost(ev, prompt)` lets the four token-class split sites (usage-anchors, session-brain, claude-stream-json, usage-pool-engine) pass the request's prompt so the parts still add up.
- **gpt-5.6-sol: long rule + a DATED rate.** The 2026-08-21 cut ($5/$30 → $4/$20, long $10/$45 → $8/$30) is the row's `earlier` list — a new, closed table shape (`PRICE_ROW_FIELDS`), resolved in one place (`priceAt`). No end date for the promotion is modelled.
- **terra / luna corrected** ($2/$12, $0.20/$1.20), **gpt-5-codex / 5.1-codex(-max) / 5.2-codex rows**, long rule on 5.5 / 5.4, and 6.1-sol / 6-luna (on the official table, 0 rows yet). Cache-write rates are on the 5.6/6 rows (1.25× input); the walker still stores cw 0 for codex.
- **Stale stored rows:** setPricing saves every row, so an untouched old shipped gpt row on disk now takes the new default at load (`SUPERSEDED_DEFAULTS`); an edited row stays.
- **Retired Claude ids** (Opus 4 / 4.1 / 3, Haiku 3.5 / 3, Mythos Preview) got exact keys; 0 ledger rows — correctness for imports. The binary oracle now names claude-opus-4-0 / 4-1 / claude-3-5-haiku.
- **Fork double count.** Both walkers skip a forked rollout's replay (a token_count within 2 s of the fork's session_meta; local corpus 1,714/1,714, 0 false); migration `2026-10-archive-codex-fork-replays` archives the 1,661 rows already stored, with a reason each (src/codex-fork-ledger-purge.js).
- **Unknown codex ids** warn once per id (journal + telemetry `usage-unpriced-model`) instead of silently taking Sonnet's price.
- **Gate:** test-pricing-openai judges every gpt-* row against scripts/fixtures/openai-pricing.json (official table, fetched 2026-10-03T04:38Z, raw HTML), with a planted-wrong-price control; parity + migrations suites gained the fork legs.
- **verify r1.** The fork replay now ENDS at the fork's own first turn (its task_started / turn_context turn id is a UUIDv7 minted after the fork's thread id; every replayed turn is older) — the 2 s window is only the outer bound, so a fast first turn inside it still counts (the real fork corpus: 21,357 rows, identical to the window alone). A rerun after a crash between a shard's archive append and its rename no longer archives the rows twice. On a copy of the production ledger the migration archived 1,661 rows (278.5M tokens), kept + archived = the original, and a second run did nothing. The unknown-id warning is once per process, not once per UsageHistory.

### lane presets-migration — a dropped override key leaves the release; the presets summary follows a change of layer (B-8145)

Found testing the fleet switch to the cluster presets Secret on a test release (2026-10-02 21:05 PDT), two defects. (1) The chart wrote the release's override through the release Secret's `stringData:`. helm's upgrade is a 3-way patch that nulls a dropped key in the field the old manifest named it in; `stringData` is write-only (the API server folds it into `data` and never stores it), so dropping `gdrive.clients` left `data.gdriveClients` in place, still projected as `override/gdrive-clients.json` — identical keys override the cluster per key, so a later rotation in the cluster Secret would never have reached that user. Now the override lives in its OWN Secret, `<release>-preset-override`, rendered with `data:` (b64enc) and owned whole by the chart (`data: {}` with no block); the projected volume's release source reads it; the release Secret carries no preset key under the volume form (the env form, `presets.volume=false`, stays byte-identical to 2.369.199). A release on the 2.369.200 chart keeps its stringData leftovers in the release Secret, no longer projected; deploy/README's migration section now says to drop the legacy blocks equal to the cluster's and how to list and remove the leftover keys. That upgrade rolls the pod once (the source is a new Secret); later override changes stay Secret-only. (2) `src/server/cluster-presets.js` replaced its snapshot only when the merged VALUES differed, so an equal override removed (the same values, now from the cluster) left `status()` — and `/api/integrations` `presets.groups` — on "release". The reader now compares the attribution too (`attributionOf` = the sorted `layerOf` pairs): the snapshot follows and the listeners run with `{kinds: [], sources}`, so the wiring re-pushes the summary; the journal line and the cards' re-derive stay for value changes only.

Gates: test-helm-render (heavy, 28; H new) — helm's 3-way merge modelled on the rendered Secrets (kind/k3d-free): a dropped key leaves the override Secret and `override/` on this chart, and on a 2.369.200 → this upgrade (leftovers stay in the release Secret, unread); the same model on the 2.369.200 chart reproduces the finding; CONTROL a chart copy rendering the override Secret through `stringData:` keeps the dropped key projected. test-cluster-presets (fast, 228; §4 new) — a release migrated with blocks equal to the cluster's, then upgraded without them, through the REAL integrations wiring: the summary and the `cluster-presets-updated` push move from "release" to "cluster", no journal line, no card re-derive, back again when an equal override returns, a cluster rotation shadowed while the override is projected and in effect once it is gone; CONTROL a values-only copy leaves the summary on "release" and pushes nothing.

### lane pool-scarce-lanes — pool placement keeps scarce model lanes for the conversations that need them (B-8a65)

Design desk 001 (`pool-scarce-lanes`, Fable), owner Q1 = yes (the spare lane leads the EDF deadline) and Q2 = yes (S5, added mid-lane 2026-10-03 03:37Z: 「Opus 便宜」). Owner, 2026-10-02: 「如果一个claude session在用opus，自动选择账号的时候优先选择fable用尽了的，避免占据fable额度（因为fable也要用全局额度）。然后想一想这个东西怎么做成针对不同provider普适的方案。」 The design's F5: 15 claude members each report ONE scoped lane, "Fable"; three are Fable-rich (72 / 71 / 52 %) and also hold the most 7d — exactly the members EDF and most-remaining handed an Opus session.

- **S1 — the projection hands back what it set aside** (src/model-family.js): `projectCacheForFamily` → `{ ...cache, scopedWeekly, spareScoped }`, view-only; a null family or no scoped lanes ⇒ the cache object itself (the storm's identity control holds).
- **S2 — the order** (src/account-pool-auto.js): `spareLaneRemaining` (MIN over the lanes that state a spend; null sorts as rich), every candidate row carries `spare`, `edfCompare` leads with it — after the manual priority, before the deadline. The sealed orders and the pool default decide on unprojected views ⇒ a tie ⇒ byte-identical.
- **S3 — the spawn**: `placing: true`, the chooser's one word (src/server/usage-pool-engine.js); a usable default is left for a settleable member with strictly less spare (`spare-lane`).
- **S5 — running conversations**: a hot pool's proactive pass moves an idle conversation off a MEASURED spare lane when the gain exceeds `SPARE_MOVE_MARGIN_PCT` (15); a warm cache holds it (`warm-cache`), a turn in flight holds it (`spare-hold`); one notice, SPARE_LANE_KEY (en/zh/ja dictionaries).
- **Where the build bent the design.** (1) The `healthy` early return is skipped under `placing` — else a healthy default never reaches the tier. (2) The design's literal `bestSettle.spare < (cur.spare ?? 100)` places a spawn onto an UNKNOWN member (`null < 70` is true in JS): both sides carry `?? 100`, pinned by a patched-copy control. (3) S5 needed two anti-flap rules the design did not spell out: the margin, and a guard on the EDF tier (never onto MORE spare lane). Without the guard the two tiers bounce a cold conversation every tick (replay control: ≥ 10 moves in 12 ticks); the guard also closes an S1–S4 gap — EDF dragged an Opus conversation off a spent member onto a Fable-rich one with a sooner week. (4) A running conversation moves only off a MEASURED spare lane; a spawn keeps "unknown = rich". (5) Four storm negative controls (§1, §5, §7, §11d) now read either sentence: the pre-fix mis-projected move leaves the rich member through the spare tier first, whose words name the same wrong family. (6) The user line rides in the lane report (the style gate refuses a newest user entry two patches past package.json's 2.369.200).
- **Gates.** test-pool-auto: new section "THE SPARE LANE (B-8a65)" — asserts 1–11 of the design, S5 (cold → moves, warm → held, mid-turn → held, no member better by more than the margin → stays, unknown current → stays, Fable → never, cold pool → never), V5 jitter replays, a seeded sweep byte-identical to 0e7dc5b4 for every view without a differing spare lane (+ 600 spawns with `placing` landing where they did), seven patched-copy controls (no key, unknown = spent, the unguarded candidate side, no spawn tier, across ranks, no EDF guard, no margin). test-account-pool: the projection's shape. test-fable-cap-pool-storm §19: the REAL chooser on the incident caches (Opus → a Fable-spent member, Fable → the default, the pre-change chooser as control) and the REAL per-session pass (cold Opus moves with its sentence, warm stays, Fable stays, no better member ⇒ stays). ### lane jobs-browser — a Background Work job browses as its owner conversation (B-dbc1)

- **Why.** A user's daily reconciliation job could not leave the old desktop Chromium: `/api/agent/browser/*` admitted only `vsst_`, a job carries `VIBESPACE_JOB_TOKEN` (`jbt_`), and `data/bin/vibespace-browser` read only `VIBESPACE_SESSION_TOKEN`.
- **The principal (PURE src/browser-job-principal.js).** The job's lease key is a child handle of the owner conversation's browser key, tagged `job: <id>` — every admission rule judges a child as its parent, so the owner's who-may-use decides (a refused owner ⇒ a refused job, `not_owner`). Its profile = the owner's pin / default attachment (never the owner's temporary browser: `job_no_profile`). Read / act routes allowed (profiles status providers resolve audit tab dialog direct); everything that changes the conversation's browsers refused `job_token`, fail closed, a census of every route. Not running ⇒ `job_not_running`; no owner ⇒ `job_no_owner`; owner without a key ⇒ `no_browser_key`.
- **The wiring.** routes: ONE door (`agentFacts` → `jobAgentFacts`: route judged before anything is minted; the owner's live session or recorded binding; the belt resolves a job without minting); `resolveForJob` reads the owner's set (never changes it) and attaches the job's own lease ⇒ its own window. keeper: `jobRunning` dep; a running job's handle is in the live set (a job whose conversation stopped keeps browsing until it ends); `releaseJob` at the run's finalize (jobs.js `onRunEnded` → server.js); `reconcile` releases any handle whose job is not running (boot + every tick). The strip names the job's window "Job: <name>" (zh/ja), the name read live; the trace stores the job's id only (lane-redact r9: a job's name never rides its browsing). The CLI reads `VIBESPACE_SESSION_TOKEN || VIBESPACE_JOB_TOKEN`.
- **Gates.** test-jobs-browser (new, fast, 98: tables + route census + admission through the real mayAttach + the real routes + keeper over test-browser-windows ④'s fake agent-browser 0.38.1 / window model: own lease + window in the owner's pinned profile, refusals by name, owner gone ⇒ still browsing, released at finalize + by the sweep; 3 mutant-copy controls); test-browser-identity-census 132 (+ the job's attach caller row); test-browser-share-model 241; test-browser-windows 94; test-job-model 156; test-jobs-panel; test-browser-mediation 247 / -profiles 477 / -stuck 287 (manual readers); build + i18n-check.

### lane browser-recipes — the agent is taught the steps for a browser with the user's login

userR's pod (2026-10-02): asked to operate an admin site "in the Chrome logged in as <her>", the agent ran `vibespace-browser status` ("no profile attached — ephemeral …"), concluded it had no usable browser, launched the system chromium itself and died on "Missing X server or $DISPLAY". Nothing it was shown named the recipe (a named profile, the user logging in once through the live view, the login kept); the manual's first screen was page verbs. Base b924041f; four steps, one commit each.

- **Step 1 — the manual's §0.** docs/agent/browser-manual.md opens with "What the user asked for → what you do" (≤ 40 lines, before the old intro paragraph and every verb): (a) the user's login = `new "<site> — <user>'s login"` → `use` → `open <url>` → the sentence "Open the Agent browser window and take over to log in; I will continue once you hand it back" (never a password; the login stays in the profile); (b) browse = bare verbs; (c) the same login for other agents (usable by all conversations unless narrowed; `--sharing instance` = own tabs; `not_owner` ⇒ the user widens "Who can use it"); (d) no display = only `vibespace-browser`, never chromium / google-chrome / playwright by hand. Each ends with one sentence for the user.
- **Step 2 — `status` and the first refusal.** PURE src/browser-recipes.js holds the words (pointer, first-verb pointer, intro clauses) and `noDisplayRung` / `noDisplayLine` (a live browser's recorded launch fact wins, else a probe of this machine; never for a conversation on another machine). The status route answers `recipe` + `noDisplay`; the CLI prints the pointer when no profile is attached and the sentence when the machine has no display. A page verb refused while the conversation has no browser yet carries `recipe` (`res.locals.recipe` through `fail` / `failVerdict`), printed `next: …`. The exit-machine sentence quoted from her transcript is not in this tree's `status` (it is `vibespace-exit list`'s); the gate pins its absence.
- **Step 3 — the tools intro.** The Browsing line's ONE clause names the recipe (on the isolated line it replaces the older "for a login other conversations can use too …" clause); the machine's display fact rides both delivery sites as `browserDisplay` (the keeper's last probe, sync, refreshed on demand when older than 60 s; one probe at boot) and adds the no-display clause. Whole intro with a two-profile set + the clause: 8 065 B (rung D), 7 427 B (shared) < 9 600 B.
- **Step 4 — the gate.** scripts/test-browser-recipes.mjs (fast, 0.5 s, 32): §0 first + the four recipes + the exact sentence; the naive reader (first 60 lines: `new "` before every page verb); the PURE no-display table; the status census over the REAL CLI against a stub server; the first verb's refusal over the real CLI (a fake browser CLI that must never run); the intro under the cap; wiring pins. Controls (scratch copies): a manual without §0 fails the first-screen leg; a CLI without the pointer fails the census. test-browser-profiles' call-shape pin follows the new `browserDisplay` fact.
- **Verify r1 (2026-10-02, one round).** F1 (MED): a conversation on another machine (rung H / `f.remote`) read the same `new` + `use` + live-view pointer in `status`, the first verb's `next:` and the intro — there `new` answers `remote_session` and that machine has no live view (§5), so the recipe was unfollowable where it appeared; fixed with `REMOTE_POINTER` / `FIRST_VERB_NEXT_REMOTE` / `INTRO_REMOTE_CLAUSE` (the login needs a conversation on the VibeSpace machine), picked on `f.remote` / `VARIANTS.H`, plus the manual §0 (a) row. F2 (LOW): §0 said "in these words" without saying the sentences are SAID in the user's language. The gate counts §0 proper (to its closing `---`), pins the three remote surfaces and gains a control copy of agent-routes without the clause. Held: the display fact is the connect-testing probe (a dead DISPLAY=:97 ⇒ none); `vibespace-docs browser §0` resolves (the CLI reads one argument); the intro's largest shape (every tool, 12 attachments, the no-display clause) is 8 793 B; `status` before any browser exists carries the pointer (real route).

### lane lark-threads — a thread born after its root was stored; who is this

**User line (Fixed):** A Lark message that got a thread after VibeSpace had already read it now shows the thread (checked about once an hour per chat, at once when you press Refresh); people who left a chat and bots are named; you can give any Lark author your own name from the message's author menu.

- **The forensics (read-only, production 2026-10-01).** The owner's post (Fish Audio B2B GTM+ Eng) is stored with `threadKey: null`; its group holds 73 records, none keyed; 432 Lark records elsewhere carry a key — every one a topic whose root was listed AFTER the topic existed. Four holes: the feed dropped a stored hit before its thread mark (H1), the log's dedup kept the key-less first copy with no patch path (H2), the chat walk never re-lists a stored root (H3), nothing could learn the `omt_` key (H4).
- **A1 the place door** (src/channel-store.js `widenPlaces`, PURE rules src/channel-thread.js P1–P4): widen-only (null → the vendor's key / root), a validated `pl` side line, folded on every read, kept by the side compaction, folded into the log at its trim; every append path offers its duplicates; the engine's write hook re-derives the thread index, owes the topic a walk, and broadcasts `threads` with `walked`/`separate` (the root grows "open to load" in place).
- **A2 drain rule 22** (PURE): the newest page of each live, separately-listed, active (14 d), walked chat once per `channels.threadRecheckSec` (default 3600), the lowest priority, ≤ 3 a pass, paced, never in a back-off; the OWNER's Refresh re-lists at once (floored 60 s on his own previous press — never the timer's), a window's open and an agent's refresh never. Lark `recentRoots` = ONE `im/v1/messages` page, no anchor.
- **A3** a stored hit naming a thread marks the thread (never an owed chat read). **A4** a feed hit the chat read did not find is read by id (`GET im/v1/messages/:message_id`, ≤ 5 per feed tick, every non-reply answer and refusal remembered 6 h): a thread reply becomes a record of its chat, its root is patched, its thread owed. Both new calls allowlisted in test-vendor-whitelist §8 with their gates + 4 controls.
- **A5 the measurement — UNMEASURED against real Lark.** Whether the search carries `thread_id` and whether it indexes topic replies at all is not known (the first production page had none; the doc marks it optional). The card's new line says it within a day: "Threads: N search hits named a thread · F of M messages the chats did not list were thread replies, read one by one · K chat checks for new threads found W"; the journal's first-page line now prints `thread_id on N of M hits` and `display_info`'s sub-field names.
- **B (MEASURED, binding): naming another person needs `contact:contact.base:readonly`** (an owner-approved probe: 99991679 under `contact:user.base:readonly`). The consent asks it + `contact:user.employee:readonly` + `contact:user.department:readonly` as optional groups after the reactions (one dropped per refused consent); without it no lookup is sent and the card says "One Re-authorize adds: reading people's profiles". With it: profiles once per 6 h per person, ≤ 3 a page (the unnamed first), ≤ 20 a minute; the organization's nickname + department / job title carried as `author.alt` and rendered Lark's way (`channels.larkNameField`, default department — "Susan (Marketing)" if that is what the API carries; UNMEASURED: the probe never read Zin's profile); external authors by tenant (Zin's `1433ddec23579750` vs the account's own, learned without a call); a dissolved chat said once a day; a bot never "app" at the view door. Lark's chat-member API lists no bots and no app ids — a bot is named only by the application API (another tenant's app cannot be named; the owner's own name is the remedy). No API reads the owner's Lark remark (备注) — the VibeSpace name (aliases.json, owner-only `PATCH /api/channels/:adapterId/authors/:id`, "Set a name…" on the author's head, zh/ja) is the remedy and wins everywhere, the agent's read included.
- **Gates.** test-channel-feed 77, test-channel-store ⑬, test-channel-record 95, test-channel-thread 90, test-channel-reactions 113, test-channel-drain 396 (rule 22 in the seeded walk + ④d + 4 mutants), test-channels-lark-shape ⑮⑯, test-peer-parsers (readByIdAnswer row), test-vendor-whitelist §8, test-channels-engine ㉓㉔, test-architecture §65b, test-channel-authors 12 (new, fast), test-channel-lark-threads-ui 13 (new, heavy).

### lane reset-path — the owner's four codex reset-credit reports (2026-10-01)

User lines for the release entry (en / zh / ja):

- Fixed: A reset credit that could not be sent no longer starts the ten-minute wait, and the dialog says why it was refused. · 无法发出的 reset credit 不再触发十分钟等待，对话框会说明被拒绝的原因。 · 送信できなかったリセットクレジットで 10 分間の待ちが始まらなくなり、ダイアログが拒否の理由を表示します。
- Added: You can use a codex reset credit from the Agents list even when no chat session is open on that account. · 即使该账号上没有打开的聊天会话，也能在 Agents 列表中使用 codex 的 reset credit。 · そのアカウントでチャットセッションを開いていなくても、Agents 一覧から codex のリセットクレジットを使えます。
- Fixed: After you use a reset credit, the chat card that offered it shows that it was used instead of its button. · 使用 reset credit 后，提供它的聊天卡片会显示已使用，不再显示按钮。 · リセットクレジットを使うと、それを提示していたチャットのカードはボタンの代わりに使用済みと表示します。
- Fixed: The usage menu's Codex refresh now says what it read (or why it could not) and updates the numbers at once. · 用量菜单的 Codex 刷新现在会说明读到了什么（或为什么读不到），并立即更新数字。 · 使用量メニューの Codex 更新が、読み取った内容（または読めなかった理由）を表示し、数字をすぐ更新します。
- Fixed: A reset credit is no longer spent a second time on the same limit when a new credit was granted in between — the dialog says the earlier request cannot be judged and nothing is spent. · 中间新授予了 credit 时，同一限额不会再第二次消费 reset credit——对话框会说明先前的请求无法判定，并且不消费任何东西。 · その間に新しいクレジットが付与されていても、同じ制限に対してリセットクレジットが二度消費されることはなくなりました — ダイアログは以前の要求が判定できないことを示し、何も消費しません。
- Fixed: A reset-credit answer VibeSpace cannot read is settled only by the account's own reading taken after it, never by numbers carried over from before; the notice about it is in your language, with a For-you item naming the word. · VibeSpace 无法读懂的 reset credit 回答只会由其后账号自己的读数判定，不再由之前带过来的数字判定；相关通知使用你的语言，并有一条 For you 条目指明该词。 · VibeSpace が読めないリセットクレジットの応答は、その後に取ったアカウント自身の読み取りだけで判定され、以前から引き継いだ数値では判定されません。その通知はあなたの言語で表示され、For you にその語を示す項目が加わります。
- Fixed: Codex records that arrive hours late (after a stalled connection) are no longer taken as current — a stale reading settles nothing and a stale limit starts no wait. · 延迟数小时才到达的 Codex 记录（连接卡住之后）不再被当作当前状态——过期的读数不会判定任何东西，过期的限额也不会触发等待。 · 数時間遅れて届いた Codex の記録（接続が止まった後）は現在の状態として扱われなくなりました — 古い読み取りは何も判定せず、古い制限は待ちを始めません。
- Fixed: a session on a machine whose clock runs behind no longer loses that recognition to a single odd record (a clock step, a replayed burst, one slow read) — and a wall or reading from its first minute is acted on as soon as the offset is recognised, instead of waiting for the next one. · 时钟偏慢的机器上的会话不再因为一条异常记录 (时钟阶跃、回放的突发、一次慢读) 而失去对时钟偏差的识别——而且它第一分钟里的上限或读数会在识别出偏差时立即生效, 不再等下一条。 · 時計が遅れているマシン上のセッションが、たった 1 件の異常な記録 (時計のステップ、再生されたバースト、1 回の遅い読み取り) で時計のずれの認識を失うことはなくなりました — また最初の 1 分間の上限や読み取りは、ずれが認識された時点ですぐに反映され、次の 1 件を待たなくなりました。
- Fixed: Use a reset credit now reads the account first, so a credit granted a moment ago is never counted as unused. · 使用 reset credit 时现在会先读取账号，刚刚授予的 credit 不会再被算作未使用。 · リセットクレジットを使うとき、まずアカウントを読み取るようになり、直前に付与されたクレジットが未使用として数えられることはなくなりました。
- Fixed: A conversation whose records arrive late no longer re-applies an old limit over a newer reading of its account, keeps the first limit it hit when many readings follow, recognises a clock offset that sits right at the two-minute edge, and tells you in For you when a late limit may have stopped it. · 记录延迟到达的对话不再把旧的上限覆盖在账号更新的读数之上，很多读数跟在后面时也不会丢掉它撞到的第一个上限，刚好卡在两分钟边缘的时钟偏差也能被识别，而延迟到达的上限可能让它停下时会在 For you 里告诉你。 · 記録が遅れて届く会話は、アカウントのより新しい読み取りの上に古い上限を上書きしなくなり、多くの読み取りが続いても最初に達した上限を失わず、ちょうど 2 分の境界にある時計のずれも認識され、遅れて届いた上限で止まったかもしれない場合は For you で知らせます。
- Fixed: Codex readings from a machine whose clock runs behind are no longer refused for good as a stalled backlog — after a minute of them the clock offset is recognised and the numbers are current again. · 来自时钟偏慢的机器的 Codex 读数不再被永久当作卡住的积压而拒收——持续一分钟后会识别出时钟偏差，数字重新变为当前状态。 · 時計が遅れているマシンからの Codex の読み取りが、止まった積み残しとしていつまでも拒否されることはなくなりました — 1 分ほど続くと時計のずれとして認識され、数字が再び最新になります。

Engineering:

- **The floor arms only on a consume that WENT OUT.** The try record was stamped at the WRITE of the verb, so a wrapper older than the idempotency key (codex refused `consume {}` locally), a wrapper that never answered and a vendor `nothingToReset` all armed "already tried in the last 10 minutes" (the owner's screenshot). The wrapper now emits `reset_credit_sent {idempotencyKey, attempt}` right after each consume write and advertises `caps.resetCreditKey`; the engine's attempt record (`openResetCreditTry`, one opener for both writers) carries the spend HOLD, converted into the charge at the send (`noteResetCreditSent`) or given back (`onResetCreditNotSent`, the 90 s ack window — `in_flight` 409 meanwhile). PURE `creditAnswerOf` / `attemptBlock` / `rungBlockUntil` (src/reset-credit.js): only `reset` and a sent-unanswered consume keep the floor; the AUTO rung tries once per limit EVENT and skips a conversation marked `_resetCreditStale`. The answer handler is ONE module-level `handleResetCreditResult` (the wrapper's record and the helper's), matching its attempt by the echoed key.
- **The helper path.** A person's press rides only a `keyed` wrapper (its own sidecar advert); otherwise ONE bounded `codex app-server` child on the account's own login (src/codex-reset-helper.js — initialize, initialized, consume {idempotencyKey}, rateLimits/read; 30 s wall; killed at the end; never rejects; the result a snapshot). Its reading goes through `writeCodexReading` (the one codex snapshot writer, factored out of `recordCodexQuotaSignal`'s `writeSnap`) as `codex-reset-helper`; usage-source names it. Allowlisted deliberately: test-vendor-whitelist §8 (an argv census of every `['app-server', …]` in the server tree with four rows, the helper's one caller after the spend ceiling and the attempt record, human-only route, never the auto rung or a timer, `MEASURED_CONNECTS`, a live strace leg over the stub with a loopback control, five patched-text controls). Measured with scripts/measure-reset-helper.mjs (codex-cli 0.159.3 under `sudo -n unshare -n` + setpriv, empty CODEX_HOME and HOME): our process 0 internet-family calls; the app-server's startup 4 DNS attempts (ENETUNREACH) from `git ls-remote https://github.com/openai/plugins.git` (its plugin marketplace sync), plus `lsb_release -a` and a `bwrap --unshare-net` probe; the logged-out consume answered in 167 ms. The stub app-server moved to scripts/codex-app-server-stub.mjs (one stub for the drift test, the UI suite and the whitelist leg). The dialog prints the harness on the account line ("Codex · CLI login") and the helper's sentence.
- **R3 — the card the credit outlived.** `resolveResetCreditCards(key, ev)` → both normalizers' `resolveResetCreditOffers` (open offers kept in `_rcOffers`, ≤ 64): at a `reset` answer (`used`, with the new window's end when the post-reset reading said it) and at every codex reading (`reset` past the card's stated `resetsAtSec`, `open` when usable) — never while a credit on it is in flight (the current wrapper re-reads BEFORE it answers: that reading is the credit's own). The resolution goes on the message; ONE `edit {resetCredit}` op per card; chat-view patches it in place (`patchResetCredit`) — no re-created card. Cards are in-memory only (never transcript records), so a server restart already drops them.
- **R4 — the answered ⟳.** `POST /api/usage/codex-refresh {key, sessionId}` → `refreshCodexForPerson` (a live local codex chat session on the identity the popup shows; the existing `readCodexLimitsViaSession` waiter, which now settles with the key it wrote) → the reading / `refused` / `archived` / `timeout` / `no_live_session`; PURE `codexRefreshToast` (zh/ja); the popup + roster repaint at the round trip, 2.5 s only as the fallback. The client no longer reads ANY live codex session when the popup shows another account.
- **verify r2 (the additions of r1 attacked; 888a75ab → ad3f3401).** ① MONEY: an attempt on an account whose stored count was unknown was recorded as `creditsAt: 0` (`Number(null)`), so the first reading ("count still 1 ≥ 0") settled an unanswered consume not-landed and the next press minted a second key — null now, a stored 0 read as unknown; then the witness-less attempt got rules (PURE `settleByReading`): `untold` when only the reading carries a count (the block ends, the count named, the next press spends on it), a window restated EARLIER is never a credit's (`R1 > R0`), one rolled to its next natural reset inside the 60 s grace is the clock, an attempt with no window expires once every window began after its send, and an unsettled attempt LAPSES at its wall's reset + grace (else 7 d) — free, said on the dialog (`lapsedLine`), still settled for the ledger. ② MONEY: the helper's app-server exited after taking the consume and the engine read its words as an answered error (free at once, a second key) — the helper's `answered` rides the payload; sent + unanswered = `unanswered` whatever the words. ③ D6: an attempt open at a stop came back `unknown` and was never charged (its hold died with the process) — charged at the boot restore, the file re-written. ④ A torn `data/reset-credit-tries.json` was silently ignored — set aside `.corrupt-<ts>`, warned, ONE For-you item (origin pool, filed lazily). ⑤ GATE: §8's never-a-timer census was engine-only — a tree-wide `consumeResetCreditFor` CALL census (route 2, engine 1; a setInterval in server.js and a new caller in ws-handler are red controls), the strace leg pinned to the FAST (push) tier and RED on a CI runner without strace. Held: the pool moved between the press and the read ⇒ the reading lands under the HELD member (measured); two ⟳ presses on one account ⇒ ONE read (both ride the first live session; two reads only when two clients name their OWN sessions — each conversation's own app-server, acceptable); a setsid'd grandchild survives the group kill (20/20 on a stub) — codex 0.159.3's binary carries bwrap `--die-with-parent`/`--unshare-net`, no `--new-session`, no `setsid` (strings, launch-free), so the real tree is reached; what the app-server WRITES into CODEX_HOME stays unmeasured (the rule: the real app-server is never launched here) — its strings name `sessions/`, `history.jsonl`, `state_5.sqlite`, `version.json`, `logs/`, `plugins/` + a 413-string marketplace block, so a throwaway home copy remains the open design item (with the refresh-token-rotation hazard a copy would introduce).
- **verify r3 (the additions of r2 attacked; the attempt lifecycle pinned as ONE closed table; a82b6f94 → ).** ① MONEY: an unsettled attempt behind a FREE newest record (a helper that never started — codex gone — ended `error` with the unsettled one as its prior) was hidden from the block; the next press carried no prior and consumed with no read first — the block walks the chain (`attemptBlock`), a new attempt's prior is the newest unsettled attempt wherever it sits (`priorForPress`, ≤ 8 live tail entries). ② MONEY: a consume answered in a word no measured table lists (or with no word) read as "answered, nothing spent" and freed the next press — `VENDOR_OUTCOMES` is a closed set (the drift gate pins it equal to every measured table); a word outside it is `unknown-outcome` (charged, the floor, unsettled until a reading), the person told the word. ③ The floor / ack window were judged by the timer's stamp — in the gap between the floor elapsing and the callback (a busy loop) a sent attempt was free and a press minted a second key; an open attempt on a non-reporting carrier past the ack window the same (the helper ran, the open attempt replaced with its timers cleared) — `armedByClock` + clock-judged `isUnsettled` / `settleByReading` / `isLapsed` (`clockOpts`), the timers only durable. ④ A lapsed prior was judged by the reading after its SUCCESSOR's consume (a false "did land") and a chain of lapsed priors grew per press — a send SUPERSEDES its priors (`supersede`: `supersededAt` refuses later readings; a lapsed prior dropped). ⑤ GATE: §8's call census missed `const f = engine.consumeResetCreditFor; setInterval(f)` and `.bind()` — a reference census + bind/call/apply red. ### lane channel-agent-watch — the agent's own watch, the requestable directory, access above a chat, next turn or wake now

The owner's three asks (2026-10-01) + the addendum. Base 7366587e (lane everyone-principal).
- **W3 — access is MAX over the grain and its ancestors.** Reproduced first on the real engine: account access for an agent, then Notify… on one chat ⇒ `watcher-needs-access` (and `grainOf` dropped such a row at read). ONE PURE rule (`eligibleKeys` / `eligibleFor` in src/channel-filter.js): a watcher is valid where its principal holds access at the grain, at an ancestor (the account, a matching rule) or a visible grant reaches it (an approved request); All agents covers everyone. `validateWatchers(list, access, {inherited})`, `grainOf(rec, legacy, {inherited})`, `effectiveGrants(…, {grantKeys, accountKeys})` all read it; the engine passes `convInheritedOf` / `siteInheritedOf`; the dialog reads `conv.eligibleAbove` (same rule) and lists those principals.
- **W5 — `deliveryModeOf(row)`**: `next-turn` (free: the hit block goes to `deliver.stashFor`, no ladder, no ledger) | `wake` (unchanged: cap + spend authorizer + pacer). A row with no `delivery` = every pre-lane row = wake, as before. Notify… gains "When is it told?" (a new row starts at next turn); `watcherView` carries `delivery` + `origin` so a whole-list save never loses them.
- **W1 — `vibespace-channels watch|unwatch`** (POST /api/agent/channels/watch|unwatch): reach first (hidden ⇒ the uniform not-found; requestable / directory ⇒ `no-access` naming `request`); next-turn written at once (ONE row, `origin:'agent'`, keywords as an inline filter), never over the user's row; `wake` = ONE request in the index's `watchRequests` + a For-you item (action `channel-watch-request`, Approve/Deny on the row) decided by the EXISTING `/api/channels/reach-requests/:id/:verdict` route, Approve = exactly the frozen row through `setGrain`. `--regex` refused by name (a pattern over peer text is a stall risk) — keywords only.
- **W2 — the directory**: per account `agentDirectory {groups (default on), singles (default off)}` (PURE `directoryOf` / `validateDirectory` / `directoryListable` in src/channel-acl.js; the Edit dialog's two switches; `PUT /api/channels/adapters/:id {agentDirectory}`); `list --all` = title (belt), kind, member COUNT, last activity, `requestable`; `request` accepts a directory row.
- Gate: scripts/test-channel-agent-watch.mjs (fast, 36; controls: a filter judging by its own grain only, an engine dispatch without the next-turn branch). The engine exports `onFresh` (the suite's seam).

### lane everyone-principal — "All agents" in every place that asks which agents may use something

The owner (2026-10-02, after userW asked for browser profiles every agent shares): every place that configures who may use something offers "All" — "every conversation, now and later" — as the first choice.

- **The census (E1).** scripts/test-everyone-principal.mjs is grep-derived and prints its table: every `principalPicker({…})` call in src/lib is a row — six SURFACES that offer the All row (`everyone:` in the call) and two EXEMPT with a reason — and every reach / ACL model (a tracked src file declaring PRINCIPAL_KINDS / WHO_KINDS / OWNER_KINDS or named *-acl.js / *-reach.js: 7) is a row whose check loads the module and proves its spelling. Before this lane three models had an "everyone" (exit reach's `everyone` mode, a browser profile's `instance` = "All my conversations", msg-acl's open-to-every-outsider levels); four did not (the picker, channel-acl, channel-filter, window-reach).

  | surface | model | everyone before | spelled now |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Channels · Grant access… | channel-filter ACCESS + channel-acl | no | `{kind:'everyone', id:'*'}` access row |
  | Channels · Notify… | channel-filter WATCHERS | no | the same principal; offered while All holds access; a fan-out, a cap per conversation |
  | Channels · Reach & policy → Grant reach to… | channel-acl | no | `{kind:'everyone', id:'*'}` grant |
  | Desktop app · Share with agents (launcher + window) | window-reach | no | `{kind:'everyone', id:'*'}` reach row |
  | Machine · Who can use <machine>? | exit-reach | yes (a radio) | mode `everyone` — the radio gone, the rows beside it kept |
  | Agent browser · Who can use <profile>? | browser-profiles | yes (a radio, the default) | `use.mode:'all'` = owner `instance` — the radios gone, rows kept |
  | Agent group · New group / Invite… | — | EXEMPT | membership, not a permission (§22 D1) |
  | Desktop app · Ask an agent to take control… | — | EXEMPT | a request to ONE agent that may bill |
  | agent ↔ agent messaging | msg-acl | yes | externalVisibility / reachability open to every outsider (no principal list) |
  | raw-API tiers (next lane) | the access row | — | inherits; the census requires `everyone` in src/channel-api*.js when it lands |

- **The picker.** `everyone: {key, name?, hint?}` (or `'roster'` when the caller's rows carry it) draws "All agents · every conversation, now and later" FIRST — above Recent, never hidden by a search, never a recent pick, its chip first, never greyed. It is never Enter's first-row fallback (`armableFirst`: typing "pag" + Enter picks a match) and the first ↓ lands on the first named row (All is one ↑ above) — "every conversation" is never granted by a stray Enter. A new glyph `everyone` (three heads); `users` stays a group's.

What a grant allows is unchanged.
- **The money rule.** An All WATCHER wakes every RUNNING conversation (a billed turn each — the row's hint and the Notify sentence say so). F.fanOutWatchers turns the one stored row into one item per running conversation, keyed `everyone:*><cid>`, each with its OWN pace ledger (`stats.fan[cid]`), pending hits, timers and scope chain; the engine's ten wake-path sites read `wakeEffOf`, the views keep `effectiveFor` (one All row on every card). Controls: one shared ledger ⇒ 2 wakes in all; no cap on a fan target ⇒ every hit bills every conversation. Known scale cost: a held burst keeps up to PENDING_CAP record copies per running conversation on the index row (bounded by the cap × the roster).

- **The words.** All agents / 所有 agent / すべてのエージェント; "Shared with: All agents (N more rows)" on a window's chip, "All agents (N more rows)" on a profile's row, the card line names All first; the agent-facing `not_owner` sentence and vibespace-browser's way-out line name the button "All agents".

### lane desktop-keepalive — the Desktop stream's liveness, and a Paste press that always speaks (userW inc-muoshmqn-dect)

- **K1 measured.** The bridge's keepalive was already a WebSocket protocol ping — the incident's "hidden tab freezes an app-level pong" guess was wrong. The ping frame queues BEHIND the send buffer (WS_HIGH_WATER 8 MiB): a live browser reading at 512 KiB/s behind a full queue never saw a ping and was cut "no pong" (test-desktop-stream-keepalive §6; the 2.369.118 pong-only rule as a patched-copy control reproduces the cut). Fix: ONE `keepAlive` for both bridges + PURE `livenessVerdict` — a pong, or bytes FROM the browser (a reading RFB client asks for each next update), or kernel-accepted bytes through a backlog (`bytesWritten − writableLength`; Node's `bytesWritten` alone counts the socket's own buffer — measured on a dead path) keep the stream; 2 silent rounds ⇒ cut, named `no pong for N ms and nothing acknowledged`.
- **K2.** Proved on the .199 shell (git): the paste box opened without a toast, and a never-settling `readText()` did nothing — the two ways a press left no ring entry. Now PURE `pasteVerdict` (send | queue | refuse), every press said, a 3 s read deadline, a press while down reconnects + queues + pastes on reconnect (30 s bound, then "not pasted"), a watching pane refuses by name, a dead RFB is never re-`disconnect()`ed (noVNC's console error ×3).
- **K3.** The status chip counts the ladder ("Reconnecting n/5…") and words the bridge's own last close (GET /api/vnc/last-close, closed code set `CLOSE_CODES` → zh/ja words).
- **K4 real leg.** test-desktop-keepalive-chrome (new, heavy, ~110 s, 10/10): a real Xvnc singleton + headless Chrome with its own background throttling — the Desktop tab hidden 90 s stays Connected and the bridge closes nothing; the VNC server killed ⇒ the press is said, the text (through the box — headless Chrome holds no system clipboard, measured) goes in while the stream is down and is read back from the X CLIPBOARD with xclip once the ladder respawns the server.
- **The fast tier caught one regression** (test-xpra-client): the shell's "Reconnecting n/5…" overwrote the xpra view's "Connection lost: <reason>" — the ladder words are opt-in (`ladderWords`), set by vnc-view only.
- **Gates.** test-desktop-stream-keepalive 30, test-vnc-view 98 (§9), test-xpra-client 279, test-desktop-keepalive-chrome 10/10, test-architecture 404, test-changelog-style 40, i18n-check, build, the fast tier ALL GREEN (211 suites, 463 s).
