### lane notify-retry — one 5-second attempt decided for ever

The owner (phone screenshot of 设备运维大师, 14:55 PDT): "以前这个是自动唤醒的啊 怎么现在开始排队要我手动发了？". Forensics (read-only): the cron job dc-discussion-watch woke its owner conversation 7 times (09-29 → 10-01 07:36, `lane: message, ok: true`); at 14:17:13 one local peer post answered `timeout` (postToPeer's 5 s) ⇒ stashed ⇒ at 14:17:15 the stash "waits for the next prompt — the 900 B digest does not fit the 0 B left under the inline cap" ⇒ nothing until the owner typed at 14:53, and the hand-over card then said "These completed while this conversation was closed" (the CLI pid lived throughout).

- **The mechanism, measured.** `postToPeer` reported `timeout` only when the `connect` event never arrived in 5 s. On Linux a unix-socket connect completes AT THE SYSCALL or fails at once — measured here with a python listener that never accepts: `listen(1)` queues two, the third answers `EAGAIN@0 ms`, never a hang — and libuv hands the connect callback to the NEXT loop iteration's pending phase, which runs AFTER the timers phase. So any stall of OUR loop longer than the timer, right after `net.connect()`, fired "timeout" on a connection that had already succeeded (the box's load is 100+; the kb already records 11–17 s create/kill loop gaps on a fleet pod). Reproduced in test-notify-retry §1 (c) on the pre-fix copy (`scripts/fixtures/peer-messaging-prefix.js`): a 160 ms synchronous stall over a 40 ms timer = `{ok:false, reason:'timeout'}` while the frame reached the inbox.
- **R2 — the primitive judges by phases.** `postToPeer` now records `phase` (connect → write → written → closed), `elapsedMs`, `transient` (the timer, EAGAIN, ECONNRESET/EPIPE before the flush ⇒ true; ENOENT/ECONNREFUSED/ENOTSOCK ⇒ false: a socket nobody serves), `late` (how far past the timer the verdict came — the one number that tells a stalled loop from a refusing CLI in the journal) and `closeError` (a reset AFTER the flush is named, never a failure — the CLI dedups its inbox; whether it read the frame is the ambiguity). The timer defers its verdict one loop turn (`setImmediate`) so a queued connect / flush is heard first; a write still in flight gets one bounded grace (1 s); a flushed frame is never a timeout. The ladder's journal line carries `phase`, `ms`, `late` and `target mid-turn: yes|no|unknown` (the server's `_isStreaming`; a terminal session by recent output), the jobs engine's `notifyLog` entry carries `phase` / `busy` / `late` — the owner's instance tells us within a day which cause it was.
- **R1 — the retry park (src/server/conversation-deliver.js).** A transient miss while `findPeer` still names a live pid, for a caller that opted in (`opts.retry` — the jobs engine), is PARKED in `data/msg-retry.json` (never stashed): the same text is posted at the conversation's next turn end (server.js wraps the pool engine's `noteTurnEnd` — the ONE name the claude / codex / ACP consumers destructure — to wake the park) and on a bounded backoff while idle (30 s, 1, 2, 5, 10 min, then every 10 min; the SCHEDULE is bounded at 60 min from the first miss — a verifier-class find of my own: bounding at the attempt let the ninth retry schedule a tenth at 68 min), then falls to the producer's stash as `not-reachable` with the attempts' facts. A dead pid / a socket nobody serves stashes at once as before, typed `not-running` (the "no live inbox" answer too). The money: the first attempt's authorization is HELD on the parked entry and converted when the retry lands — ONE billed wake; a hold is given back on its own TTL (a timer at holdAt + RESERVE_TTL − 5 s, never on a reschedule: a turn end inside the TTL converts it without asking again) and the next attempt re-judges; a refusal / a throwing authorizer at a re-judge falls to the stash as `spend-cap` (fail closed, nothing posted). The park's own floor: no retry post within 30 s of the last SUCCESSFUL post to that conversation. On disk at every mutation, an `inflight` stamp during the post (a crash inside it is said by id at the next boot, a duplicate possible, the CLI dedups); the previous process's holds are forgotten and re-judged. A hand-over CLAIMS parked entries by id (`claimRetry`) and TAKES them (`retryTake`, the hold given back — the hand-over bills its own turn); a prompt's drain takes them too when the digest fits (free, `via: 'prompt'`).
- **R3 — the stash speaks through the post when the prompt cannot carry it.** `drainNotifsUnderCap` / `drainStashUnderCap` (agent-routes) ARM a hand-over (`deliver.armStashHandover`, only for a live local peer, in memory) when the section does not fit the inline cap, and log "N stashed notification(s) will arrive as a message when this turn ends" instead of "wait for the next prompt"; the stash-handover module's turn-end listener runs it as ONE frame under the new declared reason `stash-retry` (spelled literally beside `stash-handover`, the spend census reads the literal), after the ladder's floor if a post just landed (deferred, re-checked idle + live + still waiting; a turn running again re-arms for its own end); a refusal leaves the stash and is logged; the next starved prompt re-arms. The arm is consumed before the park's own attempts, so one turn end = one frame. The fact carries `armed: true` and the strip says "they will arrive as a message when this turn ends".
- **R4 — the words.** `renderNotifStash`'s tail is by the entries' `held` kinds ("These arrived while this conversation was not running." / "The agent did not accept these when they arrived (busy or unreachable) — delivered now." / "These were waiting for a retry — delivered now." / rate-floor / spend-cap / mixed); the hand-over card's head carries "— <why>" (`heldWhyOf`, a closed table read back by `handoverFacts` as a nested key the client translates — chat-renderers translates a `{key}` param); `HELD_KINDS` gains `not-running` + `retrying`; the Background Work panel words each kind and the Delivery log says "parked for retry (connect, agent busy) · next attempt 14:17:43" / "after 3 retries"; the strip: "1 notice is being retried for this agent · next attempt in 25 s or when this turn ends", the Details row "Background Work · dc-watch · being retried"; zh / ja for every string.
- **R5 — floors untouched.** The jobs engine's 30 s floor still stamps at the attempt; a delivery that LANDS re-stamps it with the raw text's digest (the floor counts the successful delivery); the park's retries re-ask the ladder's floor, never the budget.
- **Where reality forced a change.** (1) The 60-min bound is on the schedule, not the attempt. (2) A hold is released on its own TTL timer, not when the next step would outlive it — the first cut released it at the 90 s reschedule and the 100 s turn end had to re-authorize (two authorizations for one wake). (3) `not-reachable` for a REMOTE daemon miss keeps the old kind (the brief's scope excludes remote), so the sentence says "busy or unreachable". (4) The `busy` measurement on a terminal session is "recent output", stated as unknown otherwise. (5) The strip's "next attempt in N" is re-spelled only when the fact changes (every attempt re-publishes it) — no ticking clock.
- **Gates.** test-notify-retry (new, fast, 150: §1 the primitive over real unix-socket stubs + a python non-accepting listener (SKIP with evidence without python3) + the pre-fix control; §2 the ladder with a stub registry + a scripted post under a manual clock: parked ⇒ delivered at the turn end with ONE wake billed, dead pid / socket gone ⇒ not-running, the opt-out, the backoff table + the 60-min fall as not-reachable, every hold given back exactly once, a restart keeps the entry once with the in-flight stamp released by name, fail closed + a refused re-judge as spend-cap, the floor, the hand-over's claim + take, two turn ends around one slow post = one post, the census shape; §3 the REAL JobManager: the parked / updated / delivered lines, lastNotify, the floor re-stamped, the fall into its own store (a job record gone too); §4 the fact + words + zh/ja, the REAL hand-over of a parked entry (ONE stash-handover turn, the parked hold back, the card's why, a bounced frame restored as a waiting job notice), a refused hand-over leaves it parked; §5 the REAL drains: a fitting prompt carries the parked entry free, a starved one arms + the words, the turn end posts ONE frame under stash-retry carrying every store, no loop, dead pid ⇒ not armed, the floor's deferral + a re-arm under a running turn, a refusal keeps the stash; wiring pins). Re-pinned deliberately: test-job-model (the "no live inbox" answer is not-running), test-jobs-triage (same), test-spend-paths §5 (ok → parked → stashed), test-stash-strip (the hand-over's claim line + the identity leg's take, two control anchors). Green: test-spend-paths 319, test-job-model 158, test-jobs-triage 89, test-stash-strip 275, test-architecture 404, test-fable-cap-pool-storm 360, test-stdout-registry 252, test-peer-messaging 10, test-peer-delivery 68, test-jobs-engine 60, test-session-schema 22, test-chat-hygiene 161, test-inbox-window-model 126, test-channel-groups 300, test-channel-outbox 378, test-msg-cli-groups 136; test-jobs-panel and test-channel-jump are heavy (chrome) and were not run here.

### lane browser-admin — New profile…, a profile's Chrome build, the browser CLI VibeSpace drives

The owner's two browser gaps (2026-09-30): a profile could not be created by hand (the only create was a conversation's card menu, a label and nothing else), and nothing could pin a browser version. Five chunks, each its own commit.

- **1 · New profile…** The Agent browser panel's bar gains `New profile…`, and a conversation's picker rows "New persistent profile…" open the same dialog (src/lib/browser-new-profile.js + the PURE model) with the conversation's name prefilled (POSTing the adopt route, so rung C keeps its logins). Every provider is a row with its state for the chosen machine (never hidden; CloakBrowser not installed offers Install… behind the download confirm); machines are this computer + paired machines, greyed WITH the reason; "Who can use it" = the principal picker, default every conversation. ONE POST; `use` is judged by the PATCH's own verdict over an empty record BEFORE the mint (`ownerFromUse`) — the record is born with its list in one write.
- **2a · a profile's Chrome build.** `profile.browser` = default | a build under `~/.agent-browser/browsers/chrome-<v>/chrome` on the profile's machine | a chrome file the user names. SHARED src/browser-builds.js: the listing (every folder a row, unusable ones with why), the ONE verdict (well-formed · the user's · chromium · listed · runnable · the §7.4 ladder when the directory was ever written). The executable rides `AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` through `rec.launchEnv` on every launching call of the keeper's session (the measured relaunch rule cloak's executable keeps; `session info` is launch-free); a chromium build pin does NOT set `launchFlags` (the heal's `get cdp-url` carries the same env, so it relaunches the same build). A vanished build is refused at the launch by name (`browser_build_missing`), marked on the record and filed once in For you — never a fall back. Change build… = `setBrowserChoice`: a running browser restarts and every conversation leased on it is told first (the mediator's interrupt for a mediated lease, the in-flight reader, one `onRelaunch` event → the handback announcer's card + a zero-spend `browser-relaunch` notice — never the input seam, a restart is not a takeover), its tabs reopen (`reopenLeaseTabs`, extracted from the switch). Paired machines: the `browser-serve` op gains `builds` and a start carrying the build (the machine keeps the view in `<ns>.build.json` for every later op); capability `browser-builds` — an older agent is never asked and never handed a start with a build (`builds_unsupported`). The panel row, the switch dialog's build row and the live pill's tooltip say which build RUNS (the browser's own /json/version).
- **2b · the browser CLI.** Setting `browser.cli` = path | pinned (0.38.1, the flag table's version) | x.y.z. `resolveRealBinary` gains ONE rung first (an absolute, existing, non-shim pinned path), used by the keeper (in-memory pin), browser-env (`cliPinReader`) and the agent's CLI (the pin file beside it). The install shares THE slot with the CloakBrowser install (never two at once): one detached `npm install --prefix <data>/browser-tools/agent-browser-<v> --no-save --ignore-scripts agent-browser@<v>` named in a marker (a restart re-attaches), verified off the folder and the program's own `--version`; the tarball ships native binaries 0644 (measured), so the verify makes this machine's binary executable. Measured once (2026-10-01): 52 885 291 B tarball / 119 129 537 B unpacked from registry.npmjs.org, sha1 equal to the registry's shasum — the download confirm's numbers. Both install routes refuse an agent's token. test-vendor-whitelist §8 allowlists the slot with its gates (USER-ONLY incl. the proposal runner's approve-only install, ONE SPAWN, REGISTRY, ONE SLOT) and four ungated copies as controls.
- **2c · Install a Chrome build… — HELD.** The CLI's `install` takes no version (0.38.1 `--help`), and measuring its hosts + wiring a proxy for them exceeds the bound; both build pickers say the command the user runs by hand (the real CLI by its path — in a VibeSpace terminal the bare name is the agent's shim) and that the list refreshes on reopen.
- **3 · the agent's side.** `vibespace-browser providers` prints the machine's builds and the driver version in use (versions only); an agent's `new` refuses a build (`browser_choice_user_only`), Change build… and the installs refuse its token, `--executable-path` / `install` stay refused; the agent manual says it in one bullet.
- **Found by the heavy pass.** (a) The panel's housekeeping rows did not carry the profile's build choice (the row said "default" for a pinned profile) — `browser`/`buildMissing` added in routes/browser-trace.js. (b) THE ROW SIGNATURE NEVER HELD: the panel's `rowSig` carried the raw `ageMs`, so every load rebuilt every profile row since the 2026-09-27 keyed rows (a press across a load hit a detached node) — it now carries the age as the words the row prints. (c) Measured on the real 0.38.1 here: a Chrome for Testing build dies "No usable sandbox!" without `--no-sandbox` — the CLI's default build exactly like a pinned one; the args come from the machine config the keeper composes (the real-binary leg writes its scratch HOME's own config).
- **Gates.** New fast suites: test-browser-new-profile (39), test-browser-builds (64), test-browser-cli-pin (49); touched: test-vendor-whitelist (§8, 113), test-browser-verbs (the rung order, 570), test-browser-human (the walk of the five new user-only routes; Change build… in the holder census, 191), test-browser-stuck (row-signature pins, 286), test-peer-text-census (the new notice kind, 355). - **Verify r1 (the authority, credential and kill classes, 2026-10-01).** F1 (MED, authority): Change build… on a browser the user was DRIVING from a live view (a takeover) restarted it under his hands — `setBrowserChoice` asked only `humans` (Browse yourself) and `switching`, and `stop(why:'switch')` lets a takeover stand; reproduced (takeover → Change build… ⇒ `restarted:true`, the relaunch card sent to the agent while the user drove). F2 (MED, kill/credential): a HALF-WRITTEN CLI install was resolved and pinned — npm extracts the package in place (package.json + the 0755 launcher land seconds before the 18 MB native binaries), the panel sets `browser.cli` right after the POST, and `cliPin()` read the folder: the launcher of a half-extracted package became the pin (the pin file written, the keeper / browser-env / the agent's CLI ran it) until `finishCli` re-memoed; reproduced with an early-writing fake npm (and the same read served a program that did not say its version — the suite asserted `installed:true` for a FAILED verify). Fix: THE WITNESS `<prefix>/verified.json`, written only after the program said the version; `installedCliOf` answers `not verified…` without it; the witness removed before npm runs and after a failed verify; a patched copy reading the folder alone is control ⑥c (test-browser-cli-pin 56). Fix: THE marker is both kinds' (`markInstall`, written by `runStep` for every CloakBrowser step), `reattachInstall` holds the slot for either kind until the pid is gone, then `finishCloakAfterRestart` judges what is on disk (a stamp / the measured SHA-256 ⇒ installed, else failed by name — install again, a finished download is reused); a patched copy that drops the cloak marker is control ⑥d (test-browser-cli-pin 62). F4 (LOW, honesty): a pinned install that vanished (the tools folder wiped) still read "installed" — `cliPin()` served its memo (keyed on the setting and the install generation) until the setting moved or a restart, the pin file still named the gone program; reproduced. Fix: the memo is re-stat'ed on every call (one stat per resolve) — gone ⇒ not installed at once, the pin file removed, PATH answers, said in the journal; control ⑥e (test-browser-cli-pin 65). F5 (LOW, credential — the lane's own "versions only" rule): a `{kind:'path'}` choice's PATH reached the agent on every profile-shaped answer (`agentProfileView` spreads the record: `browser.path`, `buildMissing.what`), on `status`'s lease rows (`browserView` carries `browserChoice` AND the launch view `launchEnv` with `AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH`) and on the switcher view `forAgent`; only `providers` stripped its root. Fix: `agentChoiceView` / `agentMissingView` (PURE), `agentProfileView` by kind only, the keeper's `agentBrowserView` + the routes' `agentBrowserOf` (status / use / resolve) drop the launch view; controls ⑤e (the view keeps the path) and ⑤f (status hands the launch view) (test-browser-builds 74). F6 (LOW, authority): an agent's own token on the human create route wrote a who-list (`use` — the lane's field), on the adopt route too, and on the PATCH of "Who can use it" (pre-existing, same class); the create refused an agent token only when it named a BUILD. Reproduced over the real routes (200s). Fix: `USE_IS_USERS` — an agent bearer with `use` ⇒ 403 `agent_forbidden` on all three doors; a create with no list still answers (every conversation, as the agent's `new` makes); control ⑤d is the opened create (test-browser-new-profile 43). F7 (MED, authority — what you approve is what runs): the picker's "New persistent profile…" drew the dialog's form off the rung alone (`browserVariant === 'C'` ⇒ keep, else empty), but rung D — the default — KEEPS its directory since lane browser-resume, so the dialog offered a browser / machine / Chrome build and the adopt route took the keep branch and dropped them in silence (reproduced over the real route: Chrome 146 ⇒ the default build, CloakBrowser ⇒ Chromium, 200 `adopted:true`); and an EMPTY profile on a paired machine was refused "browser profiles are local-only" (the route's refuseHost on the body's host), worded by the dialog as "not paired any more". Fix: ONE plan `adoptPlanOf(f)` answered by `GET /api/browser/adopt?sessionId=` and used by the POST; the picker asks it before the dialog opens, the dialog draws that form (PURE `adoptFormOf`; an unanswered ask falls back to the rung); the keep branch refuses another browser / machine / port / build by name (409 `adopt_keeps_browser`, nothing moves); an empty profile's host is judged by the create's own verdict; control ⑤e is the silent drop (test-browser-new-profile 51). F8 (LOW, kill — the brief's "a second install after the restart refused for how long?"): for as long as npm lived — the CLI install's detached npm had no wall clock (CloakBrowser's steps always had 15 min) and a step RE-ATTACHED after a restart had none either, so a stalled registry held THE one slot (both installs `install_running`) without bound, before and after a restart; reproduced with a never-ending npm (no deadline armed in-process, none on the re-attach). Fix: interrupt before the stop (unchanged), tell after the outcome — `outcome` `changed` | `restored` | `down` on the event, the card and the zero-spend notice (`relaunchText`); control ⑤g is the early tell (test-browser-builds 80). F10 (LOW, honesty — the brief's "the drift note's words with each mode"): a version the user NAMED in `browser.cli` (Settings: "0.39.2") — the panel's one button said "Install the measured version…" and installed 0.39.2, and once in use the row said "in use: VibeSpace's own 0.39.2 (your choice)" with no drift word and no warning while PATH's 0.38.0 "— drifts" and warns (the agent's `providers` line does say the table was measured on 0.38.1); reproduced on the PURE model. Fix: `cliRowWords` answers the `version` an install installs, `cliOfferLabel(offer, t, {version, table})` says "Install agent-browser 0.39.2…" for a named one, the in-use row says "— drifts" and warns; control ⑥g is the old words (test-browser-cli-pin 74).

H2 BUILT (MED, authority — the brief's "never under the user's hands"): a takeover landed inside a Change build… restart (after its stop, before the new launch — ~0.3 s on the real 0.38.1 + Chrome here) and was ACCEPTED; the restart then launched the new build, reopened the lease's tab and told the conversation "changed" while the user drove (reproduced on the real keeper with the pre-fix source and with the fake). Fix: the picker's door sends the `form` it drew; a changed plan ⇒ 409 `adopt_form_changed` by name, nothing moved; control ⑤f. With it H3 (the r1 held item): the picker's row now claims neither keep nor empty ("New persistent profile from this conversation…"), and the empty form says what it is in plain words (zh / ja) (test-browser-new-profile 59). ### lane custom-app — apps that survive a rebuilt machine (Layer 0 of docs/design-app-persistence.zh.md, B-ce6d)

The owner: users install apps, their agents help, and the apps survive a pod recreation. Layer 0 = the manifest + the local `.deb` cache + the human gate, on every pod with no image or chart change (Layer 1, the app SYSTEM on the volume, is the next lane). D3 as revised: the door is the user's (the Desktop apps dialog); an agent only proposes; ZERO new lines in the per-turn teaching.

- **PURE src/app-manifest.js** — the index schema, apt's own words → the plan with named refusals (needs_snap · conflict · removes · not_found · bad_name · bad_source · no_sudo · no_apt · disk with the numbers · shared), .desktop → catalog rows through validateAppRow, the dpkg set byte-identical to the root script's `q` (the base sha), the repository's stanzas / file names (no `%3a` — the epoch dropped), cacheVerdict (closure − base ⊆ cache, P15), replayRungs, driftVerdict, and THE ONE root script (nine modes; every name an argv POSITION; every argument judged before root is asked; the authority root reads is root-owned `debs/` + `sys/`, never the user-writable manifest; `SUDO_UID`'s own apps dir only). Fixtures are REAL: this Ubuntu box's `apt-get -s` and a throwaway Debian 12 container's installs (scripts/capture-app-fixtures.sh); the one invented input is the snap simulation's empty dpkg status. Measured shape the parser had wrong at first: a Debian 12 security-mirror `--print-uris` line has NO hash.
- **SHARED src/app-serve.js** (bundled by the daemon through desktop-serve) — the six `app-*` ops of the desktop-serve table: plans as the user (the system's lists, else the user's own — a container image ships none), a .deb staged + bound by sha256, a source's key fetched over https with its OpenPGP fingerprints (checked against gpg's on two real public keyrings); the RECORD reads the slot's own log by the run's nonce and the ROOT-OWNED entries (a user-written list or a forged log line is never a row). Capability `app-install` in the hello-ack; the client asks the app ops only of a daemon that names it.

### lane mobile-select — a long press on chat text selects it; the message menu opens from a … button

**User line (Fixed):** On a phone, pressing and holding text in a chat now selects it as it should — the message menu no longer pops up over the words you are selecting; it opens from the message's … button instead.
**zh:** 在手机上，长按聊天里的文字现在会正常选中它 — 消息菜单不再弹在你正在选择的文字上；改为从消息的 … 按钮打开。
**ja:** スマートフォンでチャットの文字を長押しすると、正しく選択されるようになりました — 選択中の文字の上にメッセージメニューが開くことはなくなり、メニューはメッセージの … ボタンから開きます。

- **The report and the measured order.** A tester's phone (via the owner): copying a passage of a chat opened the message menu and the selection landed on the menu. Measured in Chrome's own touch gesture path (`Emulation.setEmitTouchEventsForMouse('mobile')`, 390×844 DPR 3, Android UA — `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` never produces the native long press in headless): touchstart on the `<p>` → +501 ms OUR synthetic (untrusted) contextmenu, the chat cancels it and opens its menu with the corner at the finger → +680 ms the native long press: selectstart (the word is selected) → a TRUSTED contextmenu, pointerType touch → the chat cancels it and builds the menu a second time → selectionchange with the word under the menu. iOS fires no contextmenu on a long press: our 500 ms timer was the only menu, racing iOS's selection (the code assumes exactly that). The cause: design-mobile-gaps #5 (2026-09-20) made a long press ANYWHERE on a message open its menu, because the hover buttons are hidden ≤ 768 px.
- **M1 — one door, one rule.** PURE `src/lib/press-select.js` (press target class × device ⇒ menu | selection | native) and utils.js `installLongPressContextMenu`, THE door of a touch long press: on selectable text (a glyph within 6 px of the finger whose effective user-select is not none) the timer is never armed and a trusted touch contextmenu is stopped before any handler WITHOUT preventDefault (the platform's handles and Copy bar stay); controls (button, summary, role=button, menus), gutters, pictures and user-select:none labels keep the menu; once an app handler took such a menu press, `selectstart` is cancelled while the finger is down (the heavy leg's second measurement: a long press on a message's 3 px role strip opened our menu, then Chrome selected "Answer" and that selection closed the menu), and when the platform's long press comes first our contextmenu fires at its `selectstart`; a press nobody takes (the file viewer) keeps the platform's selection and its own long-press menu; the trusted contextmenu is one PURE table (pass / stop on text / swallow after ours was taken — it had built the menu twice). The chat's menu on touch: a … button per user / assistant message (`addMsgMoreBtn`, 36×28, floated as the content's first child — the words wrap around it; measured: over none of 8 messages' words), plus a long press on the role strip, a `<summary>` toggle or the role label (`.chat-role` is now user-select none). Mouse right-click unchanged. The rule reaches every `user-select` opt-in (the chat list, the For-you texts, the For-you window's item); their menus stay on the rows' non-text parts.
- **M2 — chrome text is never selectable.** style.css says `user-select: none` ITSELF on `[data-popover], .context-menu, #global-toasts, .global-toast, .overlap-switcher, .tab-item, .chat-msg-more` (unprefixed like the page rule — an inherited `-webkit-` none breaks typing in a field on older iOS), so chrome built inside a selectable region never inherits `text`; `onOutsidePress` gained `selection` (default = once): on a touch device a transient menu / popover closes when a text selection starts outside it (a long press is never an outside tap, so the closer never saw it), never on a caret, a form control's selection, its own opening selection or a mouse device.
- **M3 — Copy text names what it copied.** The touch menu's Copy text puts the WHOLE message on the clipboard and says so: "Copied the whole message (N lines)" (zh/ja added) — the terminal's Copy screen precedent; a code block keeps its own Copy button.
- **Gates.** test-press-select (new, fast, 66 — the PURE tables, the real door under a dispatch model + fake clock, the selection closer, the grep-derived user-select opt-in census (22 declarations, each a row with a reason) + the chrome rule, wiring pins, three patched-copy controls) · test-mobile-select (new, heavy, 30, ~46 s — both touch paths in real Chrome, the … button, chrome presses with one build and no stray selection, Copy text on the clipboard + its toast, the closer, the live census with a plain-div control, desktop right-click unchanged) · test-mobile-gaps #5 now opens the menu from the … button (ALL PASS) · test-architecture / i18n-check in the build.
- **Verify r1 (2026-10-02, adversarial round; three MED findings reproduced in real Chrome, each fixed here).** F1 a message whose FIRST block is a code block: its toolbar's "Wrap" was the element under the … (a tap toggled wrap, not the menu) and the `pre` was 38 px narrower to its last line (a table-first message likewise — a formatting context beside a float is narrowed for its whole height) ⇒ chat.css `.chat-msg:has(.chat-msg-more) :is(.chat-pre-wrap, .chat-table-wrap) { clear: right }`. F2 BUBBLE mode (Compact mode off): the bubble is a shrink-to-fit flex item and a block's max-content counts a float + a following block as max(), never the sum ⇒ every short message's words sat under the button ("hi" 41 → 68 px wide, +28 px tall; the assistant's … alone on the left) ⇒ `addMsgMoreBtn` hosts the button in the bubble's first inline-content block (`p` / `h1–h6`, else `.chat-text`), one per message. F3 a touch TABLET (isTouch, wider than 768 px — 1024 px at UI scale 100 and 125): the hover buttons were hidden ≤ 768 px only, so an invisible "Open in editor" covered the … and a tap on it opened the editor ⇒ hidden by app.isTouch's own media query. Refuted with evidence: a link's long press (a TAP on a link already opens Open / Copy on touch), the For-you popup (not a data-popover — its words select, the row menu from the meta line), Message details (its ids are click-to-copy; the popup inherited `none` before the lane), the uiScale 1.25 menu position (showContextMenu divides by the scale: dTop +2, left clamped to the viewport), the keyed swap (the button and an open menu survive it). Held (LOW, named): a `[data-popover]` with opt-in text (the mini inbox popover) is a menu press; a pen contextmenu without touch events opens the menu; a CJK paragraph gains one line beside the float (+17 px) by design; an open menu closes when the user extends a selection by its handles (the selection wins). Gates: test-press-select 69 (+3 pins), test-mobile-select 39 (①'s centre / narrowed / beside checks, ①b bubble mode, ⑨ the tablet), test-mobile-gaps 84.

### lane-drag-release — a release over a pane the page cannot hear (userW's inc-muq7uk0f-e59s, 17:19 PDT; the addendum inc-muq7wwfq-rruz, 17:21 PDT)

The owner, twice within two minutes (Mac, DPR 2.2, UI scale 0.9, a PDF `viewer` window over a Desktop window): a PDF viewer dropped onto the cell of the Desktop window did not fit — the snap highlight stayed, the window stayed put, the drag stayed armed; a resize released over that window kept resizing when the pointer came back ("松开鼠标之后，仍然像是抓着这个缩放的角落"); and the viewer could grow but not shrink ("能放大，不能缩小").

THE CLASS (the lane M class, second strike). The title-bar drag and the resize ended on a document-level `mouseup`. A release hit-tested on another window's iframe never reaches this document (the embedded page gets it — the Web view, the PDF viewer's own page is an iframe); noVNC's canvas stops its mouse events (stopPropagation + preventDefault). So the release was never heard: the drag stayed armed with its highlight, and the moves of an inward resize over the viewer's OWN page were lost too (it grew, it would not shrink). REPRODUCED FIRST in chrome on a 2×3 grid with a Web view iframe, a real Xtigervnc Desktop, a fake agent-browser live view and the real xpra rung (scripts/test-window-drag-ui.mjs, DRJ_ONLY=D,R,P): the drop and the inward resize over the Web view and the Desktop reproduced red on b924041f; the live-view picture and the xpra pane do NOT stop a mouse release (measured, printed) — the Web view and the Desktop are the two provable swallowers, and the PDF viewer's own frame is the third.

D1 POINTER CAPTURE ENDS EVERY DRAG. The title bar and each resize handle take a POINTER press and `setPointerCapture` the pointer on that element; the drag is fed from it (capture delivers every pointer event there whatever the cursor crosses — an iframe, a canvas, another window, the page's edge). ONE end door per drag: PURE `src/lib/drag-end.js` `dragEndVerdict` names what ends one — pointerup / pointercancel / lostpointercapture of the drag's pointer, the window's blur, the page hidden, and a `pointermove` with `buttons === 0` (a release the page never saw); another pointer's events, a held move, the page becoming visible and a second end are no-ops (the drag ends ONCE — the snap highlight cleared there, the drop applied where the pointer last was). The existing holds (the pointerup's geometry witness `_boundsAt`, the `_bornAt` rule) key on the same door. A press the browser gives no pointerId (or refuses capture) falls to a document feed with every end rule still applied. The seamless hand-over (xpra `initiate-moveresize`) carries the press's pointerId and captures it too.

D2 THE DRAG SHIELD. `body.wm-dragging` (set at the drag's threshold and the resize's start, lifted at the end door) ⇒ every window's content — and iframe / canvas / img / embed / object by name — is `pointer-events: none !important` (public/style.css), so the snap hit test is the workspace's for the whole gesture and no pane takes the moves or the release. The title bar and the handles are `touch-action: none` (a touch drag is pointermove, never the page's pan).

D3 THE OCCUPIED CELL. Unchanged stacking: the drop fits the dragged window into the cell exactly as onto an empty one (`_snapToGrid` → `_positionToCell`), two windows share the cell (a cell is a position, never a slot — the occupant's box is untouched); the highlight is the keyed grid-cell element, cleared by the end door, never a timer.

D5 THE VIEWER THAT COULD GROW BUT NOT SHRINK. With capture + the shield, the inward resize over the viewer's own iframe is delivered and `clampToMin` holds the window at its minimum. A `viewer` / `editor` / `browser` window has NO minimum of its own — `windowMinForPane`/`setMinSize`'s only caller is the desktop-app window (pinned); the floor is the `.window` CSS 320×180. The clamp reads the pointer delta in layout px (viewport ÷ the UI scale), so at scale 0.9 × DPR 2.2 the shrink the pointer asks for is the shrink it gets. Measured in chrome: a 1000×700 PDF viewer at UI 90 % × DPR 2.2 shrinks to 320×180, left/top kept.

Gates: test-window-drag (fast, 33 — the PURE end-door table, the real WindowManager over a fake DOM modelling pointer capture + a swallowing iframe + a stopping pane: the incident, every end kind for the drag and the resize, D3, the D5 × zoom × dpr table, the setMinSize census; controls = one drag-end copy per rule + the pre-capture feed). test-window-drag-ui (heavy, the reproduction + the base commit b924041f as the control bundle via esbuild onLoad). test-window-minsize and test-desktop-seamless updated to the pointer door (their fake `fireDoc` now sets `event.type`, as the DOM does). test-desktop-move / test-stage-visibility / test-split-ux / test-outside-press / test-architecture unchanged.

VERIFY r1 (adversarial, 2026-10-01). Two findings, both reproduced in chrome on b2fc3f89 before the fix. (1) HIGH — the third and fourth drag doors were still the pre-fix feed: the TAB TEAR-OFF (`tab-group.js _setupTabDrag`) and the ICON-merge drag (`_setupIconDrag`) ended on the document's `mouseup`, so a torn-off tab released over the Web view / Desktop pane stayed `.dragging` with the highlight on and armed, and an icon drag released there left its source window `visibility:hidden` with the ghost on screen (the window vanished). FIX = ONE feed for the four doors: `src/lib/drag-feed.js` (`captureOn`, `attachDragFeed` — DRAG_FEED's four events on the capturing element else the document, the window's blur, the page's visibility, a per-drag controller joined to the owner's —, `setDragShield`); window.js's two doors moved onto it, tab-group.js's two doors take a pointerdown, capture the pointer (the tab drag on the strip's TITLE BAR — the element the tear-off's re-render keeps; the tab element is rebuilt and a capture on it would be lost under the finger), ask `dragEndVerdict` at one end door each, and raise the shield. (2) LOW — the xpra hand-over's hold (`xpra-view.js wmHold`) waited for a document pointerup alone: a drag the WM now ends on blur / hidden / a no-button move left the pane deaf (no motion to X) and the X button down until the next click anywhere; the hold now asks the same verdict (pointerup / pointercancel / pointermove buttons==0 / blur / hidden) and releases the button at once. Measured in chrome: a mouse OR pen release the page never saw arrives as `lostpointercapture` first, then a `pointermove` with `buttons === 0` — both rules end a drag; no title-bar re-render (rename, chips, a rebuilt tab bar) replaces the title-bar ELEMENT, so a capture on it survives every re-render (window.js:113 creates it once; `_renderTabBar` rebuilds children only). Gates: test-window-drag 36 (icon-drag end-kind rows over the real mixin on the fake DOM; the pre-capture control is now a closed world of three copies — drag-feed / tab-group / window — so one patched feed reverts every door; §4 pins ONE feed and no document mouse feed in either file), test-window-drag-ui (+ legs T / I: the torn-off tab and the icon drag onto each pane; the control overlays the base commit's tab-group.js too), test-xpra-client 279 (its fake events now carry `type`, as the DOM's do).

VERIFY r2 (adversarial, 2026-10-02; the door census + attacks on r1's parts). (1) HIGH — a window CLOSED mid-drag (closeWindow aborts `_listenerCtl` first ⇒ the feed died, no end door ran) left `body.wm-dragging` up for good: every window's content dead to the mouse until another drag completed (chrome: the Web view iframe `pointer-events:none`, grid overlay + highlight stuck, the icon's ghost stuck). FIX = the feed's `owner-gone` end (drag-feed.js, named by PURE drag-end.js) + every door CANCELS, nothing dropped. (2) LOW — the shield was a boolean: a mouse + a touch drag at once, the first end lowered it for the second ⇒ `setDragShield(on, key)`, a holder set. (3) THE CENSUS (T1): twelve handle-style doors still on the document's mouseup / a bare pointerup (Resizer, theme editor ×2, minimap, top-bar + taskbar handles, explorer column, viewer pan + pptx sidebar, customize move, split divider, queue reorder) ⇒ ONE call `startPointerDrag`; test-window-drag §5 = the grep-derived census (16 feed doors in 10 files, every document/window move-or-end listener named with its reason, 3 planted controls). Gate test-window-drag 36 → 53: owner-gone legs, the fake DOM's removal rule (T2⑤) + legs, two feeds as two holders, the `!win` branch pinned by its statements (T2⑥), two feed controls. Refuted: the 3-tab host / active-guest tear-off (chrome: ended + fit), the xpra hold's new ends, the widened pin's harm.

### lane profile-lock-roll — a renamed machine's profile lock, and the first command after a restart (userW's pod test, 2026-10-01 14:24–14:35 PDT)

Read-only forensics of userW's pod (2.369.198, image 3.6.0, agent-browser 0.38.1, Chromium 154) after a pod roll (hostname `vibespace-pod-a-5d6f7c8b9a-x1y2z` → `…-7e8f9a0b1c-p3q4r`, the same RWO home):

- **W1 — the lock of a dead pod.** His pinned profile "jarvis-work" refused every start: `profile_locked — … is held by another browser process (pid 452500 on vibespace-pod-a-5d6f7c8b9a-x1y2z) — the lock (…/SingletonLock) names another machine … remove …`. Chromium's `SingletonLock` is a symlink `<hostname>-<pid>` inside the profile directory on the PVC; the old pod died with it in place; Chromium judges the lock by hostname and refuses for ever. His agent removed `Singleton{Lock,Socket,Cookie}` by hand, as the sentence suggested.
- **W2 — the bound tab of the previous life.** Right after the hand-fix the first verbs answered `tab_gone: bound tab is gone (target DC0C…, last url about:blank). Run agent-browser tab new …` — the binary keeps a session's bound tab (by CDP target id) across a daemon restart (its own `tab --help`) and, pinned, refuses once it is gone; every tab of a replaced browser is gone. The keeper's `stop()` already marks every lease so its next attach binds a tab first — a browser life the keeper did NOT end (a daemon found dead, a boot that could not adopt it, an in-place relaunch) left the leases unmarked.
- **W3 — not this lane.** `navigator.webdriver` true under the hidden-window rung on 2.369.198: the automation flag shipped in 2.369.199 (lane browser-propose); the remedy is ⚙ → Update.

**L1 — the lock verdict knows a renamed machine (src/browser-profiles.js `profileLockVerdict`, src/server/browser-keeper.js, src/browser-facts.js).** The witness is the keeper's OWN registry, never an assumed RWO fact: every launch stamps the browser record with the machine's hostname (`rec.host`, the lineage `rec.hosts`, ≤ 8, carried onto every new record like the launch mark) and `save()` stamps the registry file with its writer (`reg.host`). `profileLockVerdict({…, launchHosts})`: a lock whose hostname ≠ ours AND ∈ the recorded launch hosts ⇒ `stale-previous-host` — `clearProfileLock` removes the three Singleton SYMLINKS (`F.removeSingletonFiles`, a regular file of that name is left), says in the journal "the lock named this machine's previous name <old> — taken over (… removed; this machine is <new>)", stamps the profile `renamedFrom {host, at}`, and launches; the chat and the panel never see `profile_locked`. A foreign hostname NOT in the launch hosts stays `foreign`, refused by name — the sentence now names BOTH hostnames and the ONE command (`rm -f '<dir>/SingletonLock'`), never "held by another browser process" for a lock nobody is known to hold. A legacy record (no stamp) inherits the hostname the registry FILE was last saved under (`fileHost`, read at load before this process's first save re-stamps it), else nothing — userW's pod, on its first update after the roll, still meets the old lock with no witness and is refused by name with the command; every roll after that is taken over by itself. `reapOrphan` passes a `stale-previous-host` lock over (nothing of that name can hold it; the next start takes it over); the heal removes it too.

**L2 — a bound tab of a previous life rebinds (src/server/browser-keeper.js, src/browser-tabs.js, data/bin/vibespace-browser).** `tabsLost(profileId)` marks every lease of a NAMED profile whose browser was replaced without a stop — `markDaemonGone` (the tick, a start, the boot's judgement), `adoptAll`'s not-adopted branch (the pod-roll shape: the daemon died while VibeSpace was down), `recaptureBrowser`'s `replaced` (an in-place relaunch, the heal) — with WHY (`reg.tabLostWhy`: `life` | `closed`; the four existing writers say `closed`). At the next attach the bind prefers the browser's ONE page that no holder roots (PURE `TBS.rebindPick` over the CDP target list + `tabHoldersOf`: a fresh launch's single `about:blank`; the url read off the raw target — `pageTargets` keeps none) ⇒ `tab <targetId>` (no second blank tab per relaunch); anything else (several pages, the only page another holder's or the user's, targets unreadable) ⇒ `tab new` of its own, never another holder's; a mediated lease keeps `tab new` through its grant. The attach's answer carries `rebound {how, targetId, url, why, text}` (PURE `TBS.reboundNoteText`), the CLI prints it once as `note: your tab from the previous run is gone (the browser was restarted) — bound to <url>; re-read the page before continuing [tab_rebound]`. `tab_gone` stays for the mid-run case (the agent's tab closed by the user, r2 F3).

**L3 — said where the user looks.** The journal (the takeover line, the loss line "its browser is gone with … — N lease(s) bind a tab again at their next command", the bind line); the Agent browser panel's profile row: a `renamed from <old>` chip (title: the two names) for a day (`B.renamedFromFact`, `RENAMED_SHOWN_MS`), a launch-host chip only when the record's host differs from this machine's (`list().machine.host`); zh / ja. The housekeeping row carries `launchHost` + `renamedFrom`.

**verify r2 (2026-10-01) — the lock verdict as one closed table, four findings fixed (ee30e073, 81f80e40, a09a9178).** The table: pid × hostname × the live pid's command line × the record, 70 cells pinned in test-browser-share-model ④e with the keeper on six cells over real processes and a control per rule; it found F4 (MEDIUM): our own orphan ended under a previous name of this machine left its lock named that machine and the launch went into it — Chromium never clears a foreign name's lock (measured on 154: it hangs on its dialog) — `clearEndedOrphanLock` removes it after the end. F1 (LOW): a directory taken between the verdict and the launch answered a generic launch failure, `lockRefusalAfterLaunch` names the holder at the first answer (④f). F2/F3 (LOW): a session detached while queued behind another's rebind opened a blank tab and spent its mark — re-asked after the wait; the wait is said (test-browser-kept ⑭e). ### lane install-ellipsis — the Mac repair command died on one byte

- 2026-10-02 (the owner's Macbook, 2.369.199): `bash: line 253: DHOST?: unbound variable` — macOS /bin/bash 3.2 absorbs a byte ≥ 0x80 after `$NAME` into the name, so the dial-check echo's `$DHOST…` read an unset `DHOST\xe2` under `set -u` and the installer died before the check. Fix `${DHOST}…`; gate = test-dial-facts' macOS bash 3.2 census over every shipped shell script (installer, install.sh, scripts/*.sh) + the pre-fix line as the control (381). Workaround before the fix: pipe through `perl -pe 's/\xE2\x80\xA6/.../g'`.

### lane reaper — the scratch-orphan reaper judges by ownership evidence (B-1d08)

**the release gate's cleanup of leftover test processes no longer kills another run's processes or a shell that merely names a /tmp/vs-* file: it acts only on processes whose scratch directory's owner is provably gone, one sweep at a time**

#### The scratch-orphan reaper judges by ownership evidence (B-1d08, 2026-09-29)

Three incidents in one day: two lanes' fast tiers ran at once and one run's cleanup killed a process the other run's suite had just planted; a coordinator's `node scripts/ci.mjs --check-heavy > /tmp/vs-checkheavy.txt` was killed because a FILE named like a scratch dir was read as one; and a finished verifier's scratch server left 15 device daemons running for an hour (the case the cleanup exists for, kept).

- **A scratch directory has an owner on record.** The process that creates one writes `<dir>/.vs-run.json` — its pid, its start time and the boot (scripts/scratch-run.mjs). `scripts/scratch.mjs` `scratchDir()` (new: create + stamp) and `scratchHome()` stamp it, so do mutant-copy's dirs and the gate's own isolated worktrees (`.vs-run.json` is gitignored).
- **Three facts convict a leftover process, never a name:** the path it names is a real DIRECTORY under `/tmp/vs-*` (a file, a symlink, another user's dir, or a gone path nothing proves was a directory is not a root); that directory's OWNER is gone (the pid is gone, was reused by another process, is a zombie, or is from another boot — or the directory is gone with its record); and the process is older than the 10-minute stale floor (the old "directory gone" rule had no age). A process that names ANY directory whose owner is alive is never touched, whichever run owns it. A directory with no record keeps the old rule.
- **One sweep at a time.** Every sweep takes a machine-wide `flock` (released by the kernel when its holder dies); a sweep that cannot get it within 5 s skips and prints one line saying so. The fast tier still takes no machine lock — two fast tiers may run; only their sweeps wait for each other.
- **`node scripts/ci.mjs --reap`** keeps the same rules and the same lock (exit 3 when it could not take it), each victim line now names its evidence: the owner's state, the age, and what named the directory, and its closing count treats a victim that died but is not yet reaped by its parent as reaped, not "still alive". **`--reap --dry-run`** prints the verdict for every candidate — what would be reaped and why, what is spared and why (for example "its root's owner is alive"), and the processes that name a `/tmp/vs-*` path that is not a scratch directory.
- The test seam that points the cleanup at a fake process table (`VIBESPACE_CI_REAP_PROCFS`) is accepted only under a `/tmp/vs-*` scratch directory — by its real path, and only while that directory's owner is alive — and says so on every sweep; anywhere else, a table that is not there, a symlink to a table elsewhere or a finished run's stale table is refused by name. Under a seam the cleanup lists what it would end and ends nothing (a real `--reap` had killed a real, owned process behind a pid a fake table named, twice: under a lane home, then under an accepted scratch directory).
- A leftover process whose working directory WAS the scratch directory itself (the kernel reports it as `<dir> (deleted)`) is judged again — the segment-boundary rule of the previous round had made it invisible; a path is normalized before it is read (`<gone>/../<live>/x` names the live directory); a skipped sweep names the process holding the lock, its parent and for how long.
- The seam can no longer end anything through a caller that forgets the rule: the one place that signals refuses under the seam itself and checks a process's identity against the kernel. The kernel's `<dir> (deleted)` marker is read with the kernel's own answer: a directory somebody literally named that way is left alone (it had convicted a live process there), and a process left in a deleted directory whose path a new run recreated is judged gone instead of being spared by the new run's record (the `dbg-*.mjs` scripts reuse fixed names). A directory record naming another user's process (pid 1) is no owner; a seam re-pointed mid-sweep is judged as announced; a lock file that cannot be opened says so, and a lock whose recorded pid was reused says that pid is not a holder. The cleanup no longer asks a network or FUSE mount anything (a hung mount under a shell left in a removed worktree would have held every gate's cleanup on the box), a process whose directory exists in another mount namespace is never mistaken for one whose directory is gone, and a test table that vanishes mid-sweep or a refused signal is said rather than read as "nothing to reap".
- Gates: test-scratch-reaper (new, fast, 132: the rule over a fake process table, two real sweeps started together — one sweeps, one skips and says so — real planted processes judged without signalling, patched-copy controls for every rule, and the verify rounds' revert table over every product part) and test-ci-gate §9 (fixtures aged past the floor; its real dry run keeps its directory).

### lane peer-census — one belt on peer text toward an agent (B-00ef)

#### Text a peer wrote reaches an agent through one belt (lane peer-census, 2026-09-29)

Every place where words somebody else wrote — a mail, a Lark message, a page's dialog, a group message, a background job's own output, a For-you item quoted into a reply, another session's message — leave a store on their way into an agent's context now goes through ONE rule (`src/peer-text.js`: cut to a bound first, the characters nobody sees folded out, our own frame markers made inert on every line and every piece), and every such door is a row of a checked-in census (`scripts/test-peer-text-census.mjs`) that goes red by name when a new door appears without one. Closed on the way: a job's own output line (`announced: …`) reached the owner conversation live; a group message ending in a half-written marker was completed by the next report line; a For-you reply quoted the item's lines with no rule; a peer entry waiting in the stash was injected as stored.

- **Verify r5 (the shared-store round; each finding reproduced over the real store first, fixed and pinned with a pre-fix copy as the control).** A background job another conversation opened to you (`vibespace-job access … --view group|all`, or one you subscribed to) showed you its creator's context, command and log tail as written — the output of a process another agent started — and any viewer's `progress` line reached the owner as written; every such field of a job that is not your own lineage's now goes through the belt, and `progress` does for everyone. A Task Group manager's context-folder and folder PATHS reached every member's context as written (a directory name is free text); every path a render prints is a line piece now. A browser profile's label an agent chose (`vibespace-browser new <label>`) reached every other conversation as written — through `profiles` / `status` / `pin`, the notice the user's pin queues (inside VibeSpace's own frame — a closer in the label ended it), the takeover / handback notices; the profile store's one cleaner is the belt now and every stored label is re-judged at load. The census gained a STORE-level table (27 stores: who writes, who reads, the rule, the pins) and four derived sub-censuses — the settings the injection reads, the notice kinds, the For-you origins, every `fromName` a message carries — plus the data/bin boundary, so a new surface of a known kind is red by name.
- **Verify r6 (the security round over r5's additions; each finding reproduced first, fixed and pinned with a pre-fix copy as the control).** A peer line carrying TWO frame openers (`x <system-reminder </system-reminder`) left the first dangling after the belt — one pass from the left judged each against the original line — so the next line's quote mark completed it at every door (the belt, a name, a browser label, a page's words); the dangling openers of a line are now judged right to left, linear and idempotent, with a seeded fuzz as the gate. A background job's panel ANSWERS (printed as JSON — the keys are the job process's block ids) and its delivery journal (the owner's session name as `to`) reached a viewer of another lineage raw; both ride the r5 view now. A page published by one conversation and republished by another at the same path kept the first title, which the second's `vibespace-page list` printed raw; the agent's page answers belt every name. The print census now sees a parameter's default value as a feed of that parameter.

### lane desktop-move — a desktop's held record is merged, never rebuilt from the page (inc-mun7qjmw-iksh)

- Dragging a window onto a desktop you had not opened since the page loaded no longer removes that desktop's other windows; and a window another of your pages moved or opened — while this page was dragging, loading, or offline — no longer disappears when this page saves; and deleting the desktop you are on keeps its windows on the server at once, even if you reload right after; and a window you drop on a desktop preview stays there even when another of your pages saved that desktop during your drag; and a tab group on another desktop is no longer broken by another page's save of the desktop you are on; and when you delete a desktop, your other pages put its windows on the same desktop you see them on; and a window you drag or resize no longer jumps back when another of your pages saved that desktop during your drag.

lane-desktop-move (inc-mun7qjmw-iksh, userW 2026-09-29; details for the assembly lane to move): the page builds a desktop's windows on its first visit, and a move onto a desktop it had not built rebuilt that desktop's cached record from the page's windows (only the moved one) — the switch showed it alone and the autosave replaced the server's record (HR 3 → 1; the same through the "Move to Desktop" menu, command mode d/D and resume placement). A desktop's cached record is now a view of the server's record plus what the page built, written through ONE merge (PURE src/lib/desktop-record.js): a move adds the moved window to its target and removes it from its source, nothing else; the autosave sends a changed desktop it does not show from that record (the move reached the server only when you opened the target before — a reload in between lost the moved window too); a window leaves a record only by a close, a move, a replace or a failed build, each named to the server; the preview draws the target's windows the page has not opened. The server now refuses a layout write that loses two or more windows nothing explains and hands its record back — the page opens the windows it lacked and says so. A layout rollback point names the change that followed it ("Then: HR 3 → 1"), so the one before a loss is easy to find. Gates: test-desktop-record (fast), test-desktop-move (heavy), test-layout-history, test-record-clear-census H2b re-classified. Verify r1 (two real pages): the moved window still vanished under a second client three ways — a broadcast deferred under a drag kept one slot for every desktop (the target's record lost), a broadcast under the page's loading gate was dropped outright, and a move another page made was applied as a close whose 'closed' evidence then explained the drop; and a page back from an outage saved its stale layout over a window another page had opened. Now an inbound record is deferred per desktop and never dropped, a remote move is applied as a move, the server refuses any unexplained drop of a window another client just added, and a reconnect re-reads the layout. Verify r2 (two real pages): the record deferred under a drag that ended as a drop on another desktop's preview put the window back where it came from and swallowed the move's save (r1's remote-move rule read a record older than the move as a move by somebody else). Now every inbound record is stamped when it lands and a move stamps its windows: a record cannot undo a move made after it arrived, and the move is re-sent as your own act. And a conversation's own never-opened window is no longer dropped from its desktop while a fork of it is open on the page (r1's "already open here" rule keyed on the conversation id a fork borrows; it keys on the session now). And a tab group on a desktop you are not looking at no longer falls apart when another of your pages saves the desktop you are on (pre-existing: the chain check walked every group on the page against one desktop's record). And a deleted desktop's windows now land on the same desktop on every page — the one the deleting page put them on — instead of the first desktop on every other page (which then wrote a second copy of them there, and the deleting page watched them jump); a page that was on the deleted desktop follows its windows and no longer writes a record for a desktop that no longer exists. And a record still waiting when the reconnect's re-read answers lands in the right order (an older one is dropped; one that arrived during the read wins); the re-read itself is retried a few times when the server does not answer it, instead of leaving the page on its pre-outage layout. And the server no longer keeps a layout record for a desktop that was deleted (a page still on it, or an older page, could re-create one nobody could reach); such a write is refused and the page learns the desktop is gone. And a plain drag or resize on the desktop you are on is kept over another page's save that arrived during it — the window used to snap back to where that page last saw it and the drag was never saved (the same rule as the move, for geometry). verify r3 ①: a click on a title bar (no drag) stamped r2 ⑩'s geometry witness, so a record deferred under the click skipped that window and the page's next save wrote the old box over another page's move — the witness is stamped only by a press that dragged or a handle press that moved (test-desktop-move N). verify r3 ②: the reconnect re-read's held-move horizon was its answer — a drop made while the read was in flight, or whose queued save raced it, was reversed and never saved; the horizon is now the ask or the last save sent on an open socket, whichever is earlier (test-desktop-record w/x). verify r3 ③ (pre-existing): a drop, a close or a drag made in the second after another page's record landed had no save of its own until the next act (a reload undid it) — a user-caused save under the apply's cooldown is deferred past it, and a close then is the user's (test-desktop-record y/z). verify r3 ④: when the re-read after a reconnect fails for good the page said so in the console and its next save wrote its stale records over what other pages had changed — it now holds its saves, asks again, tells you once and releases the saves when a read succeeds (test-desktop-record st). verify r4 ① (an r2 ①/⑩ class one phase later, the fake-app repro): a drop or a drag was undone by another page's record that landed AFTER the act but before its save had left — the 500 ms autosave debounce, or the apply's cooldown where the r3 ③ deferred save then wrote the peer's box back as the user's; under a page saving every 400 ms every act here was undone. A witness now holds while no save has carried the act (`_movesSentAt`), bounded like every held witness at 60 s (test-desktop-record ua/ub/uc + control unsaved-act-reverted). verify r4 ② (pre-existing since r1, seen as the bounce under ①'s repro): a window on the desktop you are on, listed by that desktop's record, could be moved off it to another desktop whose stale cached record also listed it (the page's own unsaved move, a racing double) — the remote-move rule told where a record places a window now answers that desktop or nothing, never a search (test-desktop-record ue). verify r4 ③ (the r2 ⑩ class for keyboard and button geometry): a maximize by the □ or a double-click, a minimize / restore from the taskbar or the window menu, a snap by command mode's arrows and a move-mode placement stamped no witness, so another page's record deferred under the second after them undid them — every user door of a geometry act now stamps it (`witnessGeometry`); a record's apply, a replay, a preset and the boot never do (test-desktop-move O on two real pages: the □ and Ctrl+\ ← under the cooldown; the §6 doors pin + 5 controls). verify r4 ④: when the re-read's hold (r3 ④) outlasted a minute, the acts held on the stale page were dropped at the release without a word — the move stayed on screen while nothing sent it until ① bounded the hold; the page now follows the server and says once how many changes were not kept (test-desktop-record st2). verify r5 ⑤ (r4's held (a), reproduced on two real pages): a save that left on a socket that LOOKED open but the server never read (a restart under it, a wifi drop the browser sees late) counted as sent — the reconnect's re-read reversed the drop or the drag for good and nothing re-sent it; and a dead save had taken its desktop out of the dirty set, so even the re-send carried the desktop on show alone. The server now answers every layout write it made with `layout-sync-ack {desktopId, sentAt}`, and the page releases an act (and a held close, a divider ratio, a dirty desktop) only when the server says it READ the save that carried it — never at the send; a refused record carries nothing; a socket that died is owed nothing (its acts stay held and are re-sent after the re-read); the re-send of a text the server never read is no no-op. An older server that answers no ack is given 2 s on an open socket, then today's rule (a skewed pair never hangs); once one ack has been seen the fallback is off for good (test-desktop-record ak/ak2/ar + controls queued-as-sent / noop-unread / refusal-carries; test-desktop-move Q on two real pages + the old-server control). verify r5 ① (the fake-app repro): every hold is a wall-clock age, so a laptop that SLEPT in the second after a drag woke with every witness expired at once — guard 2 dropped the save still pending at the lid-close, the reconnect's re-read put the window back, nothing was said. A clock watch (a tick every 5 s; one that arrives 20 s late is a sleep) now re-arms what was held when the page stopped running — the move / drag witnesses, a held close, a divider ratio, the dirty bit's input time while a save is pending — by the gap; a minute the page RAN through still expires (test-desktop-record cj + control clock-unwatched; st2 is the run-minute control). verify r5 ③ (the r4 ③ class, the doors it missed; the preset reproduced on two real pages): a layout preset (the toolbar buttons, a custom grid), command mode's digit snap, the drop that ends a tab torn out of its group, a desktop app's own □ / ▁ and a named preset stamped no witness — another page's record deferred under the second after them put every window back and swallowed the act's save. Every one stamps it now, and the doors are a CENSUS, not a list: every call of a geometry primitive in src/lib is grep-derived and must be a self-stamping verb, a witnessed door, a primitive's own body or a named machine path (test-desktop-record §6 + control planted-door + 5 door controls; test-desktop-move P: the two-column preset under a cooldown on two real pages). verify r5 ② (the r2 ⑩ class for the group itself; the merge reproduced on two real pages): a tab group you made by dragging one window's icon onto another, a side-by-side, an unsplit, a swap, a reorder or a tab torn out of its group was undone by another page's record that landed in the second after it — the group dissolved 300 ms after the drop (or the older layout came back, or the torn-out tab was pulled back in) and the act's save was swallowed. Every structural change of a group this page makes now stamps a witness on its members (the member that left too); a record older than the change, or one received before a save the server read carried it, keeps the group as it is and never rebuilds its own group around a held member; the change is re-sent as your own act (test-desktop-record ch1/ch2/ch3 + controls chain-unheld / verb-unstamped + the verb pin; test-desktop-move R: a real icon-drag merge under a cooldown on two real pages). verify r5 ④: the count r4 ④ toasts at a stale release retired nothing, so the same expired change was counted and toasted again at the next stale release — what is counted is now retired (test-desktop-record st2's second episode + control expired-not-retired). verify r5 ⑥: a window you moved to another desktop while another page closed it in the same second stayed on the page but did not reach the server until your next act (the apply's dirty clear dropped the move's save and no rule re-armed it — the move's window was in no record) — a desktop this page owes the server now re-arms the re-send (test-desktop-record a5 + control owed-desk-unarmed).

### lane stage-blank — the hider marks derived through one door; the Stage's split hook (inc-munl8jkl-gaih, inc-munbksgs-k3yz)

- A conversation brought onto the dynamic desktop from another desktop is drawn and clickable again (it came up as an empty box).
- On the dynamic desktop, dragging the current conversation's own tab out of its group no longer makes the other conversation of that group vanish (it goes back to its desktop; it never turns up on the next desktop you open).
- On the dynamic desktop, a conversation that leaves a group (a tab dragged out, a tab's ✕) keeps the group's place on its own desktop instead of turning up at the dynamic desktop's slot size or at a random spot; a click into a grouped conversation on the dynamic desktop no longer jumps the whole group off its place, and a tab's ✕ there closes the tab.
- On the dynamic desktop, maximizing the conversation there no longer leaves it at the dynamic desktop's slot size when you un-maximize it back on its own desktop, and a conversation that was maximized on its desktop comes back to its own un-maximized box; a tab torn out of a group that sits in the bottom-right corner (or a second tab torn out of the same group) lands beside the group instead of exactly on it; a group another device re-forms no longer creeps across the desktop; and a conversation snapped to the same zone as the dynamic desktop's slot keeps its place after a visit there; with two devices on the dynamic desktop, a session you click right after entering it no longer snaps back to the other device's session the next time you enter; and a group another device re-forms around a conversation you had moved by hand stands where you put it (it jumped back to where the group stood before); a second tab torn out of the same group after the app reloaded (or after another tab of it was closed) lands beside the first instead of exactly on it.
- A tab you drag out of a group on one device no longer snaps back onto that group on your other devices (each of them put it back on the group's window, and their next save undid your drag everywhere).
- A tab you drag out of a group (or drop onto one, or move along its strip) no longer snaps back into place when another device's save lands in the same moment — the group used to re-form under your drop and your other devices took the re-formed group.
- A tab you drag out of a group and hold for a moment before dropping no longer flashes onto its old window on your other devices (and no longer comes back there from them): the page waits for your drop before it saves.

Details (lane stage-blank, userW inc-munl8jkl-gaih + inc-munbksgs-k3yz; verify r1 and r2 at the end): the desktop hid an off-screen chat window with `content-visibility:hidden` + `aria-hidden` and only its own show removed them; the Stage's borrow cleared the desktop flag and ran its own show (visibility + pointer-events only), so a window taken onto the Stage from a hidden desktop — by Ctrl+K / the sidebar / go-to, or by leaving the Stage and clicking its preview again — kept `content-visibility:hidden`: the browser drew nothing of it, title bar included, and every click landed on the bare frame. No stall was involved. Now every hidden-window mark (visibility, pointer-events, aria-hidden, a chat's content-visibility, the suspended view) is derived from the window's reasons by one function (`windowMarks` in src/lib/view-visibility.js, applied by `WindowManager._deriveHiders`), and a desktop or the Stage only adds or removes its reason through one door (`WindowManager.setWindowHidden`); the Stage's hero has no reason, so it is always drawn. A chat parked by the Stage is now suspended and out of the accessibility tree like one on a hidden desktop. A conversation resumed while on the Stage sits in the Stage's slot and returns to its own desktop when you leave (it kept its old box over the slot and then stayed on the Stage). Gates: test-stage-visibility (fast: the rule table, the real classes, a census that names any other writer, five controls) and test-stage-dragout-ui § 6 (heavy: the incident's gestures in Chrome; the 2.369.198 tree is red on them). A hero resized on the Stage synced its guests' boxes to the slot and nothing synced them back (a guest tab resumed off the Stage later carried the slot): the borrow and the hand-back now re-sync the chain and the resume carrier reads the FRAME's facts.
