- Under the hood: the server sends each row's closed STATE (17, one precedence in src/browser-switch.js `rowState`) and its facts; the device's own words come from the PURE src/lib/browser-switcher-model.js; the dialog is a keyed patch (a broadcast never rebuilds the button under the pointer). The profile digest carries `backends[id] = {id, major, plan, choices}`; the install verdict carries `npm` and `state.failed`; a failed switch answers `restored`, `from`, `to`. Nothing the agent's CLI reads changed.
- Gates: test-browser-switcher-model (fast, in-process · 202 ms: every state's words and control verbatim over fixture views the REAL switch module builds, the closed set on both sides, every answer worded with the rollback facts first, the hidden rows, zh + ja, wiring pins, five patched-copy controls), test-browser-switcher-ui (heavy, ~35 s: 19 views × en / zh / ja × 1280 / 360 px under DejaVu Sans, measured from rendered rects and shot, the acts, two controls), test-browser-backend ③b (the states on the real keeper, the digest's choices, the rollback on `launch_failed` and on a stale-view `backend_no_key`, the route's body, the agent's `next`), test-browser-live-ui ②b (the entry points on this build and with another browser available) + its controls now strip the own-class size rules, test-browser-share-model (the picker row), test-live-bar-layout §4b.

### "Who can use it" becomes a list of conversations and Task Groups (the owner's report: a Chinese UI, the Agent browser panel)

The row's "谁能使用" was a plain dropdown of every running conversation: no Task Group in it, and only one choice. A profile is a browser with your logins; you want to give it to a few conversations, or to everything in a Task Group, and keep it from the rest.

- **The panel row shows the list.** "Who can use it" reads "All my conversations", or one small chip per conversation and Task Group (a conversation with its agent's icon, dimmed when it is not running; a Task Group with the people icon). More than four fold into "+2 more" (two on a phone). A **Change…** button opens the dialog. If the list can no longer let anyone in (the only Task Group was deleted), an amber line says "Nobody can use it now: the Task Group it was limited to was deleted" — never "everyone".
- **The dialog.** "Who can use work?" with two answers: "All my conversations" (the default) or "Only these". Under "Only these" is the same searchable picker the channel dialogs use: Task Groups first, conversations under their Task Group, the rest under Other, recent picks on top; type to filter, ↓ and Enter or the mouse to pick, the chip's × to remove. Picking a Task Group means every conversation in it — bound to it or started in its folders — now and later. Conversations on other machines are not listed (the Agent browser runs on this machine only), said in one line. If a conversation that uses the profile right now would lose it, the dialog says how many before you save ("1 conversation using it now will lose it when you save (their pages in it close)."). Saving with "Only these" and nobody picked is refused in place.
- **Nothing is overwritten by accident.** The dialog reads the list fresh from the server (never the panel's copy) and saves the whole list with a stamp of what it read; if another window or an agent changed it meanwhile, it says so, saves nothing, and re-opens on the list as it is now.
- **Picking a profile for a conversation adds it.** Choosing a profile kept to some conversations in New Session, Session properties or a session card's menu adds that conversation to the list (the toast says so), so the panel always shows everyone who can use it. A default the conversation got on its own (a resumed conversation's own pin, a fork's copy of its parent's, a Task Group's or the instance's default) adds nothing — a fork is another conversation.
- **Leaving a Task Group takes effect at the next browser command.** A conversation that leaves the Task Group a profile is kept to is refused at its next command, and its tab in that browser closes in the same step (the refusal says so). Narrowing the list closes the tabs of every conversation it leaves out; if the Task Group list cannot be read at that moment, nobody is cut off and the command says to run it again.
- **The agent is told only about itself.** `vibespace-browser profiles` says for each profile "used by: all your conversations", "chosen conversations — yours included" (or "…through its Task Group"), "…not yours (the user can add this conversation under "Who can use it" in the Agent browser panel)", or "…unknown for yours right now"; it never sees the list or another conversation. A refused command names the button: add this conversation under "Who can use it" (Change…), or switch it to "All my conversations".
- **Upgrading keeps every conversation that could use a profile.** A one-time migration turns a profile kept to one conversation or one Task Group into a one-row list, and adds every conversation whose own pin let it in until now.
- **Verified against the list as the only admission (2026-09-28, the identity verifier — every finding reproduced on the real keeper and routes before its fix).** Three held up and were fixed: (1) a conversation that was stopped while it held a tab through its Task Group lost that tab whenever the list was edited — even a widening that kept it — because "not running" was read as "in no Task Group"; now a stopped conversation's membership is judged at its next command (a list of conversations only still takes the tab from one that is not on it). (2) `vibespace-browser backend` named any profile by name and answered with its whole record, the list included; the agent now gets the same view as everywhere else (only whether its own conversation may use it). (3) A conversation running on another machine could be written into a list by its key; it is refused like a picked one ("runs on another machine"). Refuted: the 36-cell admission table on the real routes, every pin form (a Task Group default dated after the change, a forged future-dated user pin, a pin without `by`, a fork's copy, an agent's pin) authorizing nothing, the pick adding only on the user's own acts, an unreadable Task Group list keeping every tab, the migration lossless over 38 400 random cells and idempotent, a stopped conversation staying listed across a restart, an attrited list admitting nobody, the whole-list stamp (a list moved during the picker's resolve is refused), every new route answering 401 to an agent token / a job token / no cookie with auth on, and the session list being per conversation.
- **Verified again against the tree as fixed (2026-09-28, identity round 2 — every claim reproduced on the real keeper and routes over the fake 0.38.1 before it was counted).** Two held up and were fixed: (1) **a conversation on another machine was admitted like a local one** — an ssh host's or a paired device's agent could `vibespace-browser use work`, take a lease and make this machine start work's Chrome for a loopback CDP url the other machine can never reach; and the user's pin / attach for such a conversation (Session properties, the New Session pick, `POST /api/browser/pin` / `/attach`) wrote its key into "Who can use it" — the very key the dialog's save refuses and the picker never offers. Now ONE refusal, `remote_session`, at the ONE admission (the keeper's `attach`) and at the ONE add (`addConversation`; ws-create's explicit pick says `remote` too): no lease, no launch, nothing listed; an unpin still works. (2) **The agent's `backend` verb and its `profiles` digest still named other conversations** — the `backend` answer of a profile the asker may NOT use carried every lease row whole (another conversation's browser key + webui session id; round 1 had stripped the record only), the digest carried every lease, every managed ephemeral browser (key, session id, pid) and every blocked claim (key, session id), and the admitted agent's `use` / `resolve` answers carried the record with its list and `createdBy`. Now the whole digest goes through ONE PURE view (`agentDigestView`): every record as the agent's view, another conversation's lease / grant reduced to `{profileId, mediated, other}` (the CLI's per-profile count keeps working), only the asker's own ephemeral browsers (a count of the others), a claim without its key — `drivers` alone still names who drives, by key (owner ruling A (2)'s one deliberate exception). Judged and left (LOW): the user's attach that ADDS a conversation and then fails to start the browser leaves it added (its intent, retried by the next attempt); the user's pick on a record of an unreadable owner shape replaces that shape with a one-row list (fail-closed either way); the size sweep trims an open session's oldest frames only after every closed session is bare (round 1's note); every other attack held — the hostile stored shapes, the dialog's handback (cookie only, the dialog's profile only, `not_taken` when nobody drives, a handback through a joined lease releases the browser as the sibling rule says), a Task-Group change while the conversation is stopped (kept undecided, judged at its resume), the stale-base race, the agent token on the human-only routes, the migration run twice / half-run / over junk rows, the sessions' attribution across two conversations and a helper on one profile. Pins: test-browser-share-model (the remote legs, the agent-view legs, controls (i) a keeper without the fence, (j) an add ignoring remote, (k) routes answering the raw rows, (k′) a PURE view keeping rows whole; control (h) re-based on a keeper that knows no remote key so the route's own check is measured alone).
- **Verified a third time (2026-09-28, identity round 3 — THE CENSUS ROUND: twice the fix was one door while its siblings stayed open, so this round ships a census gate and a server belt, not another example).** One more held up and was fixed, one smaller one too: (1) **an agent the list keeps OUT could switch a kept profile's backend directly** — `vibespace-browser backend cloak` on a profile "Who can use it" keeps to other conversations stopped its browser and relaunched it under the other backend (a fingerprint seed minted, "sites may ask you to log in again") whenever nobody held a lease and nobody drove, because the switch's "not the owner ⇒ a proposal" rule still read the retired single-owner shape (`owner.kind === 'session'`) and a list is never that shape; the pre-list record still made it a proposal. Now the keeper asks THE ONE admission (`mayAttach` over the conversation's live Task Groups) and hands the PURE verdict `admitted`: not admitted — a remote session too — ⇒ a proposal to the user, never a direct switch; not judged ⇒ a proposal (fail closed). (2) **The agent's `profiles` digest still carried every browser RECORD whole** (`browsers`: every record's pid, its daemon namespace — a conversation's `vs-bk-…` bs-session id —, socket dir, directory, launch env and `startedBy: "attach bk-…"`, another conversation's ephemeral records included); now a named profile's record is its state facts only and another's ephemeral record is absent (its reduced lease row carries no record id either). Also: a session on another machine can no longer `new` / `new --adopt` a profile here (refused `remote_session` like `use` — it could never use it); an agent's `blocked` claim naming a profile the list keeps from it is refused `not_owner` (the user's live view of a kept profile never showed a stranger's claim with a one-click switch beside it; a `--remember` hint is not written either); and the New Session dialog no longer offers a browser profile once a host is picked (round 2's finding 6). **The SERVER BELT:** every `/api/agent/browser/*` answer — a success, a refusal, a route written raw tomorrow — passes the PURE `agentAnswerView` last, on the one wrapper registered before every agent route: another conversation's browser key in any string is masked `bk-********`, its webui / conversation id `[another conversation]`, its browser pid nulled; what the asker itself sent stays as it wrote it; `$.drivers` is the one exception (owner ruling A (2)) and it is spelled once (`BELT_EXCEPTIONS`); a body the belt cannot judge is answered `belt_failed`, never raw. **The CENSUS (test-browser-identity-census, fast, 57):** every lease / pin / owner-list write in the keeper's text is inside a known function with the fence before the write (a new site is RED by name); every caller of a fenced primitive across the routes / ws-create / trace routes / stream bridge / bindings is known, the raw doors are migrations-only and read-only; the belt precedes every agent route, every route answers through `res.json`, names its view and has a walk row, every CLI call names a walked route; the RUNTIME WALK over the real keeper + routes + mediator (A admitted with a helper, an ephemeral, a mediated grant, a drive claim and two takeovers; B not; R on another machine) walks every answer for B and R and the shipped CLI's stdout — no string equals A's key / webui id / conversation id / pids / bs-session ids / helper key except `$.drivers.<profile>.browserKey`, present and alone; eleven patched-copy controls (a raw `joinRaw` door, an `attach` without its fence, a `setPin` writing the owner, an unknown `k.attach(` caller, a raw route before the belt, `/profiles` raw, a `res.send` route, the routes WITHOUT the belt + a raw route ⇒ 49 hits, the REAL belt over the same raw route ⇒ masked, a belt with a second exception, the pre-fix switch rule). Judged and left (LOW): a `profile_locked` refusal names the pid of the Chrome holding a directory the asker IS admitted to (the lock forensics' designed sentence — "VibeSpace never ends a browser it did not start"); the switch proposal's `reason` names other lease holders by key before the belt masks them (masked on the wire); the ssh back-tunnel path reaches the same routes the walk drives (R's token is that path — not booted).
- Under the hood: `owner` is `{kind:'instance'}` or `{kind:'only', who:[conversations by browser key, Task Groups by id]}`, read by ONE function (`whoMayUse`); the admission takes the conversation's Task Groups as they are at every command and no pin; `GET /api/browser/profiles/:id/use` + `PATCH …{use, base}` (409 when the list moved); the migration `2026-09-browser-profiles-who-list`. The picker files are a byte-for-byte copy of lane-channel-render's; its suite is excluded here until that lane's merge brings its row.
- Gates: test-browser-share-model (in-process: the 36-cell admission table, every stored shape, the write's refusals, the real keeper and routes over the fake 0.38.1, five patched-copy controls), test-migrations (the fold, with the control), test-browser-pin, test-browser-who-ui (heavy: 40 sessions, zh keyboard and mouse picks, one PATCH with its stamp, a second tab keeping its unchanged chip, the 409 re-open, the phone at 360 px), test-browser-share (heavy, the real 0.38.1 + Chrome: a Task Group's conversation opens the profile, unbinding closes its tab).

### Naive-user round (2026-09-28) — what a person reading these surfaces in zh / ja / en at 1280 and 360 px ran into

- **"Who can use it": the two warning lines were invisible.** The "will lose it" sentence and the empty-list refusal were written into the alert icon's box (a zero-height box), so each line was 0 px tall, the two overlapped, and on a phone the sentence ran off the screen, cut mid-word. They now have their own text, wrap inside the dialog, and sit right above Cancel / Save instead of at the end of the scrolling list — on a phone they used to be below the fold, exactly when Save refused. A note line is now always re-worded through its own text (`noteText()`), and a census fails any code that reaches into a note's first span.
- **The key card no longer says something false.** With no key configured anywhere, the switch dialog's CloakBrowser card said "The saved key can't be used: the cluster provides no default for this integration". Nothing was ever saved; the card now says one sentence ("CloakBrowser needs a license key from its maker.") and explains a key only when one EXISTS and can't be used (it can't be read, the chosen preset is gone, …). The key card's help no longer promises "Empty means the free tier" — an empty key is no key (every switch and start refuse it), so the help now says a key is needed (yours, or one this VibeSpace provides), and the card's Test says so instead of passing.
- **The browser-limit popover had no background** (its colour named a token no theme defines): its rows were drawn over the bar and the banner showing through. It is painted with the dialog colour now; the replay window's panes lost the same dead colour. A new census fails any popover or menu whose background is a colour nothing defines, keeps the browser dialogs free of them, and holds the product-wide count from growing.
- **"You're driving this browser by hand" now has the button that ends it.** The card said to hand the browser back and that it would update by itself, but the hand-back button was behind the dialog. The card's button now does it — "Hand it back to your agent" — and the dialog stays open and turns into the switch once it's done.
- **The blocked note is no longer a dead end.** Where no other browser is offered, it now says "… Take over to get past the check yourself.", and the agent's evidence is behind **Details** on the note itself (it was only in the dialog nobody could open). Its buttons are the house text buttons.
- **Session properties shows the whole browser line** (it wraps between its parts; the browser's name never breaks) — the words about who can use the profile and how many use it now were cut off with no way to read them. The Agent browser panel's head line ("2 profiles · 0 B on disk · …") wraps on a phone instead of ending in "…".
- **A stopped browser's live view on a phone** gives its Sessions list the whole width with the status above it (it had 198 of 360 px, every row cut, the status squeezed into six lines). **The replay on a phone** keeps the chosen session's row in view of its list.
- **Words.** zh says 配置 for a browser profile everywhere (档案 is gone); ja says ブラウザ everywhere and スクリーンショット instead of フレーム; the replay's buttons and counter say 上一步 / 下一步 / 第 1 / 6 步 like their tooltips; the folded browser name in the live bar's ⋯ reads "Your agent's browser: Chromium" (or "Switch browser (now Chromium)…"), as does the profile picker's row; a deleted Task Group's chip explains itself instead of repeating its name; the Agent browser panel's row states ("1 conversation uses it", "last used 3 h ago") are in the device's language (the server's English stays the agent's and the CLI's).
- **Chat cards.** A session's end card says why it ended ("· the browser was switched", "· the conversation stopped", …), and a session in which the agent did nothing offers no Replay.
- **Manage agents** no longer lists CloakBrowser on a build that doesn't have it, and a plain fact there is not drawn in red.
- Gates: test-browser-switcher-model (the needs-key and driven-card tables, controls (f) the pre-fix key filter and (g) the pre-fix driven card), test-browser-share-model (the note-line census + control), test-live-bar-layout §4c (the dead-token census + two controls), test-browser-sessions (end reasons, no Replay on 0 actions), test-browser-housekeeping (the panel's row words from structure), test-browser-backend (an empty key's Test fails by name); heavy: test-browser-who-ui ⑨ (both notes on a 360 px phone in zh / ja / en + an in-page control), test-browser-switcher-ui (the hand-back from the dialog, the no-preset card), test-browser-replay-ui ⑦b / ⑦c (+ controls), test-browser-live-ui ②b (the banner, the popover's colour), test-browser-identity (the whole Session properties line).
- Not changed, and why: the picker's section word 「セッション」 is the shared principal picker's (another lane's file, byte-identical); "(PSS)" on the panel's memory reading is the keeper lane's deliberate label; the CloakBrowser Settings rows' wording (cloakserve / loopback / docker) belongs to the cloakserve rung, which this build does not wire.

### Verifier round (regression + perf, 2026-09-28) — three findings, each reproduced, fixed and pinned with a control

- **A replay of a long session silently showed its last 1 000 actions** under a session row that said 5 000: the answer to `GET /api/browser/sessions?session=` carries the newest 1 000 and now NAMES the whole (`entriesTotal`); the replay window's head says "Actions (last 1 000 of 5 000)" with a tooltip saying the earlier ones are on disk (zh 操作（最近 1000 步，共 5000 步）, ja 操作（最新 1000 件／全 5000 件）). Measured before the fix: a 5 000-action session opened in 93 ms with 1 000 rows and no word about the other 4 000. Pinned in test-browser-sessions ⑤ (1 200 actions ⇒ 1 000 + `entriesTotal` 1 200) and test-browser-replay-ui ③c.
- **The replay's action rows were rebuilt whole on every reload** (each `browser-trace-appended` of the same conversation while its agent kept working, every sweep): 1 000 rows detached and re-made, a click under the pointer lost (the picker's documented Chrome behaviour). The rows are keyed by trace id now, patched in place, moved only when they moved; test-browser-replay-ui ③c fires a trace broadcast and asserts the first and last row keep their nodes.
- **One "Who can use it" Save over 50 leases was 50 registry writes and 50 whole-digest broadcasts** (+ 50 active-sessions re-publishes to every client): `detach()` commits, and the narrowing detaches one lease at a time — measured 8.7 ms in-process on tmpfs, and each write is a sync `writeJsonAtomic` on whatever disk data/ sits on. `updateProfile` now runs inside `batched()`: one write, one broadcast per Save (1.6 ms for 50 leases, 6 ms for 200). Pinned in test-browser-share-model (w) with an unbatched keeper copy as its control (50 / 50).
- **The worded-icon-box census (test-live-bar-layout §4b) read five worded live-bar buttons as `none`** — Tabs / Console / Actions, the fit chip and the browser-name button write their words 230–500 lines below their `createElement`, past the 40-line window the census copied from test-ax-paint — so they were never judged (they are reached by `.browser-live-bar > .file-tool-btn { width: auto }` today; the census could not have said so). The classification now reads a name's own span (its birth to the next line that gives the same name another element): 43 worded sites, still 0 flagged; a control strips the bar rule's `width: auto` from an in-memory copy of style.css and requires the five flagged BY NAME (red on the pre-fix census: 0 of 5). Also verified in a real Chrome: every (0,2,0) rule the lane added (`.file-tool-btn.browser-live-cap-stop / -cap-default / -mode-btn / -handback`) computes `width: auto` over viewers.css's 24 px box, in isolation and inside its bar, en and zh; a bare worded `file-tool-btn` (the control) stays 24 px.

### Gates (live input)

- NEW fast suite `test-live-input` (in-process · 8.4 s): the cutting rules against the browser's measured behaviour (3 000 random texts), the Mac key table, the chip words (en + zh + ja), the real live-view bridge over a stand-in stream server (order, one receipt, the credit pacing, copy out to the driver only and only on the driver's own key or click, "Fit here"), one recording start — each rule with a patched copy that goes red.
- NEW heavy suite `test-browser-live-input` (47–58 s): the real agent-browser 0.38.1 and its Chromium, driven like a person from a page on plain http — a click into the picture, Ctrl+V and ⌘V, a real input-method composition, a double click, a drag, copy and cut into the viewer's clipboard — on a named profile (the owner's case), a conversation's own browser and a shared profile; a Mac viewer; the chip in English and Chinese; and a control build where the old behaviour fails every one of those legs.
- The heavy suite also drives a hostile page (synthetic copies on a timer) against a viewer on plain http and one on a secure address: the clipboard stays untouched with nothing pressed and after a click; the control tree without the door writes the page's text after one click.
- `test-live-input` also checks the chip words as a Chinese and a Japanese reader sees them (no space after 。, 照着 / 那个窗口 / そのウィンドウ, no raw error), and the live-view bridge: a failed resize's late echo is never read as the agent's, a shared browser's held size re-fits at the handback, a takeover fits at once and nothing is resized under a held button — each with a patched copy that goes red. The heavy suite drives a shared browser on the real fence: the plain chip while you drive, the page fitted again at the handback.

### Integration — two lanes and the mirror's channel-jump wait on one tree

- **A pin no longer lets a conversation into a profile — the late browser key follows the list.** 2.369.195's late browser key (a session from before per-session browsers gets one on its first browser command) dated the default pin at the session's START, so a pin could not outrank a "who can use it" narrowing made later. With "who can use it" a list, the list is the only thing that lets a conversation in and a pin is only the conversation's preferred profile, so that date rule (`latePinAt`, and the checks that pinned "a pin dated 0 lets nobody in") is removed. A late key still restores the profile its session started with (the start-time witness — a default set later never reaches it), and it never adds that conversation to any profile's list: a new check on the real keeper, with a patched copy that does add it as its control. The identity census now also counts `restorePin` (it may write a pin, never an owner or a lease) and the late key's two calls.
- **The upgrade's list migration keeps 2.369.195's answer.** The one-time move to "who can use it" as a list adds every conversation whose own pin let it into a profile until now; the lane was written against 2.369.194, where an undated pin on a profile with no narrowing date counted. 2.369.195 had already made such a pin (the late browser key's landing on the current default) let nobody in, so the migration now skips it too: nothing 2.369.195 refused is opened by the upgrade (test-migrations (e), with a copy that folds it as the control).
- **The live view's bar carries both lanes' parts:** the copy chip ("Copied in the page — click to copy") and the fit chip fold at the address's priority, after the viewers count and the recording chip; the browser's name is a switch button when another browser is possible and a plain label ("Your agent's browser: …" in the ⋯ menu) when not. The attach line in the server log is written only when a conversation takes or re-takes a browser, and a conversation whose tab was closed when the user took the profile from it gets a new tab bound before its next command.
- **"Who can use it" uses the principal picker 2.369.195 shipped.** The dialog's branch carried byte-identical copies of the picker, its styles and its translations; each is kept once (the two words both branches translated differently keep 2.369.195's), and test-principal-picker runs in the fast tier. Picking a running conversation that has no browser key yet asks the late-key engine with its documented arguments.
- **Five heavy reds on the merged tree, each root-caused (each red on both attempts, green after its fix; none a flake).** test-integrations-ui still expected the CloakBrowser card's format check to pass with no key ("empty = the free tier") — the dialog lane made that a failed check that says why, so the leg now checks the failure's words and then saves a well-formed key the user's way and sees it pass. test-browser-who-ui pinned the dialog branch's own zh word for "+2 more" while the dictionary keeps 2.369.195's (one key, one word) — the leg now reads the word from the dictionary. The gate now runs with `claude` hidden and a scratch HOME (no vendor call), which showed three suites had silently needed the machine's own setup, red on 2.369.195 too under the same run: test-cwd-recreate and test-resume-breaker spawned the real `claude` (now a stub that keeps the one CLI behaviour they read — a resume of a conversation with no transcript says "No conversation found" and exits), and test-browser-resources' first two legs read the invoking user's agent-browser config (now a fixture user HOME of the same shape: the no-sandbox argument this machine needs, `headed: true` for the generated config to override).
- **The mirror's channel-jump wait:** test-channel-jump now waits for the turn's end state (three rows AND the drafted mark) instead of the intermediate row count — the 2.369.195 Actions mirror read the rows between the third read and the draft on the slower runner, red twice.

## 2.369.195 — right-click a Word file (or press the Word viewer's "Open in LibreOffice") and it opens in LibreOffice on the machine that holds it; an agent can take back or replace a draft it proposed, and you choose on the Approve button whether it hears now or with your next message; a channel conversation reads like an IM, the chat shows which mail or Lark chat an agent read or drafted, and what is waiting for an agent's next turn is shown above its composer; a Gmail account can reuse a storage mount's OAuth client; a viewer closed from its side-by-side tab stays closed; a session from before the browser feature can use the browser without a restart

### Open with LibreOffice (the owner's ruling 2026-09-27, option ②; docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md §7.9)

- **Right-click a Word file (or a spreadsheet, or a presentation) in the file explorer → "Open with LibreOffice".** The document opens in LibreOffice Writer (Calc, Impress by its type) running as a VibeSpace desktop app — the xpra window, LibreOffice's own title on it — on the machine that HOLDS the file: a file on a paired machine opens there, never copied. You edit it there; Save writes it back in place. Measured on this box: the click to a ready window in 1.4 s. The in-browser viewer stays read-only; its own "Open in LibreOffice" button comes with the viewer's next release and uses the same door.
- **A machine without LibreOffice says so, in one sentence where you clicked:** "LibreOffice Writer is not installed on this machine" and "Install LibreOffice on this machine…" — the same install dialog as xpra's: every command shown first (the module's package + the Carlito / Caladea fonts a Word document is laid out with), nothing runs until you press Install, no password prompt (passwordless sudo, else the commands to copy), an install already running there is followed, never started twice. The Desktop apps catalog lists LibreOffice Writer / Calc / Impress too; one that is not installed carries "Install…" beside it.
- **When LibreOffice closes after the document changed, every open editor of that file knows at once** (a `file-changed` signal): the code editor reloads a clean copy immediately (or shows its "changed on disk" chip when you have edits) instead of waiting for its 15-second check.
- **Each LibreOffice window is its own LibreOffice** (its own profile, removed when you end it): a second document never lands inside the first one's window. Stopping LibreOffice from VibeSpace no longer leaves the document "in use" — the lock file LibreOffice leaves behind is removed, but only when it names that very session (a lock of your own LibreOffice elsewhere is kept).
- **The Word viewer has an "Open in LibreOffice" button** (its toolbar's right end, and the file explorer's preview of a .docx): the same door as the explorer row — the document opens in LibreOffice Writer on the machine that holds it (a remote file on its own machine). On a machine without LibreOffice the button is not greyed out: pressing it shows, right under it, the same sentence as the explorer ("LibreOffice Writer is not installed on this machine") and "Install LibreOffice on this machine…". A narrow window keeps the button's icon and drops its words.
- **A click on an app in the Desktop apps dialog is no longer lost** when the dialog refreshes itself: while any app ran, the list was rebuilt every 5 seconds and a click that straddled the rebuild did nothing (about one click in fifty). Only the Running list refreshes now, and only when it changed.
- Refusals by name, never silent: the file on another machine than the one chosen, a path that is not a real path on its machine, a file LibreOffice does not open, a machine that is not answering, an agent on a paired machine too old to know LibreOffice ("reconnect to upgrade"), a file that is gone.
- Under the hood: PURE `src/office-open.js` (the verdict, the argv with the path last, the lock witness, the install set); SHARED `desktop-display.officeFacts` (which binary, which modules — a module is installed when its library is there); the install machinery generalised (`installPackage`; `installXpra` is `installPackage('xpra')`, its behaviour unchanged); `GET /api/desktop/open-with`, `POST /api/desktop/install {what}`, the `file-changed` broadcast. Gates: test-office-open (fast, PURE, a patched-copy control per rule; §9 now pins the Word viewer as the door's second caller — its app named by the verdict, never a hard-coded exec — beside two patched copies it refuses), test-office-desktop (heavy: real xpra + LibreOffice Writer + chrome), test-docx-viewer ⑫ (heavy: the button → the door → the launch route, spied, then the same button on a machine without Writer shows the sentence + the offer — both machines constructed with a scratch LibreOffice, so the leg runs on any box), test-docx-viewer-model ⑩/⑫ (the toolbar item and its wiring).

### Windows: a closed window stays closed (inc-mukeyzpt-lpou)

- **A viewer closed with its tab's ✕ stays closed.** The owner: "刚才用ctrl+点击，并排模式打开了个文件查看，切换桌面-回到桌面-关闭这个并排的文件查看器-重新切换桌面-回到桌面-刚才关掉的查看器变成了独立窗口" — Ctrl+click on a file path in a chat that was side by side opened the file beside it; after switching to the other desktop and back, closing the viewer with the ✕ on its tab, and switching away and back once more, the viewer was back as a free-standing window. The ✕ on a tab skipped a step every other way of closing a window takes: the desktop kept its own copy of the window list from the earlier switch, and the next return re-opened the window from it (with its old id). Closing a window now clears it from every place that can bring it back, whichever ✕, menu or key closes it; the tab's ✕ is now the same close as the title bar's.
- **Two other clients cannot bring it back either.** If another open VibeSpace (a second browser, the phone) sends its layout within the half second before this one's close is saved, the closed window is no longer re-created — the close wins and is sent once; the side-by-side group keeps its layout instead of falling back to tabs. And a client that was showing another desktop while the window was closed drops its hidden copy as soon as the new layout arrives, instead of showing it again on its next visit and writing it back to everyone.
- Gates: test-split-close-resurrect (new, heavy: the owner's sequence twice with the recorded timings, the echo and the second client, each with a control that brings the incident back), test-chain-layout ⑭, test-window-binding-model ⑥ (every place a window's life ends runs the one clean-up — a census with a control), test-desktop-apps (the tab ✕ close pin).

### Channels: "From storage" in the account dialog's OAuth client select (design-integrations-per-account §2.7)

- **Connecting a Gmail account can now reuse the OAuth client of a storage mount — no secret to copy by hand.** The owner: "帮我把 mounts 里（某个存储挂载）那个 gmail 在 channels 里也配置一份吧，至少 oauth 信息转移进去，我可以 reauthorize 把 compose 加进去。我没办法在界面里看到 oauth client 和 secret". A Gmail or Google Drive storage mount that holds its own Google client (the id + secret typed once for it) now shows up in the `OAuth client` list of **Connect an account** and **Re-authorize** as `From storage: mail archive (custom client 1234…, you@example.com)`. Pick it and sign in: the server copies the client onto the account itself, the account becomes an ordinary "Custom client", and from there Re-authorize works as for any account (so signing in again adds the compose permission).
- **The secret never passes through the page.** The list shows only the mount's name, its mailbox and the first characters of the client id. When you choose it, the server reads the secret with the storage key, stores it again under the channels key (a new copy, not the mount's) and starts the sign-in; no answer, broadcast or log line carries it, and the copy is recorded in the channels audit log by mount. A Lark account is offered none (no storage mount holds a Lark app).
- **Refusals say what happened**: the mount is gone, holds no client of its own (a preset or an id without a secret), holds another provider's client, or its secret cannot be decrypted. An agent's token can neither list these clients nor use one (403).
- API: `GET /api/channels/oauth/mount-clients?kind=gmail`; `fromMount: <mountId>` on `POST /api/channels/oauth/start`, `…/adapters/:kind/connect` and `…/adapters/:id/reauthorize` (docs/kb-api.md).
- Gates: test-channels-engine ⑮ (fast: a real storage manager + the real engine + the routes — the consent under the mount's client id, the secret re-sealed under the channels key and nowhere on disk or in a body, the refusals, the agent 403; controls: a copy that skips the seal, a copy that echoes the client, a route copy without the agent refusal, a mounts copy that opens the secret before judging the vendor, an engine copy whose Connect skips the one-client rule), test-oauth-field-parity §9 (the option on both dialogs, sent as `fromMount` alone; 7 controls), test-integrations-ui ⑩ (r) (chrome: pick "From storage: mail archive …", the consent URL's client_id is the mount's, Connect makes a Custom-client account, its Re-authorize offers the option too).
- **Verify r1 (the adversarial round: 83 probes against a real storage manager, the real engine and the routes; no leak).** Every response body, broadcast frame, engine log line, the audit log and every file under the scratch data directory were censused for a marked fake secret across the happy path, a refused token exchange, a cancelled sign-in, an undecryptable mount, the ambiguous bodies and every 404/409 refusal: it appeared nowhere, and the mount's own ciphertext only in mounts.json. The identity door held (a re-authorize whose consent names another user leaves the account on its copied client) and so did the three races: the mount's secret rotated between the sign-in and the paste-back — the exchange uses the copy taken at start; the mount removed before Connect — the sign-in's copy lands and the mount is not read again; two sign-ins on one mount — two independent ciphertexts. Two fixes. (1) A `fromMount` naming another provider's mount had that mount's secret decrypted BEFORE the provider was compared — nothing left the server, but a OneDrive mount whose secret cannot be opened answered `mount-secret-undecryptable` (the key state of a mount the account may not even borrow) instead of `mount-client-vendor`; the provider now rides down to the storage module, which refuses before it opens anything (⑬ counts the decrypts: zero across the whole refusal table; a storage copy with the two lines swapped is the control). (2) Connect's own body skipped the one-client rule — `{flowId, fromMount, credentialKey}` was accepted with the stale field ignored, while start and re-authorize refuse the same pair as `ambiguous-client`; one rule now guards every verb that reads `fromMount` (⑬; an engine copy with the old line is the control). Words: the owner-only Edit dialog prefills the copied secret exactly as it does for any custom client, and as the storage mount's own Edit does (`GET …/config`, decision D3) — "never passes through the page" describes the sign-in, and the design says so now. Noted, not changed: on an instance with sign-in off a local process that omits its agent token cannot be told from the owner (the channels routes' standing doctrine); the account card masks a custom secret to its last four characters (the registry's masking rule, the same for a typed one).
- **Verify r2 (a fresh adversary, 102 probes: a decrypt spy per request over a 32-body table, the mounts store under a concurrent edit / removal / key rotation, the copied credential's whole lifecycle, hostile names, words).** Held: an edit in flight is read as the OLD pair, never a torn one (the record is patched in one synchronous step after its unmount); a key file swapped under a live process changes nothing until a restart, and after one every old ciphertext answers `mount-secret-undecryptable` by name — never a wrong client, a flipped byte too (AES-GCM); the copied secret is GONE from the record once a re-authorize under a preset or a typed client lands, Duplicate re-seals it (D4, no token), Disconnect keeps it like any custom client, Remove deletes it; nothing about it rides a frame, the agent manuals or the export bundle; a hostile name / mailbox / client id is text on the list (the shared dialog draws labels with textContent). Two MEDIUMs, fixed. (1) The ORDER, generally: a body refused on its options (`unknown-option` / `bad-request`), on a mount whose stored client id the Gmail row's rule refuses (the storage side never validated it), or — at Connect — on ANOTHER mount whose id is not the sign-in's client, had that mount's secret decrypted first; an undecryptable other mount at Connect answered `mount-secret-undecryptable` (its key state) where the truthful answer is `flow-client-mismatch`. Fix: the mounts module gained the KEY-LESS half, `oauthClientIdOf` (gone / no client / another vendor / the id, nothing decrypted; `oauthClientOf` is it plus the secret), the wiring hands it to the engine as `head`, and the engine judges every key-free fact on it — the options first, then the id rule, then (at Connect) the id comparison — before `of` opens anything (⑬ counts zero decrypts across the table; three engine copies are the controls: the head skipped, the id rule skipped, Connect through the decrypting read). (2) A Connect refused for a bad option CONSUMED the finished sign-in (the flow was taken before the options were judged; the next Connect answered `no-flow` and the consent had to be run again) — the options are judged first, the take is last (⑬: the flow survives every refused Connect; a copy that takes first is the control). LOWs, fixed: a `fromMount` that is present but not a mount id (a number, an object, an array, the empty string) was dropped and the consent began under the DEFAULT client — `400 bad-request` by name now (`null` = absent); the owner-only `GET …/config` (the plaintext Edit prefill) accepted a self-identifying agent bearer on a sign-in-off instance while the mount routes refuse it — `403 agent-forbidden` there too; a mount name with a newline forged a second journal line and a hand-edited 2 000-char name rode the list and a refusal whole — names are bounded once in the mounts module (`lentName`: control characters out, 60) and again on the engine's list; `no-mounts` now says what to do next, and `agent-forbidden` where. Noted, not changed: a Gmail storage mount's Edit takes no `clientSecret` (its custom client is set by its guided sign-in — the storage side's own rule, silent).
- **Verify r3 (a third adversary, where r1/r2 did not go: the pending flow's PLAINTEXT LIFETIME, re-authorize's own refusal table, list freshness, key rotation at the route, the audit line; 44 probes + a gc probe).** ONE MEDIUM, fixed — one layer below the lane: the shared consent machine (src/oauth-loopback.js) never forgot a flow. `take()` has no caller (the engine reads results through `onDone`), `cancel()` and the timeout left the record in the machine's map, and the record holds the `exchange` closure the adapter handed in — for Gmail the PLAINTEXT client secret (since this release the storage mount's borrowed one). So a cancelled, timed-out or landed sign-in kept the secret in memory for the process lifetime (a gc probe: 42 of 43 closures retained), the map grew one record per begin with no bound, and nothing capped running sign-ins either (40 loopback listeners at once from one loop). Fix, in the machine (Lark's fixed mode gets it too): the closure is dropped at the flow's END (cancel / timeout / superseded, or when the exchange returns — an exchange in flight keeps it and consults `cancelled()` itself), a code landing on an ended flow is reported by name and never exchanged, ended flows retire from the map 30 min after their end (the dialog's polling still reads them meanwhile), and at most 32 sign-ins run at once — the 33rd supersedes the oldest by name. Gates: test-oauth-loopback ⑦ (the closure of an ended flow collectable with gc forced, the running one's not; retirement; a paste-back onto a cancelled flow with zero exchanges; the cap) with a patched copy without the release lines as the control (it keeps every closure); test-channels-engine ⑮ (33 pending `fromMount` sign-ins ⇒ the first superseded, 32 running). LOW, fixed: the answers said `credentialKey: custom` and nothing more, so a mount whose client was edited between the list and the pick signed in under its CURRENT client with nobody told — the rule, now stated and pinned: the choice is BY MOUNT, the copy is the mount's client when the sign-in starts, Connect naming the same mount lands that copy, and every borrowing verb's answer carries `fromMount {mountId, name, clientIdPrefix}` beside the audit line's prefix (⑬ + a control copy without the field). Held: nothing about a pending sign-in on disk before Connect or mid-exchange; the start answer's field census; re-authorize's nine refusals key-free by census (a disabled account refused stays disabled); a paste-back naming another account's URL refused on both routes, the code never exchanged; `.channels-key` rotated ⇒ the card says undecryptable and a same-mount Re-authorize re-copies cleanly under the new key; `.mounts-key` rotated ⇒ `409 mount-secret-undecryptable` on the wire, a re-entered secret opens; one audit line per copy, none per refusal, eight bounded fields. LOWs, not changed: a vendor error that echoes `client_secret` would be worded verbatim into the status and the log (Google does not echo it); `by:'user'` cannot name a second allowed email's cookie (the cookie model issues anonymous tokens — the routes' standing spelling); the pre-r4 wizard path persists the sealed copy before its consent lands, as for every typed custom client. This round is not "only LOWs": the door is verified again.
- **Verify r4 (a fresh adversary that broke r3's own change: the fixed-mode twin, the cap as a weapon, the drop itself, retirement vs readers, memory after r3, who reads `fromMount`, the storage side; 60 probes + a heap probe whose secret is minted by a child process and searched by shape).** Four fixes. (1) r3 dropped the exchange closure at a sign-in's end and kept the completion callback — both are born in one scope, and a closure holds its whole scope: a heap snapshot of the real Gmail adapter after a cancel still held the borrowed secret (30 min, until retirement). Both go now; the gate drives the REAL Gmail and Lark adapters under a heap-snapshot search (present while running, gone after a cancel, still present over the old shape). (2) A vendor error that echoes the client secret we sent was worded verbatim into the account's "Last connect failed" line — adapters.json in the clear and the digest broadcast to every client — and the For-you item; Google and Lark do not echo today, a gateway could. The adapters now withhold, by exact value, every secret the request carried (client secret, refresh token, bearer) before the error exists; the vendor's other words stay. (3) The sign-in machine's own ends — the 10-minute timeout and the 33-open-sign-ins cap — used to end an account's re-authorize silently (the dialog waited its whole 10 min; the cap also borrowed the word for "a newer sign-in of this account stands" and was swallowed mid-exchange). They are said now: the card and the Re-authorize dialog read "The consent flow ended: …", the Connect dialog's polling the same sentence, Connect answers "the sign-in ended before it finished". (4) A sign-in cancelled while its port was still being bound kept the listener for the process lifetime — for Lark the registered port, every later Lark sign-in falling to paste-back until a restart; not reachable through the routes today (reproduced through the engine in one tick), closed at the bind. Also: an agent's token is refused on every verb that begins or completes a sign-in whatever the body names (it was refused only when it named a storage mount; since r3 thirty-three begins could end the owner's sign-in). Held: `fromMount` in an answer reaches only its caller (no frame, digest, agent surface or file but the audit line); 29 verbs including every refusal leave the storage records byte-identical; a mount removed and its key rotated after the borrow leaves the account working under its own copy; one exchange for a landing repeated three times; an exchange in flight at a timeout / disconnect / cap eviction stores nothing. Gates: test-oauth-loopback ⑧ (75), test-channels-engine ⑮ (12–14) (334), test-channels-gmail-shape ⑧ (169), test-channels-lark-shape ⑨ (138), test-channels-accounts-model.
- **Verify r5 (a fifth adversary over rounds 1–4: the heap at every stage, the scrub by construction, every end of a sign-in, the route census, the storage side once more, the words; 40 probes in six scripts under /tmp/vibespace-lanes/cfm-verify/r5/ + a retainer walk over the heap).** No MEDIUM. Held: after r4 the borrowed secret and the refresh token are in the heap only while a sign-in runs or an exchange is in flight — gone once the exchange returned, after Connect, after a refresh, after a refresh the vendor refused with an echo, after a cancelled re-borrow, a disconnect, a remove, and idle (the real engine + machine + Gmail adapter over a vendor that retains nothing; the same over Node 24's real fetch through a local stub — nothing lingers in the fetch layer; the express body parser keeps nothing after a flow ends); every end of a sign-in (cancel, timeout, over-limit, superseded, landed then ok / failed / twice / pasted back, take, stopAll, an exchange in flight at each) drops both closures, reports exactly as often as it should and leaves no listener or fixed port behind; two sign-ins of one Lark account with the older one's exchange in flight land the NEWER token only; with sign-in on every consent and account verb, both agent tokens and the storage paths answer 401 without the cookie; the mount's secret is decrypted once per borrow and never cached, and a storage secret re-entered AFTER the borrow makes the account stop (the vendor refuses the old copy) until the mount is picked again, which takes the new copy in place. Five LOWs, fixed. (1) A refused CLIENT read as a refused token: Google's `invalid_client` after the storage mount's secret was re-entered said only "Unauthorized (401)" / "the vendor refused to refresh the login", so Re-authorize under the same held copy hit the same 401 and nothing said why — the sentence now names the client and what to do (pick the mount again, or re-enter the secret). (2) The Re-authorize dialog's own 10-minute stop fired at the same instant as the sign-in machine's and only cleared its poll, so a re-authorize left open for ten minutes kept "A … sign-in page opened" and a disabled button for ever; it now waits past the machine's end, reads the watcher once more and says the fail or "The sign-in was not finished in time — sign in again" (zh + ja), button enabled. (3) The scrub withheld a sent value in two spellings and the form body has a third (URLSearchParams percent-encodes `!'()~` and writes a space as `+`) — withheld in that spelling too; and it read the Bearer with a regex, which parks the whole Authorization header in V8's legacy `RegExp.input` until the next regex anywhere in the process (the ONE bearer the heap walk found after every pass) — read by slicing now. (4) The agent-token courtesy stopped at the verbs that begin or complete a sign-in: the status poll (the running consent URL carries the flow's state — a forged landing ends the owner's sign-in with a vendor refusal), cancel, the Edit dialog's save (a secret rewrite, a policy flip), duplicate, disconnect and remove accepted a self-identifying agent token on a sign-in-off instance — refused by name now, `an account is the owner's`. (5) The storage side that LENDS the client carried no such courtesy at all — `GET /api/mounts/:id/config` (the plaintext client secret), the Drive and Gmail guided sign-in routes (start / status / callback / cancel) and the token write — while the r2 note said "the mount routes refuse it"; they do now, and the note is corrected. Refuted, with the evidence: a listener's own error after bind does not crash the process (libuv drops an EMFILE accept without reaching JS — a 64-fd child with an open flow and three connects stays alive); a secret shorter than the ≥ 6 scrub floor cannot be sent (the registry refuses under 8); an HTML error page, a WWW-Authenticate echo and a value nested past the scrub's depth reach no worded field; the one-time authorization code is not withheld (dead after the exchange; judged). Gates: test-channels-engine ⑮ (14: thirteen verbs; 15: the storage routes' census + control; 16: the staged heap search in a child process — eight stages over the real engine, two holder-class controls: an adapter that keeps the client it resolved, an engine that memoizes the decrypted client) (344), test-channels-gmail-shape ⑧ r5 (the third spelling, the regex-free Bearer read pinned on `RegExp.input`, `invalid_client`'s words; three controls) (178), test-oauth-field-parity §10 (the dialog's stop + zh/ja; four controls) (273).

### Lane channel-withdraw — the agent's own withdrawal; the delivery choice on the Approve button; the receipt's diff and its fate

The owner, in real use (2026-09-27): "agent 似乎没有撤回之前制作的 draft 的能力，必须要我手动 reject 是吗？" — then "如果我修改后批准，agent 似乎也收不到我的修改动作和批准动作的通知，并不知道我希望以什么方式回复", "我在界面里完全看不到有消息在 queue", and "收件箱里的 approve 动作需要在账号-level 的通知配置里控制行为有点反直觉".

- **An agent can take back a draft it proposed, or replace it with a better one — you no longer have to reject it by hand.** `vibespace-channels withdraw <proposalId> [--why "…"]` takes back one of its OWN proposals while you have not decided it yet: the approval card turns into a dim "Withdrawn by <agent> · <why>" card with no buttons and the For-you item goes away, live. `reply … --replaces <proposalId>` / `compose … --replaces <proposalId>` withdraws the old draft and proposes the new one in one step — the old one goes only if the new one is accepted, and a decision of yours landing in the middle waits for it. Another agent (even one in the same Task Group) cannot withdraw it (`not-yours`); a draft already sent, being sent, decided, or whose outcome was lost cannot be withdrawn (`not-withdrawable`). The agent learns the verb from its manual (`vibespace-docs channels`); the command is pre-approved like `reply` (it only ever retracts its own proposal).
- **When you approve a draft you choose whether the agent hears now or with your next message — right on the button.** An agent's draft now has **Approve ▾** and **Reject ▾**: "Approve — tell the agent with your next message" (free, as before) or "Approve and wake the agent now (starts a turn)", plus "Approve with edits…"; "Reject — tell on its next message" or "Reject with a reason and wake now". The last choice you used on this device becomes the button. A woken receipt is one turn, at most once per draft, under the spend ceiling (a refusal is said on the card and the receipt waits for the next message instead). The old per-watcher "receipts wake me" option in Notify… no longer does anything (the server logs once at boot how many watchers still carry it).
- **When you edit a draft before approving, the agent is told what you changed.** The receipt shows the agent a line diff — "- you proposed / + the user sent" (at most 2000 characters) — and, after an edit or a rejection with a reason, ends "Use this as guidance for the next draft."
- **The card says whether the agent knows yet:** "Handed to <agent> at 14:02", "Waiting for <agent>'s next message" (it switches to "Handed …" the moment that message picks the receipt up — no reload), or "<agent> is gone — receipt kept". Approval cards are now kept in place when nothing about them changed, so an update elsewhere no longer redraws a card you are editing.
- What this instance showed (corrected by the verify round, from the outbox, the audit log and the drafter's transcript): the three drafts decided in the last day (two edited and approved, one rejected; all drafted by 运维管理) had all their receipts stored for its next message, none woke the agent; the rejection's receipt reached it 21 s later (22:50:23Z, the owner's next message) and the two approvals' receipts 20 s after the last of them (22:55:47Z) — two batches, not one; nothing on screen said they were waiting.
- **Verify round (adversarial; money + authority).** Counted with a fake ladder: a double click, two tabs, a retry after a network error, a reject racing an approve, an approve with edits, a replace chain — each proposal is billed ONCE (the second decision is `bad-state` and names the state); under the spend ceiling the wake is refused by name on the card and the receipt stays stored; a drafter that is not live (or whose Task-Group sibling is) is never replaced by another session; a bogus or missing `deliver` is next-turn (the route refuses a third word with 400); a withdraw fired while the vendor call is parked lands after it and is refused `not-withdrawable` — the message that went out is `sent` with its receipt, never "withdrawn"; hostile `--replaces` ids (an object, another agent's, a sent one, a withdrawn one, no principal) create nothing; a refused replacement leaves the old draft byte-identical with its For-you item; two concurrent replaces make ONE new draft; the money census sees the receipt site inside the one door. Two defects found and fixed: (1) **the 24 h sweep could expire a draft the agent was replacing that instant** — the sweep took its due list, a replace of one of them passed its check and made the new draft while the sweep was busy with an earlier proposal, and the sweep's write landed between the check and the withdrawal: the agent got an "EXPIRED unapproved" receipt for a draft it had just replaced. The sweep now asks "is a replace holding this id" inside the store's serialized write, at apply time (the hold is set before the replace's first await, so it is either visible or the replace's check reads the expiry and refuses before anything is made). (2) **the card said "Waiting for <agent>'s next message" for good about a receipt the agent had already read** — a receipt stored before this lane (no `ref` on its stash entry, the owner's three of that day) never gets a "drained" event. At boot, every stored-and-not-drained receipt is looked for in its drafter's queue (by ref, or by the proposal id its text names); one that is gone reads "Handed to <agent> with an earlier message" (no time — nobody recorded it). A wake-now approve whose send the vendor refused still wakes once, with the FAILED receipt (the decider asked to hear now; a failure is worth telling) — pinned as designed. Gates: test-channel-outbox §5v (the sweep window with an unguarded copy, the legacy fate with a no-reconcile copy, the one-bill counts, the vendor refusal), test-channels-engine (g) (the route: `deliver` refused by name, the `expectWakes` echo, a missing field = next-turn, no user-side withdraw route).
- **Verify round 2 (adversarial; the `unless` class generally, the reconcile's truth, the stash cap, the identity form).** Every outbox state change was enumerated (propose → sending/awaiting, approve → failed/sending, reject, withdraw, the send's sent/failed/unknown, reconcile, the boot `sending → unknown`, the sweep's expired) and its decision placed: every write runs the PURE table INSIDE the store's serialized callback; approve / reject / withdraw / replace (and now reconcile) queue on the proposal's own chain, so the sweep's `unless` sees the hold; the remaining pairs are disjoint by state (the table refuses `sending → expired`, `unknown` leaves only through reconcile). Constructed and pinned: a sweep during a vendor-parked approve 25 h after the draft expires nothing (sent, one receipt); two overlapping sweeps expire each draft once; a peer message carrying the receipt's own `proposal <id>:` line keeps nothing waiting (the legacy match needs the engine's source). Four defects found and fixed: (1) **a stored receipt the stash CAP dropped (30 later entries — a Task-Group sibling's messages, channel notices) was never read, the card said "Waiting for <agent>'s next message" for good, and the boot reconcile read the missing entry as "Handed … with an earlier message"** — the ladder now reports an `evicted` entry (with the count held), the engine stamps it, the card says "Not delivered — <agent>'s queue was full; the receipt is kept here", the reconcile never guesses over a recorded eviction (the receipt itself stays on the proposal); (2) **a replace the process died inside — the new draft stamped `replaces`, the old still awaiting — left TWO approvable copies of one message after the restart** (the design's own worst case: a duplicate in somebody else's room) — at boot every such replace is finished (the old one withdrawn, `replacedBy` the new, its pointer retracted); (3) **a session that had no conversation id yet could draft as `webui:<id>`** — its receipt was stashed under a key nothing drains, the card called the live session "gone", and its own later withdraw was `not-yours` — `reply` / `compose` / `withdraw` now answer 409 `bad-member` ("this session has no conversation id yet — try again after its first turn", msg send's sentence) before anything is created; (4) two concurrent Check-outcome presses asked the adapter twice — reconcile now queues on the proposal's chain (one ask, the second is `bad-state`). Round 1's cheap LOWs fixed: a browser on the agent withdraw route is 403 `not-yours` by name ("reject it from the card instead"), a card left alone while you edit it patches its primary Approve label when the remembered choice moved elsewhere, and a real drain after a boot guess records its time. Gates: test-channel-outbox §5v2 (each with a patched-copy control: a ladder whose cap drops silently, an engine without the boot replace sweep, a bare reconcile export, a drained branch that keeps the guess), test-channels-engine (g2) (the REAL agent routes: 409 by name from a session without a conversation id, 403 by name for a browser; a copy without the guards creates a `webui:` drafter).
- **Verify round 4 (adversarial; the fork rule enumerated, the press in Chrome, the prune, the money leftovers, the receipt bytes, the seams with lane channel-jump).** Two more verbs let a fork that still carries its parent's conversation id speak AS the parent — fixed: `vibespace-msg send --wake` from such a fork minted the pair group under the PARENT's id and the target's reply woke the PARENT (a billed turn on the wrong conversation, the pair bound for good), and `vibespace-channels request` recorded the parent as the requester under the fork's name (the owner's approval widened the parent's reach; a session with no id yet recorded a placeholder nobody matches). The caller's own id is now decided in the one place every msg verb asks (`msgCaller`), and `request` is guarded like reply / compose / withdraw — all answer 409 by name. Three LOWs: the store's bound now drops what nobody decided first (withdrawn, then expired) — one agent's 520 replaces had pushed another drafter's ten decided records out before a single withdrawal left; a receipt whose stash write FAILED (a full disk) is `undelivered` by name instead of "waiting" then "handed" at the next boot; a "wake now" the store could not record is named on the card. Refuted with reproduction: sixteen fork shapes agree between this lane's rule and the browser-key lane's; the button's words and its fact never disagree at any instant on a page with two sections; Enter / Space post what the button says; a still-open ▾ menu's second decision is refused and toasted; a stale card on a withdrawn draft is refused by name on every path; pruning breaks no replace chain or fate; a downgraded or failed wake row never wakes later (a second press, Check outcome, the engine's own re-entry, a restart: 0 billed); the wake is charged to the member held at the wake; a CJK diff over budget still yields a clipped line + the pointer + the guidance under 4 096 bytes; a 20 000-case frame fuzz of the diff and block finds zero live frames. Gates: test-msg-cli-groups (the pending fork over the REAL groups engine, the raw-id copy as control), test-channels-engine (g2) r4 (the request verb, the guard-less copy), test-channel-outbox §5v3 r4 (the rank, the unwritable stash, the row-lost words — each with a patched-copy control), test-channel-groups (the msgCaller pin).
- **Verify round 7 (adversarial; the fork class closed by CENSUS, not by the next example).** Round 7 asked whether the class was finally closed and answered by a grep-derived census made into a gate: every raw "which live session carries this conversation id" comparison across the tree is now classified in a checked-in table, an unlisted one fails the suite, and a patched copy that adds one on a fresh module fails (the negative control). The tree holds exactly six such reads — one is the msg-endpoints finder already fenced by the fork predicate, the other five name or bill nothing on the parent (a display name, a shared-transcript read, two user-explicit stale-id fallbacks for rename/kill, and the real-usage odometer which keys the pool member by the session's own webui id). The correct sites the earlier rounds produced read the predicate, so a revert to a raw read re-reddens the census. No new defect: the "harmless" list was attacked one site at a time (the helper-ask item, the reset-credit item, the unresumable breaker, the pool display name, the normalizer thread default, incident capture, layout persistence) and each proven to name/bill/grant/record nothing on the parent; a grant a pending fork holds under its placeholder key survives adoption (the key set always carries the webui key); every money attack of rounds 3–6 re-run green (test-channel-outbox 270, test-spend-paths 310, test-channels-engine 279). The .195 merge checklist was made current against lane-channel-jump's head (the three ladder lookups sit in a region jump does not touch; take withdraw's fork-aware jobsCaller and group-report caller on top of jump's drain-under-cap ordering; take withdraw's no-cid wording). Gates: test-msg-cli-groups §2c (the census + its negative control).
- **Verify round 6 (adversarial; the predicate's last three readers, the adoption hand-off, the frozen memo, the durability verdict, the money re-run, the words).** The delivery ladder itself still found "the live session carrying this conversation" by the raw id — fixed: for the seconds a codex fork carries its parent's thread id (its wrapper advertises the peer lane before `thread/fork` answers), a Background Work notification owned by the stopped parent was written into the FORK's wrapper (a billed turn on the fork) and charged to the fork's account; with both live and the fork restored first, the parent's turn was charged to the fork's account and the fork's next prompt read as a machine turn; the peer card was drawn in the fork's window; a browser handback of a pending fork would have billed the parent. "Share with agent…" on a fork that had not announced its own conversation yet granted the PARENT (it could act on the user's window and on the app the fork opened) and the fork lost the grant the moment it adopted its own id — fixed: the engine keys a pending fork by its placeholder, the dialog sends the live session, an ambiguous key is refused by name. A pending fork's prompt rendered the parent's unread group messages and marked them read for the parent — fixed. Words: "Ask an agent to take control" on such a fork said "say something to it first" (its own code and sentence now, zh/ja); the refusal every agent verb gives said "try again after its first turn" (a fork announces its own id within seconds — "wait a moment and repeat", and `vibespace-msg` prints the remedy). Refuted with reproductions: the adoption hand-off (an ask, its reply, a message by name, a window grant all follow the fork), the frozen outbox copy (no reader mutates it), the stash's durability verdict. Every money attack of rounds 3–6 re-run green. Measured and left to the owner: the 6.5 MB outbox broadcast per change at the 16 KB bound (CPU trivial, the wire under an agent's loop is the cost).
- **Verify round 5 (adversarial; the caller identity from the other side, the store's read cost, the stash's one outcome, the card in Chrome, the merge preview).** A fork that still carries its parent's conversation id was still somebody's ADDRESS — fixed: both rosters listed it under the parent's id with its own name, so with the parent not live another agent's `vibespace-msg send --wake "<fork>"` minted the pair group under the PARENT's id (bound for good) and authorized a billed turn on the parent, and with the parent live every message to the parent was refused `ambiguous`; and a Background Work job such a fork created was OWNED by the parent's conversation — every notification a billed turn on the parent, for the job's whole life. One predicate now decides whom a live session may be addressed as (`addressableId`: its own id or nothing), behind every roster and every caller resolver; a pending fork's job creation, page attribution, its For-you items and the owner's "ask it to take control" are refused, unattributed or keyed to the fork itself until it has its own id. One proposal's read deep-copied the WHOLE outbox (34 sites): at the store's bound with 16 KB texts one agent's replace held the server ~836 ms — one copy per write now, frozen (~480 ms at that extreme, the rest is the store's five rewrites per replace; ~20 ms at ordinary sizes). Every producer of the agent-message queue now hears one named verdict when the disk refuses the write (the entry stays in memory, "queued in memory only — lost if VibeSpace restarts", a 30 s retry) — a peer message used to vanish at the next restart with one log line. Four refusal codes that reached the card and the chip raw are worded (zh, ja). Refuted in Chrome and in code: the fork's adoption window, the prune at a store of decided records, the phone's ▾ menu, two surfaces on one broadcast, the 200-draft draw, every fate's zh/ja wording.
- **Verify round 3 (adversarial; over the REAL delivery ladder, the REAL spend guard and the REAL routes).** Counted and pinned: 20 concurrent "approve and wake now" on 20 drafts of one drafter — in 20 conversations and in one — under a spend cap of 2 ⇒ exactly 2 billed turns, 2 ledger stamps, 18 refused by name and stored; a double click, reject ‖ approve, approve ‖ withdraw in either order ⇒ one outcome; an authorizer that throws bills nothing; a wake-now approve whose send was lost wakes ONCE at the Check-outcome five hours later; a stranger, a sibling, a reader, an adopted fork and another conversation's job cannot withdraw (the stranger gets the same bytes for an existing and a nonexistent id); a resumed conversation's new session still owns its draft. Three defects found and fixed: (1) **the Approve button's words were not its press** — after "Reject with a reason and wake now" was picked on one card (its box opens, nothing posted), another card's primary still reading "Approve — tell the agent with your next message" posted a wake: a billed turn the words said was free; the press now does what its own button says, and a pick re-words every primary on the page at once; (2) **a fork that had not yet announced its own conversation id (it carries its parent's) could take the parent's drafts back and draft AS the parent** — the receipt, and an "Approve and wake now" turn, landed on the parent; such a session now answers 409 by name ("this session is a fork that has not announced its own conversation id yet … try again after its first turn"; an adopted codex fork still drafts as itself); (3) **withdrawn drafts never left outbox.json** — the store's bound did not know the new terminal state, so an agent's withdrawals / replaces accumulated for good (540 on disk, the whole file rewritten on every write) and the bound dropped the owner's DECIDED records instead; the bound is now every terminal state, pinned equal to the policy's. Seven LOWs fixed: the proposal's one wake row is answered by its WRITE (a failed write is no wake — it woke under a log saying it had not); the boot replace sweep takes every hold before its first await (the TTL sweep expired 2 of 4 replaced drafts beside it); a stored receipt is on disk before the card says "waiting" (a crash inside the 500 ms debounce lost it and the next boot said "Handed"); the receipt's diff is frame-inert against the JOIN of its lines (a tag split over two lines, or assembled from the draft's and the edit's lines, was live) with a whole-block belt; the receipt block is budgeted in BYTES (a Chinese edit's diff was clipped at the drain and its guidance sentence was the part cut); one sentence for a missing and a stranger's proposal id on `--replaces`; `replaces` must be a string. Gates: test-channel-outbox §5v3 (a patched-copy control per fix), test-channels-engine (g2) (the pending fork over the REAL agent routes, the codex-shaped adopted fork, the guard-less copy), test-channel-record (the joined-lines rule), test-channels-groups-e2e ⑩ r3 (chrome: a pick on card X re-words card Y at once and Y's press does what it says — one woken receipt at the agent's stub).
- Gates: test-channel-outbox §5 (the withdrawn rows of the state machine with a `sent → withdrawn` mutant; withdraw own / sibling / outsider / sending / sent / unknown; replace accepted / refused-atomic / the hold, with two patched-copy controls; the diff table and a no-diff copy; the delivery-choice table and a wake-twice copy; the fate table; waiting → handed on a drain), test-channels-engine (a stored receipt opt-in ignored; five "wake now" rejects = five wakes each once, repeated receipts never twice, a session that is not live never woken, the ceiling named; the ONE-door census), test-channels-agent-cli (withdraw / --replaces), test-channels-groups-e2e ⑩ (chrome: withdraw → the card and the For-you row without a reload; the split menu, the remembered choice, the woken receipt reaching the agent once, the fate line patched in place).

### From the chat to the conversation — the channel witness (B-099e, docs/design-communication-panel.zh.md §26)

The owner: with hundreds of mails and Lark chats, finding the conversation an agent is working on is the slow part — and the agent already knows. "那就按照这个做吧" (plan A: the server watches; the agent gets no new tool and no extra context).

- **Every tool call that read, searched, replied to or wrote a channel conversation now carries one row per conversation on its card** — the account and the title ("Work mail › Invoice for March"), what the agent did there ("drafted a reply · read 12 messages", "3 search hits", "wrote a new message") and the time. The drafted one comes first; three rows are shown, the rest behind "+N more". A click opens that conversation's window (or brings it to the front); a new mail that is not sent yet opens the Outbox. A card with rows is not folded away into "3 Bash".
- **The chat's status bar names the conversation this turn touched last**: "Channels · Ops room". With one conversation a click opens it; with several it lists them, drafted first. The chip goes away when your next message starts a turn that touches nothing.
- **The conversation window says who was there**: "Drafted by Session 1 · 3 min ago" / "Read by Session 1 · just now" under its title — a click brings that agent's chat to the front.
- **Nothing changed for the agent** except one sentence in its manual ("Everything you read or draft here is shown to the user as a clickable card in the chat — you never need to tell them where"). The server records what the agent's own `vibespace-channels` calls touched, only after an answer the agent was allowed to see; a hidden conversation leaves no trace.
- **It survives a restart**: the rows are kept with the session and come back on the cards after the server restarts. Conversation titles and mail subjects are drawn as plain text everywhere (a subject spelling HTML or one of our own markers stays text).
- Gates: test-channel-touch (fast: the rules as tables, eight negative controls, wiring pins), test-architecture §63 (every agent channel route records what it touched), test-channel-jump (heavy: a real browser, a stub agent running the shipped `vibespace-channels`, the three surfaces, a hostile subject, a server restart).

### What is waiting for an agent is visible above its composer, with a Hand over now button

The owner: "能看到，只是会堆积到我下次发消息给它，这个有点 confusing，因为我在界面里完全看不到'有消息在 queue'这件事情" (notices pile up until I next message the agent, and nothing in the UI says so).

- **What is waiting for an agent is now visible above its composer**: "3 notices are waiting for this agent's next turn: a channel receipt, a job result, a message from Ada". It covers everything that is held for the agent's next turn — replies you approved or rejected, Background Work results, messages from other agents, the browser handback, a window request.
- **Hand over now** delivers all of them at once, as one message; when the agent is idle the button says it "starts a turn" (it counts against the same limit as every turn nobody typed). If the limit is reached or the agent cannot be reached, a message says so and the notices keep waiting. The strip disappears by itself when your next message hands them over.
- **The session card in the sidebar says "N waiting"** too (hover it for the list).
- On a phone the strip folds to one line and the button.
- **Verify round (2026-09-27, four defects reproduced on the real ladder before the fix).** (1) Two clicks on "Hand over now" — a double click, the button in two tabs, a click during a slow post to a paired machine — were two ladder calls: the same notices delivered twice and two ledger rows; a conversation now has ONE hand-over in flight, and a second click is refused by name ("already in progress"). (2) Your own message sent while a hand-over was still on its way took the same notices at its injection, so the agent read them twice (once in your turn, once from the hand-over); the hand-over now CLAIMS what it is delivering — your message's drain leaves a claimed notice alone, and a refused hand-over gives the claim back. (3) "starts a turn" was decided by whether the agent was busy, but a claude session that is mid-turn is still charged (its inbox queues the message and runs it as its own turn); the cost is now the server's word, read off the harness's lane — only a codex turn that folds the notification into the running turn is free. (4) More than two waiting job results were delivered with their middle elided and no file to read them from (the next-turn injection writes one); the hand-over writes the same file and names it.
