And typing into a browser shared with all conversations now reaches the page — the sharing proxy refused your own keys while you drove (measured on agent-browser 0.38.1: one input record is one browser call and the stream server reports nothing back; with the fix the real browser receives every key you type while you drive), so it now admits exactly the inputs the live view forwarded.
- **A deleted profile leaves no pin behind.** The Agent browser panel's Delete… (owner ruling A (6): every chat's lease released, the browser stopped, every pin cleared, the directory set aside) now leaves each chat that pinned it saying "work was deleted — its pin was cleared" instead of a raw id or silence, a pin left behind by an earlier delete is cleared at start-up, and the API refuses a set-aside or DELETE of a pinned profile without `unpin` ("N conversation(s) use this profile").
- **The New Session dialog lists every profile** the Agent browser panel lists (a separate-tabs one too — under owner ruling A the pick is the conversation's pin, opened through the keeper on its first browser command) and updates while the dialog is open; the first row reads "No profile (temporary browser)".
- **Session Properties' Agent browser section** updates the moment you pin, keeps the name on one line, uses the window's own buttons, and Esc closes the window.
- **Verify round (the sharing proxy's fence).** The first cut let the agent's own browser commands spend the credits your takeover minted: an `agent-browser click` racing your click landed on the shared browser while you were driving, your own key was refused, and the bar said "delivered". A credit is now bound to the exact click or key it was minted for (measured on agent-browser 0.38.1); nothing else passes the fence while you drive, and nothing of the agent's can burn your credits. **Verify r2:** the credit is also bound to the tab you are looking at — an agent's own connection to the shared browser, on one of its other tabs, could mirror the Enter you were about to press and land it there as if you had typed it (your own Enter refused, the bar saying delivered); now only a call on the tab you drive can spend your credit, and a mirror anywhere else burns nothing. **Verify r3:** while you drive, the agent could still move what you were looking at — its raw `tab` switch on the shared browser was not stopped by the fence, the picture followed and your next keys went to the tab it chose; a takeover is now anchored to the tab it began on: a switch you did not make is refused where it is seen (your keys answer "the browser moved to another tab while you were driving — hand back and take over again to drive it", nothing is forwarded), and the agent's `vibespace-browser tab` / `open` / `back` refusals say by name that they would move your view. Two more doors closed: a method that makes the page ignore every input (armed before your takeover, it swallowed your keys while the bar said delivered) is refused on every lease, and moving the focus to another field while you drive is refused. Receipts say what was seen — "it reached another tab than the one you are looking at and was refused there", "the browser has not answered it" — and over a browser that streams directly the bar says "Typing is sent to the browser" (VibeSpace sees its own write, not the page's answer).
- **Verify r4 (the fence is a census, and the grace is measured).** Three rounds each found the takeover fence one method short, because it was a hand-written list (Input.* + a navigation family, then + the deaf-page arm, then + a focus move). It is now a CENSUS: every one of the 664 methods the installed Chrome (153.0.8010.47) lists in its own protocol has a row in src/cdp-census.js, classed input (15) / view (106) / page-mutation (195) / read (176) / session (11) / harmless (147) / refused (14); while you drive a shared browser, input and view are refused, reads / session / harmless answer, and a method the census does not know (a newer Chrome's) is refused BY NAME until it gets a row — never a silent hole. The page-mutation class (script evaluation, DOM / CSS edits, cookies…) stays open by design (D6) behind ONE new setting, `browser.fenceScriptsWhileDriven`, default OFF (the owner has been asked); ON, that class is refused too and the refusal names the setting. The takeover anchor's 1 s grace (r3 F6: a whole second in which an agent's tab switch was followed) is now 62 ms = 3 × the measured p99 of the daemon's tabs-record latency (2 × 100 real switches on agent-browser 0.38.1 + Chrome 153.0.8010.47: p99 15.4 / 20.4 ms; scripts/measure-anchor-grace.mjs). Gates: test-browser-mediation ⑥ (the census over the pinned protocol fixture, every row's verdict on the anchor's tab and the lease's other tab, the unknown rule, the switch read live by the real proxy, three patched-copy controls), test-browser-mediation-chrome ⑥ (heavy: the launched Chrome's own /json/protocol — extras print and fail — and every class against a real paused lease with the raw endpoint as the oracle), test-browser-fact ③ r4 (the grace pinned to its measurement).
- Gates: test-browser-fact (fast: the fact over every combination, the follow rule, the receipts and the sharing proxy end to end with three negative controls incl. the theft, a census that no surface derives its own answer), test-browser-identity (heavy: the five study scenes in chrome with real clicks and keys). src/browser-fact.js is the one fact and its words.

### Lane R5 — Gmail and Lark are read at a steady pace, a vendor's rate limit is a short wait said by name, and a linked account's sign-in has one door

- **Gmail is read at a steady pace, and a vendor's rate limit is a few seconds' wait, said by name** (lane R5; the owner on 2.369.185: "gmail一直被限速 你可能要控制下gmail默认的读取速度"). What happened: Google refused whole passes ("Quota exceeded for quota metric 'Total Query Cost' and limit 'Units per minute per user'", three times in ten minutes on two accounts) that stayed UNDER our 3000/min budget — each spent ~2 000–2 800 units in ~20 s; a per-minute cap is a sum, not a shape, and Google meters finer than a minute. Each refusal then climbed the account's failure ladder to its 15-minute maximum and filed a "For you" item. Now: ① reads are PACED PER SECOND (PURE `src/channel-drain.js` rule 18 — a per-account token bucket; a call short of tokens is a `wait` of ≤ 1 s after which the drain picks again, a human's press first; never a refusal, never a skip) and every Gmail / Lark request awaits the bucket before it is sent — Gmail 40 quota units a second (one thread read; ≤ 80 in any second, ≤ 2 440 in any minute; the 873-thread first read ≈ 14.6 min, evenly), Lark 5 requests a second, each never faster than the minute's budget (new settings `channels.gmailUnitsPerSec` 5–100, `channels.larkRequestsPerSec` 1–50); ② a vendor RATE refusal waits the vendor's own Retry-After (Lark `x-ogw-ratelimit-reset`) or 5 s doubling to 60 s, never counts as a failed pass, and reaches "For you" only if it persists through 10 strikes; auth / transport failures keep the 30 s → 15 min ladder; Gmail's 403 "usageLimits" / quota-metric refusals are typed rate-limited, not forbidden; ③ the account card says "Google 限速中 · 12 秒后继续" ("Google is limiting the rate · resuming in 12 s") from the first strike — the vendor by its declared name, Feishu / Lark by the account's brand — and "首次读取中 · 已 120/873 个会话 · 约剩 13 分钟" while conversations are read for the first time (a long paced pass repaints at most every 5 s); the budget sentence names units/s beside units/min. Gates: test-channel-drain (a paced walk profile, the 873-row first read, 5 mutants), test-channels-aggregate ③d/③e (+ pre-fix controls), test-channel-caps, test-channel-adapter-contract, test-channels-gmail-shape / -lark-shape ⑥b (the vendor's cost table pinned), test-channels-e2e ⑰ (heavy). Verify round: a request filed while the pass slept on a pace wait was judged only when the sleep ended (a refusal ~0.9 s late) — `pokeDrain` now wakes the sleeping pass (③f, real timers, with the no-wake control); ③e runs under a real-time watchdog; the bucket is per ACCOUNT (two accounts of one Google user sum — documented, §6.2b).
- **Verify r2 of the pace (vendor-budget class):** outside a pass the bucket was a check-then-charge across an await — 20 concurrent attachment fetches (a window's thumbnails) left in one instant (400 units in a second on the real Gmail adapter, the burst Google refuses) and a page-back filed mid-ingest waited for the whole ingest (14 minutes on 873 threads). The bucket is now judged one caller at a time per account, in arrival order, with the units reserved as they are let through: 20 × 20 units take 9 s at 40/s, never above 80 in a second, and a page-back takes the next slot. Also: one open "For you" item per account — a failure on the other ladder (transport after a rate wait, or the reverse) retracts the standing item as superseded before filing its own; two had been filed and the first outlived the recovery. A persistent daily-limit 403 is retried at most once a minute per account (said in the design). Gates: test-channels-aggregate ③d′ + ③g (real timers, two patched-copy controls, the pre-fix page-back printed) — 305 → 318.
- **Verify r3 of the pace (vendor-budget class):** a caller queued behind an account that was REMOVED (or rebuilt) while it waited for its pace was let through, unpaced — 17 attachment fetches of 20 units left within 1 ms of a remove(), each a vendor call the owner had just ended; such a caller is now aborted by name ("the account changed … the request was not sent"), and a paced call that outlives its live entry never runs. Also: the judged bucket is capped before the reservation comes off (a latent arithmetic slip the charge's microtask ordering masked), a reservation an adapter never metered is dropped after 2 s with a log line instead of holding the account's bucket down for good, the first-read wait past 90 minutes is said in hours and minutes ("about 5 h 49 min left"), and the Chinese budget sentence no longer counts quota units as 次. Recorded lows: the adapter FIFO is arrival order (a 100-unit send-shaped call behind the user's own 30 thumbnails waits ~15 s; the drain's humans-first orders requests, not the adapter's queue); after Disable / Disconnect the calls already queued finish paced.
- **Verify r4 of the pace (vendor-budget class) — ONE GATE, ONE EXIT, both a census.** Every round had found one more path around the pace; this round closed the shape. THE GATE: every Gmail / Lark request goes through the adapter's `api()` (token → pace → meter → the bearer re-read AFTER the wait → send); every other outbound call in the two adapter files (+ the Gmail push lane) is a `// gated-inline: <id>` site with its own pace + meter right above it or a `// ungated: <id>` site whose id the module's frozen `UNGATED` list names with a reason an agent or a loop cannot multiply (a human consent, once; the Pub/Sub long-poll; the integrations Test button) — a grep census in test-channels-gmail-shape ⑥c / test-channels-lark-shape ⑥c fails a new outbound call outside the gate (patched copies adding a bare call, dropping a send's pace, or naming an unlisted id are red). Found by it: a Lark SEND was neither paced nor metered (now both); the token refresh had no single flight, so 20 concurrent thumbnails at one expiry were 20 refresh POSTs, and under Lark's rotating refresh token 11 of 12 were `invalid_grant` — each stamping the STALE token back over the sibling's fresh one, logging the account out and asking the owner to re-authorize (one refresh in flight per adapter now; a refused refresh stamps `invalidGrantAt` only while the stored token is still the one it tried); a request captured its bearer BEFORE the pace wait, so a disconnect or a re-authorize that landed during the wait was followed by requests carrying the dropped / old token (the bearer is re-read after the wait: a disconnect refuses by name, a re-authorize's token is the one sent). THE EXIT: every lifecycle end of an account's right to call the vendor — remove, disable, disconnect, an options rebuild, a client switch, a refused connect, the engine's stop — takes the engine's ONE `dropLive`: r3 had recorded that `setEnabled(false)` and `disconnect()` let 18 queued fetches (360 units) finish, paced, with the captured Bearer after the owner had ended the account — both take the exit now (0 calls after, every queued caller aborted by name, a fresh fetch on a disabled account refused `disabled`); a fetch that OUTLIVED its entry writes nothing (a remove() mid-fetch used to resurrect the removed account's index row + log page and write its attachment cache file); an exit never refills a bucket (the rebuilt entry inherits the minute window + per-second bucket — a disable/enable was a fresh 80-unit burst). The exit census in test-channels-aggregate ③g (v) fails a second `live.delete` site, a lifecycle verb without its exit, a `dropLive` call in an unlisted verb, or a vendor-then-write path without its guard (four text controls + three driven controls). Recorded, no code: the adapter FIFO is arrival order (a 100-unit send behind 30 of the user's own thumbnails waits ≈ 15 s; the only agent-class caller outside the pass is the pass's own single fetch, so a human is never more than one slot behind an agent — a two-class queue would buy ≤ 1 s). Measured: 200 pokes 1 ms apart still ≤ 40 units/s, 36 ms CPU; a SIGKILL mid-wait persists nothing (the store carries no bucket, reservation, queue or sleeper) and the next boot's first fetch leaves at once.
- **Verify r5 of the pace (credential class) — the token's writers.** The r4 closure judged every vendor call; attacking its own edges showed the token a call carries had three unordered writers. Fixed: a refresh writes only while the store still holds the token it tried (a re-authorize landing during a refresh was reverted in 25 of 50 trials; a disconnect was undone and the account called the vendor again; a client-switch rebind ended with the old client's token ⇒ `invalid_grant` ⇒ logged out); a store write the disk refuses keeps the vendor's token in memory and flushes it at the next request (under Lark's rotating refresh token one lost write logged the account out); a bearer that expired while the request queued is refreshed once before the send (34 of 50 thumbnails at the 5 units/s floor went out expired); a consent naming another Google / Lark user than the account's is refused by name at the one token door and at the rebind (`src/channel-identity.js`; the identity survives a disconnect — to read another account, add it as a new account); a failure landing after a disconnect no longer stamps the disconnected record; the budget read right after a disable/enable shows the ghost's minute, not zero. Pinned in test-channels-gmail-shape / -lark-shape ⑥c (d)–(g) and test-channels-accounts ⑫, each with a patched copy as the control.
- **Verify r6 of the pace (credential class) — whose account, and the door's compare-and-swap.** A short round on r5's three fixes, on the real engine + real store + the real gmail.js / lark.js over scripted vendors. Fixed (credential, medium): a consent the vendor could not NAME (the profile / user_info read failed) was stored — a brand-new account then took ANYONE's next consent, and a stranger's nameless consent landed on a BOUND record unjudged ("no common key"); now the adapter refuses it by name (`namelessSentence`: nothing connected, retry) and the door refuses a nameless consent onto a held identity. Fixed (credential, medium — the migration edge): a LEGACY Lark record (pre-r5, `auth.user` = the display name) held no identity, so a stranger's consent bound it; a legacy Gmail record disconnected after the upgrade (auth.user wiped) took a stranger too — the door now judges by the token the record HOLDS (`heldIdentity(rec, storedToken)`) and every legacy record is stamped ONCE at boot (`stampIdentities`). Structural: the ONE token door is a compare-and-swap (`meta.supersedes`, judged inside the serialized store callback at APPLY time) — r5's re-read-then-enqueue relied on there being no await between the two, and a patched adapter with one reverted a re-authorize again; a persist in flight for ANOTHER token queues the later write (the r5 single flight handed it the earlier token's promise and dropped it — under Lark's rotation the store then kept a retired token ⇒ the next refresh `invalid_grant`); Lark's paced refresh re-reads the token after its pace wait (a disconnect / re-authorize during it no longer sends the POST with the dropped / superseded refresh token). Said: a refreshed sign-in the disk refuses files ONE "For you" item naming what a restart before the disk recovers means (retracted when a write lands); the residual — a restart before that — stays needs-reauth by name. Measured 50 trials × {re-authorize, disconnect, rebind, remove} × {gmail, lark} with the refresh POST held, and 50 same-tick microtask orderings: 0 reverted, 0 vendor calls with a wrong bearer. Pinned: test-channels-gmail-shape / -lark-shape ⑥c (h)–(k) (the r5 persist as the control), test-channels-accounts ⑫ (f)–(i) (an engine copy without the CAS + an adapter copy with the await as the control).
- **Verify r7 of the pace (credential class) — a human act during the consent's completion wins.** A short round on r6's closure (the compare-and-swap door, the boot stamp, the nameless refusal) on the real engine + real store + the real gmail.js / lark.js over scripted vendors with the consent's profile read held mid-flight. MEDIUM (credential + money, fixed): a disconnect, a cancel, a newer sign-in or a client-switch rebind's disconnect landing WHILE the consent was being completed was undone by the consent landing late — the record connected again and the pass it kicked made 4 vendor calls on the account the owner had ended; an older flow's late completion overwrote the newer sign-in's token. Fix: the loopback hands the exchange the flow's own `cancelled()`, the adapters pass it through, and the door refuses INSIDE its serialized write a consent whose flow was ended meanwhile (`cancelledSentence` naming the cause); a flow cancelled mid-exchange ends `{ok:false, cancelled}` whatever the exchange returned. Lows fixed: every judgement of the door (cancelled / nameless / identity / the CAS) now runs at apply time — the identity check sat before the store's await, so two consents of one tick on an unbound record were both judged against nothing (the record ended bound to whichever was enqueued last); a CAS write naming '' landed on a CLEARED store (now never); a consent naming whitespace or a bare word passed the adapter's truthiness check and landed a token that named nobody (an `email` is an identity only when it looks like an address; Lark ids trimmed); the boot stamp took a Lark display name with an '@' as an email and named none of the records it could not stamp (one log line now). Held: the ENOSPC shape on the real store (the item names EACCES, the next request flushes and retracts it), an 8 s profile read stores nothing until it answers, a hanging one is bounded at 20 s and nameless, the 15-shape legacy table with an idempotent second boot. Gates: test-channels-accounts ⑫ (j)–(k) + (d) rows (166), test-channels-gmail-shape ⑥c (l)–(m) (139), test-channels-lark-shape ⑥c (l) (121), test-oauth-loopback ⑥ (45); controls: an engine copy without the cancelled check, one with the judgement hoisted.
- **Verify r8 of the pace (credential class) — the closing round on `cancelled()`: the write is the fact.** One medium fixed: r7's loopback overrode its report whenever a cancel was marked — `{ok:false, "nothing was connected"}` over a consent ALREADY ON DISK — so a cancel, the timer's cancel, a newer sign-in or a stop() landing between the door's serialized callback and `finish()`'s report left the account connected on the consent's token with a last sign-in line saying nothing was connected, and no pass kicked (measured with an injected loopback whose exchange runs the act after the write); a stop() mid-exchange had the door refuse by name and then `onAuthDone` stamp adapters.json after `store.close()`. Fix: `finish()` reports `ok` = the exchange resolved (it cannot undo a write; an exchange consults `cancelled()` before writing and throws to refuse) and carries a late cancel beside `ok:true`; `onAuthDone` reads `ok` as landed, judges a disconnect-since by the record (no pass, no connected line), skips only a refused superseded flow; `onPendingDone` keeps refusing the carried cancel (its durable write is still ahead); both doors read the engine's `stopped` as `shutdown`; nothing is written after `stop()`; the refusal's tail says what the record holds. Held: 20 orderings of A in flight / B superseding under cancel and disconnect on both paths, the real deadline before/after the write. Recorded: a refused door still rides the store's unconditional atomic rewrite (same bytes, new inode); `flows.take()` is never called. Gates: test-channels-accounts ⑫ (l) (196; a loopback copy with r7's override and an engine copy without the stop guard as controls), test-oauth-loopback ⑥ (48), test-channels-gmail-shape ⑥c (m) re-pinned (139).

### Integration

- **The first click after the page loads is no longer swallowed by the fading loading screen.** The boot splash fades to opacity 0 once the workspace is ready but stayed over everything (z-index 999999) until a 300 ms timer removed it — on a busy machine longer — so the first press after a page load landed on an invisible layer (the .190 heavy run's lost click, B-b122). It now stops taking clicks the moment the fade starts (`pointer-events: none` in the same statement, src/client.js). Pins: a source pin + control in test-browser-live; the behavioural pin is ⑥'s negative control, whose press right after a reload now waits for the picture to be the element under the pointer.
- **A takeover is of the whole shared browser, and "who drives" still names the view.** With owner ruling A (2.369.189) a named profile is shared by every chat; S2's rule — taking over the browser interrupts, pauses and tells EVERY chat on it — now meets it: the other chats' commands answer `browser_paused` (each told by its own card, each reminded of its own verbs), not `browser_busy`; a chat taken with another view's takeover remembers which chat's view holds it, so the Agent browser strip still says "you, in <chat>" (test-browser-share-model / test-browser-share updated to the rule).
- **S5 × S2 on pins and deletes.** The pin is the conversation's default attachment (ruling A), so S2's attach-at-start of a shared profile chosen in the New Session dialog was dropped (the pick is the pin); ruling A's Delete… is the one delete dialog and S2's refuse-or-warn sits behind it on the server (release → the housekeeping verdict → the pin guard → unpin with the cleared mark → the set-aside); the keeper's placeholder `pinnedBy` / `clearPin` and the routes' placeholder `unpinProfile` gave way to S2's (the cleared mark the chip reads); a verb refused after a pin opened is still named on the handback's re-run list.
- **An attachment fetch the account's end aborted is not a remembered vendor refusal (R3 × R5).** A disable, a disconnect or a new sign-in aborts the queued picture fetches by name; R3's negative cache used to remember that abort as the vendor's `transport` refusal, so the next ask after a disable answered "transport" instead of "disabled" (test-channels-aggregate's lifecycle leg). An answer that outlived its account keeps nothing, the negative cache included.
- **The mirror's fast job may take up to 30 minutes on GitHub's runner (it was cancelled at 15 on 2.369.191).** The fast tier has grown to build + 184 suites (1049 s here; .190's fast job took 843 s on the 2-vCPU runner and .191's, with S1's suites added, was cancelled at the job's 15-minute limit); `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `fast` job now has `timeout-minutes: 30` (the heavy job's 45 unchanged). Re-tiering the grown fast tier is a separate backlog item.
- **Gate (lane live-settle): test-browser-live ⑥ judges a typed value and a press only after they settled, not at an instant (B-b122 — the leg went red once in each of the .189 and .190 heavy runs and passed on retry).** The page's reports were separate fetches and the collector kept the last ARRIVAL (".189: the page held 'tomsmit'" while the page itself held "tomsmith"); the negative control's click was sent into the boot splash, which stays over everything at opacity 0 for 300 ms after the app is ready (".190": `hitC: {lost: true}` — the composer part had passed). Now every page report carries the page's own stamp and the newest wins, a typed value is judged after the view's own count of sent keys and two page reports in a row, a click is sent only when the picture is the element under the pointer and the view is driving, and an agent command after Hand back waits for the handback's own record; the same sweep fixed ②'s drop leg (it stopped at the first drop, which a loaded box can make with the fps gate) and the env-file read (byte-identical to lane S2's fix). No product change.
- **Gate: test-browser-live ⑧ waits for the Hand back's own records** — the view's mode record and the announcer's journal line — instead of 300 + 900 ms and 900 ms naps.
- **Gate fixes to the lanes' own pins (test-only):** test-browser-share-model's pre-ruling control re-spelled for the route's `attachPin(k, f, v, verb)`; test-browser-takeover ⑨'s wired-out control reads what the sibling call alone makes (S5's one-driver layer now refuses that copy's next command `browser_busy`); test-browser-fact ④ expects no re-point ONTO a directory (a pin is never a directory under ruling A); test-attach-rebuild's wiring pin admits S3's `kind` beside `recorded`; test-user-todos-layout's two-argument census counts 16 sites (S1 + R4 + R5); test-browser-identity's Set-aside scene clicks ruling A's Delete… and reads the dialog's words. And one fast-tier red on the re-run (1 run in 5, master's S4 suite): test-browser-fit's restore leg judged at the first sight of the restore's set, ~10 ms before its journal line, and started its clock after the client's close resolved — it now starts the clock before the close and waits for the restore's own journal line.

## 2.369.191 — a sub-agent's permission request is answerable from the chat and every outcome reads true; an account, a rule's conversations or one conversation can be shared with several agents in two steps — who may read and act, then who is woken — and an agent can write a new mail; the mirror's timing bound

### Lane S1 — a helper's permission request can be answered: the card is in the chat under the helper, in the helper's log, behind the "waiting for you" chip and in For you (B-6e95)


Both naive-user studies, task T9: "帮手要权限时没有任何地方能点'允许'" — asked to read two pages with two helpers, both helpers sat on "running Fetch page" for 4–18 minutes; the orange "waiting for you" chip lit up, the inbox said nothing needed the user, and no screen had an Allow button.

- **The helper's request is a permission card in the chat.** When a helper (a sub-agent the assistant started) needs permission — to fetch a page, run a command, edit a file — the card appears inside that helper's card in the conversation, saying which helper asks and what for ("Helper “Fetch title of example.com” needs your approval · WebFetch https://example.com"), with the same Allow / Always Allow / Deny as any other request. Always Allow adds the rule to the session exactly as it does for the assistant's own requests. The helper continues as soon as you answer.
- **The same card is in the helper's log.** View Log on a running helper opens its live log, and the request is on the tool it wants to use there too; answering in either place answers both.
- **"waiting for you" says who waits and takes you there.** The chip's tooltip names the helper and the tool (or how many requests wait), and clicking it scrolls to the card and flashes it — even when the card is far up the conversation. The chip also stays after a server restart while a request is still waiting.
- **For you.** A helper's request left unanswered for a minute is added to For you ("Helper “…” needs your approval to use WebFetch"); clicking it opens the conversation at the card, and the item clears itself when the request is answered or withdrawn.
- **Stopped helpers say so.** A helper stopped while it was waiting shows "No longer waiting — the helper was stopped" instead of buttons; its card's chip reads "stopped" (hover: "Stopped before it finished") instead of "⟳ running", and a helper stopped mid-run keeps its title and says "Stopped before it finished" instead of the internal "The user doesn't want to proceed with this tool use…" text.
- **A server restart keeps it.** A request that was waiting is still a live card after a restart; one answered or withdrawn before it stays settled.
- **A request answered twice, or after the helper was stopped, sends nothing (verify r1).** Pressing Allow or Deny on a request that was already answered in the other window — or that the assistant withdrew when the helper was stopped — no longer sends a second answer to the assistant; the window says so ("Already answered — allowed. Nothing was sent."). And when a conversation is terminated or exits, any "Helper needs your approval" item it left in For you is cleared, and no such item is filed afterwards for it.
- **A page kept open across a server restart no longer loses the first half-second (verify r2, B-63f1 ②).** After a server restart every open chat window rebuilds itself a moment later (a short random delay so many windows do not all redraw at once). Anything the assistant or you wrote in that moment used to show up and then vanish when the window redrew — and it stayed gone until the next restart or a reload. Those records are now held and shown after the redraw, in order, nothing twice. Gates: test-reattach-stagger (fast, 19, with two pre-fix controls) and test-reattach-stagger-ui (heavy: 12 real restarts with the delay pinned to its maximum, 0 losses; the pre-fix build loses 6/6).
- **A helper's request in For you has no Reply box (verify r2).** Typing a reply on a "Helper … needs your approval" item never could approve anything (only the card's Allow / Deny reach the assistant), but it cleared the item while the helper was still waiting; the item now has no Reply box (clicking it goes to the card, where Allow / Deny are), and a reply sent anyway is refused by name ("Answer it on the helper’s card — click the item to go there") without clearing the item. An Allow pressed in a helper's log window left open from before a Terminate + Resume no longer reaches the resumed assistant (that request belonged to the ended process); the window says it did not reach the agent. An Allow pressed in the same instant a helper was stopped no longer reads "✓ Allowed": the assistant had already withdrawn the request and dropped the answer, so the card now says the helper was stopped. And a future Claude Code that tags the request with the helper's call (`parent_tool_use_id`) still lands the card on the parent chat (it was routed to the helper's log alone).
- **A helper's request now has exactly one life, whatever happens to it (verify r3).** Every earlier round found a situation the card or the For-you item did not know about (answered twice, a stopped helper, a killed conversation, two identical requests, an old window after a restart). The states a request can be in, the events that move it and what each move does are now one table (`src/helper-ask.js`), and every screen, the inbox and the answer path read it: an answer reaches the assistant at most once per request in any order of events; a request the assistant settled itself (its own result arrives with no answer from you — the request expired or was decided elsewhere) shows that outcome; a request whose helper has really finished says so instead of taking an answer that could never arrive; a killed conversation's requests say "the conversation ended"; a For-you reply on a helper's request is refused by the same rule. And the **one-minute For-you clock survives a server restart**: a request already waiting for 45 s when the server restarts is added to For you 15 s later, not a minute later; one already past a minute is added as soon as the conversation is rebuilt. Gates: test-helper-ask ⑪–⑰ (fast, 164: the table walked on its own — 36 seeds × 2000 steps — and on the REAL answer path with a fake assistant, 2 000 seeded steps with ~130 real rebuilds and the stdin frames counted per request; a restart matrix over six states; five table mutants and two consumer mutants as controls), test-helper-ask-ui (heavy, 44: the clock across a real restart).
- **A request the CLI gave up on reads "Denied", not "Allowed" (verify r4).** Claude Code 2.1.281 answers a WebFetch permission request nobody acted on for five minutes by itself, with a result that says the request was not answered in time; that result was read as an approval, so the helper's card (and a conversation's own card) said "✓ Allowed" for a request the CLI had denied. The CLI's own deadline sentence now reads as the denial it is, on both cards. **A takeover also interrupts a helper's pending browser request (verify r4, the owner's 2026-09-27 ruling).** When you take a browser over, a helper's waiting request to click, fill or navigate on that browser is answered stale like the conversation's own — judged by the browser the helper's commands actually run on (its own child browser when it opened one, else the conversation's). **A future ask shape is visible (verify r4).** A permission request the CLI sends in a form this version does not know (a new request subtype or a new field inside it) now raises the schema-drift card naming it, instead of vanishing while the chip says "waiting for you". **Quieter after a restart (verify r4).** The first lifecycle event after a restart no longer re-announces an unchanged "waiting" set, and a restart no longer rewrites an unchanged request-clock map when two requests arrived in the same tick. Gates: test-helper-ask 188 (the real-engine walk now counts EVERY effect per step — stdin, For-you store writes, card ops, chip ops, meta writes — against the table, with two engine mutants the old oracle could not see), test-record-shape, test-browser-takeover.
- **A helper's refusal reads "Denied", an interrupted or expired request reads "Not run", and a result VibeSpace cannot read says so (verify r5).** The words a permission card ends with now come from a table of the sentences Claude Code itself writes when a request is refused, interrupted, dropped at a resume or left unanswered — read from the CLI's own list inside the 2.1.281 binary — instead of "anything that is not the familiar rejection sentence counts as allowed". Every helper's refusal used to fall on the wrong side of that rule (a helper's refusal is worded differently from the main assistant's) and showed "✓ Allowed" whenever the helper's own result was the only witness; so did "[Request interrupted by user for tool use]" and the request Claude Code retires two seconds into a resumed turn. A result outside the table now reads "Ended — reason unknown" (never "Allowed"), the request leaves the waiting list, and one card per conversation names the sentence so the next CLI version's new wording is visible. A fetch of a page not mentioned in your messages, which Claude Code asks about a second time with a fresh id, now shows that second request on the fetch's card (it used to be invisible and was refused by the CLI after five minutes); a helper's second request is settled by its result too. The release gate reads the CLI's own list and fails, naming the sentence, the day a build adds one; the answer side has one builder of the reply frame, with the CLI's accepted shape pinned.
- Measured on Claude Code 2.1.281 (one real turn): the helper's request arrives on the conversation's own stream with the helper's id and is answered on the conversation's own input — see docs/kb-bugfix-invariants.md. Gates: test-helper-ask (fast, 212 after verify r5, with its patched-copy controls), test-helper-ask-ui (heavy, 42, with a pre-lane control).

### Lane R4 — a channel account (a rule's conversations, one conversation) is shared with SEVERAL agents in two separate steps: first access (who may see and act), then notification (who is woken) — access alone never wakes anyone; and an agent can write a NEW email


The owner, on 2.369.185's account menu 交给一个 agent…: "只能交给一个agent吗？不能给多个？不能只给读取权限不做推送/汇总？" — and then: "你之前的交互的问题是把'让agent能访问对话'和'让agent会被通知'耦合在一起了", "这实际上应该是两种不同的操作，前者是后者的前提". And: "给我一个agent使用我的 gmail 的能力，让它能读取和发送邮件".

- **Grant access… first.** The account's ⋯ menu, a conversation's menu and a rule's line offer 授权访问… (Grant access…): a list of agents and Task Groups, each with its authority — 起草 (you approve every send) or 可发送 (sends directly where the channel's policy allows). As many as you like; Add / Remove. Access lets them see the conversations and act on them (read, search, refresh, reply). **Access alone never wakes anyone** — nothing is billed on its behalf.
- **Then Notify….** 通知… (Notify…) lists who is WOKEN, and on what — one row per agent or group, picked only from those that already have access there (with nobody yet it says 先授权访问 and opens Grant access… for you). Each row keeps the familiar fields: every message or a filter, a wake per batch or one digest per window, wakes per day at most, the receipt option, and its own estimate; the dialog adds them up. Removing someone's access removes their notification too, and the dialog says so before you save. A number past its limit is now said where you typed it ("已保持在最大值 1440") instead of silently changing.
- **The card says both.** "访问：A（可发送）, 组 · 工作（起草） · 通知：A 每批唤醒 按过滤器" — on the account card, on every conversation row it covers (dim, "(account)" / "(rule)") and on the conversation window's chip. The old 交给一个 agent… entry is gone.
- **Several agents never share one budget.** Each notification has its own daily cap, its own held messages and its own digest window; two agents watching the same account each get exactly their own number of wakes, even when one pass brings news to a hundred conversations. One batch never wakes the same session twice (an agent named directly and a group it belongs to). A woken agent is told who else is on the conversation, so two agents do not both answer.
- **For agents:** `vibespace-channels status` now says what you were given — access (and its authority) and whether you are notified ("not notified — nothing wakes you"); `list` shows the two separately; `search "…"` searches the conversations you can see; `compose <account> --to … --subject "…" "text"` proposes a NEW email (Gmail) on an account you have whole — the same approval rules as a reply (review by default; sends directly only when the account's policy is direct, you have 可发送 and no link or attachment is involved); a channel that cannot start a conversation (Lark) says so by name, and an account without the send permission creates nothing. The manual (vibespace-docs channels) explains access vs notification.
- **Existing hand-offs are kept.** Each becomes one access row plus one notification row for the same agent or group (its wake count carried over) — migration `2026-09-channels-access-watchers`, run once at startup.
- **A group you just created no longer vanishes from the Grant access… and Reach lists on a slow page (verify r1).** Two requests for the Task Group list are in flight when a page opens; when one of them finished after the list had already been updated by the server's broadcast, its older copy replaced the newer one and the pickers went empty until the next change. The page now keeps the newer list. Gate: test-tasks-mirror-race (heavy: the interleaving constructed, 20 loads at CPU ×12, a control bundle without the guard).
- **Gmail replies were about to be refused by Google (verify r1).** A reply on Gmail is created as a draft and then sent, and Google's own method table lets `drafts.create` / `drafts.send` run only under `gmail.compose` (or modify / mail.google.com) — never under `gmail.send`, the scope the Connect step asked for. Connect (and Re-authorize) now ask for `gmail.compose`, which covers both replies and new messages; a Gmail account signed in under the older permission can still write new messages, says `send-scope-not-granted` on replies, and the sentence asks you to re-authorize "to allow drafts and sending". A composed new message also carries an `X-VibeSpace-Proposal` header so that Check outcome can find it in your Sent mail even if Gmail rewrote its Message-ID. And the first direct send on a conversation whose send capability had never been looked up no longer falls back to review — the authority is judged on the capability the proposal itself just resolved (engine).
- **A removed agent never receives a message that was on its way (verify r2).** If you remove an agent's access while a notification for it is already being delivered and the delivery is refused (a spending limit, a busy session), the message is no longer kept for that agent's next turn — it is dropped, and the account's log says so.
- **Receipts count against the same daily cap (verify r2).** When an agent's notification is set to wake it on the outcome of its own drafts, those wakes now count against its daily wake cap like any other; over the cap the receipt still reaches it on its next turn, and the card shows the cap as the reason.
- **A `compose` with a Bcc is refused, not quietly sent without it (verify r2).** `vibespace-channels compose` carries To / Cc only; a request naming a Bcc or a reply target is refused by name.
- **A notification row without access is inert (verify r2).** Should a hand-edited store hold a notification for an agent that has no access at that grain, it never wakes anyone; the server names such rows once at boot.
- **Receipts are paced one at a time (verify r3).** Rejecting (or expiring) several of an agent's drafts at once used to wake it once per receipt regardless of its daily cap — five billed turns under a cap of 2 — because each receipt read the cap before the delivery and wrote it after; a receipt now waits its turn behind the agent's other wakes and reads the cap there, so the cap holds under any number of simultaneous rejects.
- **A group member that dies mid-notification does not lose the message (verify r3).** When the session a Task Group's notification was sent to ended while the delivery was under way, the message was dropped as if the group's access had been removed; it is now held for the group and the next notification wakes another live member with it (the account's log says `member-gone`).
- **Every notification wake goes through one door (verify r4).** Four verify rounds each found a new place that could start a billed turn beside the one serialized path. The engine now has exactly one entry for a billed channel turn — the wake, the digest and the receipt all reserve their ledger row before the turn is asked for and settle it after — and a test counts every such site in the source, so a fifth one cannot appear unnoticed. Under 50 simultaneous messages across five conversations of one account with a daily cap of 3 (with ten receipts arriving at the same time, a digest closing, or a Task Group of five) exactly three turns are billed and the rest wait.
- **A restart no longer starts turns on its way out (verify r4).** A wake queued behind one in flight when the server stopped used to run anyway — a billed turn into a process about to exit — and the messages a stopped wake set aside were dropped with the closing store. Now they wait on disk and go out after the restart.
- **A ledger that cannot be written holds, it never bills (verify r4).** If the notification ledger could not be written (a full disk, a blocked store), every wake was billed and the daily cap never counted. Now a wake whose ledger row cannot be written is held with its reason, and a row written but not settled still counts against the cap.
- **A crash no longer holds a notification's daily cap for a day (verify r5).** A wake reserves its place in the daily count before it is delivered; if the server died between the reservation and the delivery, that place stayed taken for 24 hours even though nothing was ever sent. A fresh start now frees a previous run's stuck reservations, so the agent is woken again; a reservation from the running server is never touched.
- **A digest set to zero wakes a day is refused, and an old one still delivers (verify r5).** Setting a digest notification to a daily cap of 0 (which could never deliver — a digest is itself a paced wake) is now refused with a plain sentence; a digest saved with 0 before this is read as 1 so it still delivers once per window, and the server names any such row once at startup.
- **One malformed message no longer drops a whole conversation's notifications (verify r5).** If a single incoming record could not be matched against a filter, the conversation's other messages and other agents' notifications for that batch were lost silently; each record and each notification is now handled on its own, and a failure is logged by name and skipped.
- Gates: test-channel-filter, test-channels-engine ⑪ (r3: (h) five concurrent rejects, (i) the member dying mid-wake; r5: (l) one bad record, (m) a crash's stuck reservation, (n) a cap-0 digest — each with a patched-copy control), test-channels-aggregate ⑨c/⑨d, test-channel-acl, test-migrations, test-channels-agent-cli, test-channels-gmail-shape ⑧ (the scope table) / ⑧b (fast); test-channels-aggregate-ui ⑤/⑦, test-channels-e2e ⑮, test-channels-i18n (heavy). Design: docs/design-communication-panel §24.

### Lane dserve-bound — the desktop-serve gate's "answered at once" checks read the launcher's own wait instead of a stopwatch (the 2.369.189 mirror red: 1002 ms on a slow runner against a literal 1000)


The Actions mirror of 2.369.189 failed one check of test-desktop-serve — a runner that cannot take the install lock must be reported at once — because the launcher answered in 1002 ms on a busy 2-CPU runner and the check said "under 1000 ms". The product was right: the launcher's wait for the runner had polled once, and the rest was starting a handful of shells on a slow machine. The check now proves what it meant — the wait ended because the runner died (no pidfile, no exit file, fewer polls than the wait's cap, counted) — with a time bound derived from the launcher's own wait (half its 10 s cap, read from the module), and every other stopwatch bound in the suite was converted the same way (evidence first; a bound only from the constant it is about).

### Integration (the three lanes on one tree)

- **A digest's open window is no longer drawn as "held" (the R3 × R4 seam, backlog B-adb7 (a)).** 2.369.190's first screen called a conversation held (amber "→ X · held") whenever ANY message waited on it — but with R4 a digest notification keeps its matches waiting on the conversation until its window closes, by design. The server now says for whom each waiting message waits (`touch.pendingFor`), and the first screen counts a digest's messages as held only once its window has closed with them still waiting; a single conversation handed over on its own keeps its "→ X" (b). Gate: test-channels-focus ⑦ (a nine-row table, the real engine — a digest hit pending ⇒ no tag, 61 min later ⇒ amber — and two patched-copy controls: the pre-seam "any pending is held" rule, and a tag rule that does not pass the watchers).
- **R3's first-screen checks follow R4's model.** An account-grain and a rule-grain notification now both fire on a conversation both cover (another agent's rule never silences the account-wide one), so test-channels-focus ② expects three deliveries (Room 44 wakes the rule's agent AND the account's), and test-channels-aggregate-ui runs R3's checks (the account's conversations not listed for the hand-over alone; an agent's read lists exactly one, tagged) after R4's rewritten ⑤.
- **Merged by hand:** src/server/channels-engine.js (R4's rewritten wake / digest / receipt paths keep R3's facts — the wake names whom it reached, `touchView`, the one-shot `healSelfAt` — and 2.369.188's `kind: 'notification'` on every stash), the i18n dictionaries (union), the For-you producer census (15 sites: + the helper-ask item, + the composed-message pointer), the design's R4 section renumbered §24 (R3 holds §23).
- **Three heavy suites pinned what lane S1 changed (test-only).** test-fold-ux's swap census counted every `.replaceWith(` in chat-view — it now names both: the one message-element swap and S1's agent-chip patch (a chip inside a helper card's label, never a message element). test-tool-progress read the subagent branch's old spelling (it now also refuses control records). test-queue-steer's stamp pin follows the stagger into `_armViewReset`, and its ⑭b experiment gains a layer: S1's reset hold removes the same race on its own, so the PRE-FIX arm strips BOTH the recency guard and the hold (else it reproduces nothing), the recency guard is proven alone with the hold removed, and a third arm runs the whole product (the held payload first, the answer after, the row kept).
- **Gates on this tree:** npm run build (i18n-check 5259 zh / 5259 ja); fast tier 183 suites green in 1011 s (test-helper-ask 212, test-reattach-stagger 19, test-desktop-serve 198, test-channels-focus 160, test-channels-engine 257, test-channels-aggregate 296, test-user-todos-layout 190); the heavy tier's verdict is recorded in the release commit.

## 2.369.190 — the Channels panel opens on what needs you or an agent, each row with one small tag, and a Lark picture is shown as a picture; the Agent browser's live picture fits its window, and the phone gets a real live view

### Lane R3 — a Lark picture is shown as a picture; the Channels panel opens on what needs you or an agent, each row with one small tag, the full list one switch away

The owner, 2026-09-26, on 2.369.185 (docs/design-communication-panel §23): "lark图像不能预览吗？" (a Lark picture came out as the text "[image]" and a bare "image ⬇" chip) and "开头不要把所有消息都放进来，很多是没用的，建议只放重要消息/conversation（比如推送给agent了的，或者某个agent刚刚读取了的），并展示一个小tag表示状态。" (the panel opened on all 879 conversations).

**Pictures.**
- A picture in a Lark message (a picture on its own, or inside a rich-text post) is drawn as a thumbnail in the conversation window, fetched on demand through our own route and cached. Its "[image]" text line disappears once the picture is drawn (agents and search still see it). Clicking it opens the usual image viewer. A rich-text post wrapped in a language key (`zh_cn` …) now yields both its text and its pictures.
- **A picture that cannot be drawn says why.** Before, any failure silently turned the thumbnail into an "image ⬇" chip. Now:
  - If waiting fixes it (this minute's vendor budget is spent, the vendor asked us to back off, or it rate-limited us), the thumbnail shows "retrying in N s" and loads itself again, at most twice.
  - Otherwise the chip names the reason ("budget spent", "forbidden", "not found", "not cached", "vendor error" …), puts the full sentence in its tooltip and offers **Retry**.
  - A file that is not a displayable picture (HEIC …) becomes a download chip marked "no preview".
  - Every failure is reported to telemetry (`chan-attachment-failed`).
- **The picture's fetch stays cheap.**
  - Nothing is fetched while a conversation is ingested, only when a window shows the picture.
  - A cached picture is served even when the minute's budget is spent.
  - Five thumbnails asking for the same picture at once make one vendor request and one charge.
  - A picture the vendor refused is not asked for again for 10 minutes. Your Retry skips that wait; it never skips the budget.
  - A vendor rate limit pauses the whole account's picture fetches, not just that one picture.
  - A picture older than the newest 5000 messages is found through its own message.
  - A cache hit no longer rewrites the cache ledger (writes are grouped every 5 s and flushed on shutdown).
- The picture fetch is now explicitly allowlisted: scripts/test-vendor-whitelist.mjs §7 is a census that reads the source and names three gates (fetched on demand, cache checked first, charged to the budget). Four ungated patched copies each turn it red.

**The first screen.**
- The Channels panel now opens on the conversations that **need attention**. A conversation is listed when any of these holds:
  - an agent's draft awaits your approval, or a send's result is unknown;
  - it is handed to an agent or a Task Group on its own (a conversation handed over by a rule or with its whole account is listed only once a wake for it was delivered to the agent in the last 24 h, or its wake is held — see r2 below);
  - an agent read it in the last 24 h;
  - a wake for it is held;
  - you replied in it in the last 24 h.

  Your agent groups are always listed too.
- Each listed conversation shows **one small tag** in place of its source label, under the title at every width. The tags are "N to approve", "send unknown", "→ Agent" (amber when its wake was held), "Agent read 5m ago", "New since Agent", "last wake held" and "replied 3h ago". The agent's name is the part that shortens when space is tight; the words always stay whole.
- The header is a two-way switch across the whole bar — "N need attention" | "All 879". The row under it holds a **Filter** box, New group and Outbox (the two buttons moved down so the switch is never cut). In the attention view, matches outside it are offered as "N more in All", and any filter text can also start a message search across every connected account.
- Behind this, an agent's read (the `vibespace-channels read` route) is now recorded on the conversation (who, when, up to which message) and sent as a one-row update. A hidden read is never recorded, and re-reading the same messages within a minute records nothing new. Each wake records which agent it reached. Your own newest message comes from messages the vendor marks as yours or from your own send; conversations active in the last two days get it from their recent history once, at startup. Conversations nothing touched carry no extra data.
- Gates:
  - New fast suites **test-channels-images** (61) and **test-channels-focus** (116; 148 after r2).
  - Extended: test-channels-lark-shape (84 → 94, the resource request), test-vendor-whitelist (64 → 91, §7), test-channels-groups-ui (61 → 62).
- Verify r1 (the adversarial pass, same day): two ways of fetching every picture at ingest slipped both money gates green — an internal `attachment()` call queued for the next tick (the whitelist census only knew four receiver names, and the images suite's "no bytes at ingest" pin counted before the tick) and a wiring file's own `engine.attachment(`. The census now counts every `.attachment(` in the server tree and every bare `attachment(` in the engine, the pin settles first, and both mutants are its controls. A tag whose agent arrived without a display name showed the raw session id; it now says "an agent" / "a Task Group".
  - Heavy: test-channels-aggregate-ui ②b (a Lark-shaped picture, the overlay, a rate-limited picture that loads on its own retry, a refused picture's zh chip with Retry; after r2: the account-grain rows NOT on the attention list until an agent reads one), test-channels-groups-e2e ⑨ (5 handed over / 3 read by an agent through its real agent route / 1 awaiting among 51, the header counts, All, the filter in both views, one column at 375 px), test-channels-e2e ⑰ (every tag's words fit line 2 in en/zh/ja under both fonts, with a control), test-channels-i18n (the attention list shot).
- r2 (2026-09-27, the integrator's ruling D4): **handing a whole account, or the conversations matching a rule, to an agent no longer puts every one of them on the first screen** — the owner's 824-thread mailbox handed to an agent would have filled it again, the exact thing he asked to stop. Such a conversation is listed only once the hand-over acted on it: a wake for it was delivered to the agent in the last 24 h (tagged "→ Agent", the tooltip saying "with the whole account" / "by a rule"), or its wake is held (amber). Otherwise it is listed only for its own facts (an agent read, your reply, a draft awaiting approval). A conversation handed over on its own is listed as before. test-channels-focus 116 → 148 (the account + rule grains in every state, the spec fixture now 3 conversations + the account + a rule ⇒ 7 listed, one delivered wake per grain ⇒ 9, and two patched-copy controls: the grain check removed puts all 50 back, a delivered wake with no window never leaves); test-channels-aggregate-ui's account-grain leg now proves the opposite (none listed, then one after a stub agent reads it). The test-channels-gmail-shape suite now removes its scratch directory on every exit (it left one per run — 245 on the gate machine).

### Lane S4 — the agent's live view fits its window, and the phone gets a real one (naive-user study 2)

Study 2 (2026-09-26, all three testers): "实况画面只占窗格上面一截" — on the desktop the live picture used only the top 40–60 % of its pane, black below; "手机上的实况窗口" — on a 390 px phone "网页按桌面宽度缩成顶上约 260 像素的一小条，下面全空，Pricing 链接只有 20 像素宽", no pinch, the live view did not open when the assistant started browsing, and the only way in was a status-bar chip "整个在屏幕外" (x≈403 of 390); and a live view "一片白，网址栏写着 example.org、助手说已打开".

- **The page is laid out at the size of the window you watch it in.** While a live view is open, the agent's page takes the size of the view's pane, so the picture fills it exactly — a split pane 700×900 shows a 700×900 page, not a shrunk 1280-wide one with a black band. Resize the window and the page follows. With several views of one browser, the one whose person is driving decides, otherwise the largest one on screen (a hidden one never counts); the others show the same page scaled to fit, never stretched, and say "Sized for another window". When nobody has watched for 5 seconds the page goes back to its own size. A size the agent chose itself (`set viewport` / `set device`) is never overridden — the view scales it, says "Agent's size W×H", and "Fit the page to the window" takes it back. New setting *Lay the agent's page out at the live view's size* (`browser.fitPageToView`, on by default).
- **On a phone the live view is a real one.** The page renders at the phone's width (the Pricing link is its normal size, and tapping it works); it opens by itself, full screen, when the agent starts browsing in the conversation you are looking at, with "Back to the chat" in the notice; two fingers zoom the picture while you watch (one finger pans, a double tap zooms 2×) and your taps land where you see them when you drive; the status bar's "Agent browser" chip stays on screen however you swipe the bar. Notices with a button are no longer squeezed into half a phone screen.
- **No more blank picture under a loaded URL.** A page that painted twice in quick succession and then sat still could leave a viewer with its first (white) paint for good — the last frame is now always delivered. After a navigation the stream sent no picture for (a jump within the page), VibeSpace asks the page for one. If a view still has no picture it says "Waiting for a picture…" after 2 seconds (the old picture dimmed) and "No picture came in 10 s" with a Reconnect after 10.
- Measured on the real agent-browser 0.38.1 (scripts/fixtures/browser-stream/fit-0.38.1.json): a set viewport makes every frame that size; a device scale factor never enlarges the frame and changing it on a still page produced no frame at all (the fit keeps factor 1 — "DPR-aware" means the pane is measured in CSS px, so a DPR-3 phone gets a 390-wide page); a headed window cannot be narrower than 500 px (the view fits it there and says so); a jump within the page sends a new URL and no frame. PURE src/browser-fit.js; the bridge (src/server/browser-stream.js) sets the page through `keeper.setViewportFor` (the daemon's own `set viewport`, never starting a browser) and takes fresh pictures with `keeper.freshFrameFor` (src/server/browser-viewport.js `captureFrame`). Gates: test-browser-fit (fast, 116 — six patched-copy controls: device px, no holder rule, no trailing frame, no own-mirror recognition, no fresh frame, no re-check of a restarted browser) + test-browser-live-fit (heavy, 40 — the real 0.38.1 through a scratch instance, a desktop and a phone client: pane = frame ±2 px with a pixel census and its control, auto-open, the link, the pinch, the chip and its control, the waiting sentences, the viewer rule). The chrome suites' fake agent-browsers answer `set viewport`; lane J's letterbox legs run with the new setting off.

- **Verify r1 (the adversarial pass on this lane).** Two viewport sets in flight at once — the agent's own `set viewport` and the view's fit — are now told apart by the ORDER the browser processed them in, never by the size asked for: the agent's choice landing first is put back if the fit landed after it, and landing second it is announced as the agent's, never as "fitted". The 5 s restore waits for a running turn to end (no reflow under the agent's feet). The agent's choice and the size to restore to survive a server restart (a note on the browser's own record, gone when the browser relaunches). A live view on another virtual desktop stops voting (it kept the page at its size before). On a phone, a second browsing conversation's live view opened below the screen — an earlier split window was still displayed under the active one; only the active window is displayed now.

- **Verify r1, continued.** The same order rule also holds when the browser's record of the two commands arrives after the view's own command has already returned (both late: judged when ours lands; ours late: still recognised as ours, never taken for the agent's choice). A size the page did not take is said once in the view ("the page did not take the size") instead of being believed silently, and not asked again for 30 s. An agent-chosen width narrower than a headed browser's 500 px floor is no longer forgotten on a reconnect. The view's own resizes now appear in the agent browser's action trace as a "page size" row (`live view: set viewport W H (fit | restore | put-back)`), so the agent's clicks before and after a reflow are told apart; the agent's own `set viewport` stays an untraced observation.

## 2.369.189 — a browser profile with a name is usable by all your conversations — one browser, a second chat joins it in its own tab, and the Agent browser window says who can use it, with Rename… and Delete… (owner ruling A); an account on paid overage credits wears a money icon instead of a sentence (the owner: "这啥玩意啊 不如显示个钱的图标"); and the 2.369.187 / 2.369.188 mirror red was the release gate's own sample, not the browser release

### Lane S5 — a named browser profile is usable by all your conversations (owner ruling A, 2026-09-26, "A吧")

- **A named browser profile is usable by all your conversations (owner ruling A, 2026-09-26 — "A吧" = 有名字的档案默认给所有对话用).** Two naive-user studies failed the same task: a login made in one chat could not be used from another (`not_owner`, and the only way out offered was a command line that made a second, still-refused profile), and pinning the profile to the second chat in Session properties started a second Chrome on the profile's folder ("SingletonLock" in the live view) and then silently fell back to a temporary browser. Now:
  - **Every named profile is shared by default** — the ones you create in the Agent browser window, the ones an agent creates with `vibespace-browser new`, and "New persistent profile from this session's browser". A profile runs **one** browser: a second conversation joins it in its own tab; nothing ever starts a second Chrome on its folder.
  - **Pinning a profile to a conversation (New Session, Session properties) makes it that conversation's default browser** — its next browser command opens it (joining the running one), nothing is relaunched, and if it cannot open, the agent is told so by name (never a silent temporary browser). Your pick is the permission: it works even on a profile kept to another conversation, and your latest choice wins.
  - **One conversation drives a shared browser at a time.** While another chat's agent is working in it, a command is refused `browser_busy` naming that chat and how long to wait at most; while you drive it from another chat's live view, it says so. The live view's strip shows a shared profile's tab and names who is driving it.
  - **The Agent browser window's profile row** gains **Who can use it** (All my conversations / Only <a conversation> — narrowing takes it from every other chat, after a confirmation that says how many), **Rename…**, and **Delete…** (warns how many conversations use it, takes it from each, stops it, clears every pin, and keeps its logins under "Deleted profiles (kept aside)" until you press Delete permanently). The isolation chip reads "separate tabs".
  - **Refusals name a button, never a command line** (`not_owner`: "switch it to All my conversations in the Agent browser panel, or pick it for this conversation in Session properties"; a conversation's own browser from before this version holding the folder: "press Stop on that browser").
  - A shared browser counts toward the limit of each conversation that holds it, and once toward the machine's ceiling; joining a running browser never trips the machine ceiling.
  - Migration `2026-09-browser-profiles-all-conversations` makes every agent-made profile usable by all conversations (the conversation that made it is kept as its creator). Live sessions pinned before this version stop handing their own browser the profile's folder at boot.
  - Gates: test-browser-share-model (fast, 70 — the PURE tables + the real keeper and routes over a fake 0.38.1, with patched-copy controls: the pre-ruling route dying on SingletonLock, a silent-fallback route, a keeper without the one-driver check), test-browser-share (heavy, 21 — the real agent-browser 0.38.1 + a real Chrome: two conversations, one Chrome on the folder, `browser_busy` through the CLI, a takeover through the real live-view bridge, the switch's button refusal, Delete… with two pins, the migration on a pre-ruling registry), test-migrations (+ the migration leg); flipped asserts in test-browser-pin, -handles, -mediation and test-profile-blindness. Docs: design-agent-browser-v2 §3.2.6 (+ §3.2.5 / §3.3 / §6.2 / §11), the agent manual, kb-file-structure, kb-features, kb-bugfix-invariants.
  - **Verify S5 (adversarial, real 0.38.1 + Chrome; three fixed on the branch):** (1) MAJOR — a **fork** of a pinned conversation said "Pinned: work" in Session properties while its bare commands opened a temporary browser, silently (the ladder's 'conversation' rung was never recorded under the fork's NEW key, and no directory rides the spawn env any more): the keeper's `copyPin(parent, fork)` copies the parent's pin verbatim (its `by`/`at` — never a laundered authorization) and ws-create calls it on the fork branch. (2) MEDIUM — a live view a conversation had open on a profile the user then kept to ANOTHER conversation ("Only …") could still take it over and refuse the holder's agent `browser_busy` "the user drives it from <that chat>": `keeper.takeover` of a named profile now needs that conversation's lease (`no_lease`, naming the Session-properties button), and the bridge ends every view on a lease that goes (a typed "no longer holds that browser profile" — no stale picture). (3) MEDIUM — the migration treated an unreadable / torn `browser-profiles.json` as "no file" (ran, ledger stamped forever): only ENOENT is nothing-to-migrate; anything else fails by name and is retried at the next boot. Gates: test-browser-share-model 70 → 77, test-browser-share 21 → 26 (③b: the narrowing under a takeover from the other chat's real live view), test-migrations 210 → 213 (a torn registry, a `null` file, the file whole again). Held (pre-existing, measured on master): after a lane-H relaunch the agent's next verb is the binary's `tab_gone` until `vibespace-browser tab new <url>`; a killed driver frees the drive after DRIVE_HOLD_MS (90 s), its lease after the 2-min carrier grace.

### Lane credits-icon — an account on paid overage credits wears a money icon, not a sentence (the owner on the Agents roster: "这啥玩意啊 不如显示个钱的图标")

The owner, looking at a member row of the Agents roster that read 正在使用付费溢出额度 beside its next-usable countdown: "这啥玩意啊 不如显示个钱的图标" — "what is this thing? better show a money icon".

## 2.369.188 — text meant for the assistant is no longer shown as conversation: VibeSpace's own reminders are one grey line folded by default, a browser you hand back reads "VibeSpace · you handed control back …" instead of a message from another agent, and no agent can pass itself off as VibeSpace (naive-user study 2)

Two findings of naive-user study 2 (fresh-eyes testers driving a scratch instance): "聊天里到处是给助手看的内部文字" — the chat was full of text written for the assistant — and "交回控制后，助手以为是另一个会话在跟它说话" — after a browser hand-back the assistant believed another session was talking to it.

- **The chat no longer shows text meant for the assistant as if it were conversation** (naive-user study 2: "聊天里到处是给助手看的内部文字"). VibeSpace's end-of-turn reminder, its tools intro and its per-turn reminder each show as one grey line — "VibeSpace reminded the assistant to update its status" — folded by default with the status call they asked for; expand to read the text, or turn them off entirely in Settings → Chat → "Show VibeSpace notes to the assistant" (the assistant still receives them). The reminder now asks for the bookkeeping calls only: "do not restate your answer; end with at most one short line", so the assistant stops repeating its answer ("Task complete — …") or telling you "Status is set to done …". A helper's launch line reads "Helper started: Fetch title of example.com" and a Stop task result "Stopped: Fetch title of example.com" instead of "Async agent launched successfully. (This tool result is internal metadata — never quote…" and raw JSON (the raw record is still behind the expander).
- **VibeSpace's own notes are never mistaken for another agent** (naive-user study 2: "交回控制后，助手以为是另一个会话在跟它说话"). When you hand the browser back, the chat card reads "VibeSpace · you handed control back after 17 s — the page is now …" instead of `Message from " VibeSpace browser "` (the stray spaces are gone too; what the assistant was told sits one click away), and the note the assistant receives opens with "VibeSpace (this workspace, not another agent) reports:" — the same for Background Work and channel notifications. VibeSpace's own chat cards (the auto-resume notice, the usage-limit card with its reset-credit button) are titled "VibeSpace · …" too instead of `Message from "VibeSpace"`. Messages from real agents keep their card.
- **An agent cannot pass itself off as VibeSpace** (verify: an agent could send "VibeSpace (this workspace, not another agent) reports: …" and get the accent VibeSpace card). Whether a card is a VibeSpace notice is now decided by the path the message took, never by what it says or what its sender is called: an agent whose message opens with VibeSpace's own sentence keeps its "Message from “name”" card, and an agent or session named "VibeSpace", "VibeSpace browser", "Background Work · …" or "Channels · …" (in any capitalization or spacing) is shown as "Message from an agent calling itself “VibeSpace”". The assistant is not fooled either: a message held for a closed conversation reaches it as `from "<name>":` unless VibeSpace itself sent it, and VibeSpace's own sentence is said once, never twice.
- **"Your inbox" is named where it is.** A new For-you item pops a toast "Added to For you (bottom right)" (the corner where the button actually sits on your screen), and assistants are taught to say "the For you tray at the bottom right" instead of "your inbox". The Settings row now reads "Agent tool: vibespace-ask (the For you tray)", a notification delivered to you says it went to "the For you tray", and the agent manual and the vibespace-ask help say "the For you tray only notifies".
- Gates: test-chat-hygiene (fast: the note / sentence / notice tables over the real producers' words, the Stop wording and its byte budget, the sender-name census, the impersonation table over the real ladder and the claude / codex / ACP normalizers, the census that every card and stash writer states its path, the "your inbox" census, eight patched-copy controls), test-chat-hygiene-ui (heavy: a stub claude behind the real chat-wrapper playing the study's records in chrome — and a peer named "VibeSpace" plus a peer whose words open with VibeSpace's sentence, live and from the held-message drain), test-migrations (a saved "Card kinds that collapse" selection gains the new kind once).

## 2.369.187 — handing a whole account (or the conversations a rule matches) to an agent with a filter saves again (the owner's toast "请求被拒绝: mode 'filtered' needs a filterId")

The owner, handing a Lark account to the group 工作 with 匹配过滤器的消息 (two time windows), one digest per window and 起草, pressed 保存 and got the toast `请求被拒绝: mode 'filtered' needs a filterId` — nothing was saved.

- **A filtered hand-off saves.** "Hand the whole account to an agent" and "Conversations matching a rule" save *messages matching a filter* again: the server stores the filter you built in the dialog and the assignment points at it (every such save was refused since 2.369.185; *every message* was unaffected). Re-opening the dialog shows your rules and saving again replaces them.
- **A refused save says what to fix, in your language.** A filter that is still incomplete, a missing agent, a negative wakes-per-day number and the like now read as a sentence about the dialog (e.g. 过滤器还没保存 — 请先添加规则，再保存), never as the server's internal English message.
- Cause: the server checked the assignment for a filter id before creating the filter the same request carried. Gates: test-channels-engine ⑩ (fast: the owner's exact request at both grains through the real routes, eight refusals worded by their code, a patched copy with the old order as the control), test-channel-filter, test-channels-aggregate-ui ⑦ (heavy: the owner's dialog in the browser).

## 2.369.186 — a window you pick by name is shown, even when it is the first tab of a tab group (inc-muiq348r-jwb5)

The owner, on an Android phone: "我在手机上怎么切换不到 vibespace 大开发这个 session？" — "VibeSpace 主开发" was the first (host) window of a tab group made on a desktop, with "Project B 大开发" on show; tapping its row in the phone's window switcher left Project B on screen while the title bar said 主开发.

- **Picking a window by name shows it.** The phone's window switcher (tap the title), a sidebar card, Ctrl+K, the taskbar window list and grouped chooser, Switch window, go-to / find, and re-opening Settings, Usage or any other one-of-a-kind window now switch its tab group to THAT window — the group's first window included — restore a minimized group and bring it forward. Before, only the group's other tabs could be picked this way; picking the first one raised the group on whatever tab it showed.
- **A click on the group keeps its tab.** Clicking or tapping a tab group's own title bar or the content on show keeps that tab and makes it the active window (the phone's title, highlight and close button used to name the hidden first window after any tap into the other tab's content).
- **Find window across desktops keeps your active window** (verify r1). Locating a tab of a group that lives on another desktop sets that group to show the tab there, without making the hidden window the active one — Ctrl+\ x, the taskbar highlight and the phone's title keep naming the window in front of you. (The same slip existed before for a group's other tabs; the one door now keeps it for every tab.)
- **The switch syncs like a tab click.** It is saved and sent exactly as a tab click is; another open client keeps showing its own tab. The phone switcher also lists a minimized group's other tabs under *Minimized*.
- One door: `WindowManager.revealWindow` (PURE `revealTab` / `pressTab` in src/lib/chain-layout.js). Gates: test-chain-layout ⑬ (fast, the verdict tables + two patched-copy controls), test-architecture §62 (fast, the census: every `.focusWindow(` / `wm.restore(` call in src/lib is a listed raise-only site, every naming door counted, four negative controls), test-split-ux 13 (heavy: the sidebar card, window list, palette and go-to on a desktop page; the switcher at 448×850, DPR 3, touch, Android UA; a desktop and a phone control with the door neutered reproduce the incident).
- **The Communication panel's freshness pill is always drawn whole.** 2.369.185's Actions mirror went red because, in the runner's font (DejaVu Sans, about 10 % wider than this machine's Noto Sans), "refresh paused" came out as "refresh pau…" in the 188 px panel; a CSS cap ellipsized every pill wider than 82 px. Now the pill never shrinks and the conversation title gives way instead (the full title stays in its tooltip). The pill uses short words: a paused conversation says "paused" (已暂停 / 一時停止中) and one that has never been scanned says "no scan yet" (尚未扫描 / 未スキャン). The full sentence ("refresh paused", "not scanned yet") stays in the pill's tooltip. This also fixes pills that were cut on every machine: English "not scanned yet", Japanese "まだスキャンしていません" (cut to "まだスキャンし…"), and "refresh paused" / "not scanning" / 还没有扫描过 in a linked account's ↳ rows, which are 17 px narrower. test-channels-e2e ⑯ now checks every word the pill can show (zh/ja/en, at most 82 px) in both a normal and a ↳ row, plus a pill with the longest sentence. Each check runs twice: in this machine's font and with DejaVu Sans forced. The control is the pre-fix product (the old CSS as a scratch copy plus the old words as a mutant module): it cuts "refresh paused" at 82 of 89 px in DejaVu Sans and draws it whole in Noto Sans, which reproduces the mirror-only failure on this machine.

## 2.369.185 — a linked channel account is an aggregated IM: every conversation of a linked Lark or Gmail account is listed and fetched (no Track step), read with its images and attachments, searched and marked read; refresh follows activity (30 s / 5 min / 15 min at most) with your own per-conversation override; an agent may refresh a conversation itself within named limits; and a whole account, one conversation or the conversations matching a rule can be handed to an agent

The owner, 2026-09-26 (docs/design-communication-panel §5 invariant 6, §6.2, §6.5, §7.3): once linked, the Channels panel is "an IM that aggregates all my IMs — I read the messages, download attachments, view images in it; on top of that I can hand the whole account, or one channel / chat / the chats matching a pattern, to a specific agent"; the old Track-first flow was "too restricted to be of practical use". And: "if the API allows callbacks, not polling is better; if polling is unavoidable … 15 minutes at most. Let me override any conversation's refresh period at any time. An agent should be able to fetch the latest messages itself. Make the cache cap 5 GB per account, and every time/capacity parameter configurable."

**Reading — every conversation, no Track step.**
