### Lane I — the agent browser's live view bar never wraps or overlaps, in every language and width; the window menu opens the live view

The owner, zh, a ~1400 px live view of an ephemeral browser: "观看" / "接管" stacked one character per line over "并排到 VibeSpace 主开发 旁" and the URL, the word "undefined" before the viewer count, "标签页 (1)" / "控制台 (0)" / "操作 (0)" squeezed into vertical stacks — and no "Agent browser — live view" on the chat window's own menu. "你这些UI都检查过吗？" The honest answer was no: the live view was gated for behaviour in English, never looked at in zh / ja at real widths. It is now.

- **Why it broke (audit I):** every text button in the bar is a `.file-tool-btn`, and viewers.css's `.file-tool-btn` — a 24×24 ICON box, loaded after style.css — won every same-specificity tie, so the bar's own `width: auto` never applied: each label was a 24 px box with its words stacked one glyph per line, painting over its neighbours. The web-view hand-off wrote `UI_ICONS.web` (a key only the file icons have), so its innerHTML printed "undefined" (since 2.369.134).
- **The bar now:** every item keeps its words on one line at its own width; the URL alone flexes (down to 120 px, ellipsised); what does not fit folds into ONE ⋯ menu by priority — Tabs / Console / Actions first, then the backend chip, then bind / viewers / recording, the URL, then the mode badge last (its sentence becomes the ⋯'s first row and the ⋯ takes its colour); the one mode toggle and Reconnect never fold. The ⋯ rows carry the live counts ("Tabs (3)", ✓ on the open pane) and do each item's own act. The badge speaks in short words ("Agent is driving" / "You are driving" / "Another viewer is driving"), the "— agent asked to pause" sentence is its tooltip; ONE toggle (Take over ↔ Hand back — the Watch button was a second Hand back); the bind button is an icon (its words carry the session's name). The globe hands the URL to a web view.
- **The window menu:** a chat (or terminal) window whose conversation has a browser — running, or used since the session started — offers "Agent browser — live view" on its title-bar / tab / taskbar menu; it opens the live view BOUND beside that window, or binds / brings forward the one already open (never a second viewer). A bound live pane's menu says Unsplit once (its own Unbind only while it is a free window). The sidebar card keeps its entry.
- **The desktop-app strip** follows the same rule: with an agent lease at 600 px the status collapsed to nothing, the chips to one-letter stubs and ⋯ / Paste painted outside the strip; now the status flexes, the agent / origin / fact chips and Keep running / Stop fold into its ⋯, and the window-live form has the same one toggle and short badge.
- **Fixed on the way (the same tie):** Stop was never red, the copy chip never accent, Hand back never yellow, Confirm never green, the Browser profiles panel's Set aside / Delete never coloured and its 2.369.145 nowrap fix never applied; the paste box's Send / Cancel were 24 px boxes.
- Measured (the new heavy gate: 72 live-view states, 18 with two profiles, 54 desktop-strip states): at 1400 and 900 nothing folds in any language (the bar needs 631 px in zh, 717 in ja, 702 in en); at 600 zh folds Console + Actions, ja and en fold Tabs + Console + Actions (ja Take over: Console + Actions); the desktop strip under an agent lease folds its fact chips + Stop at 600 (ja also Stop at 900); zero overlaps, zero wrapped labels, zero clipped buttons, zero stray words in every state.
- **Verifier r1 — a bound live view at the split divider's clamp:** dragging the divider as far as it goes left the live pane at 15 % of its window — 134 px beside a 900 px chat — while the badge + toggle that never folded needed 169–222 px: the toggle was cut and the ⋯, the only way to the folded URL / bind / Tabs / Console / Actions, was clipped out of the bar in every language (ja already at a 1400 px window). Now the badge folds too (last), so the bar degrades to [toggle][⋯] (71–99 px), and a split pane never renders narrower than its own bar's minimum: the view publishes it (`barLayout`'s new `floor` + the bar's padding) through `WindowManager.setPaneMinWidth`, the grid spells it as the pane track's minimum (`splitColumns(ratio, mins)`, capped at the window floor minus the divider) and the divider stops there — the ratio stays what you dragged. Measured at the clamp: 900 / 600 / 320 px windows ⇒ panes of 134 / 87–115 / 87–115 px, toggle and ⋯ inside the bar in all 18 states (zh / ja / en × Watch / Take over); the floor removed ⇒ 47 px panes, both outside again. Five lows recorded, not fixed (docs/design-agent-browser-v2.md §4.4).
- Gates: test-live-bar-layout (new, fast: the PURE fold rule over hand-computed tables + 3000 seeded bars, the cascade-tie census over every `.file-tool-btn` companion class, the wiring pins; mutant-copy controls), test-browser-live-ui (new, heavy: every state shot and measured at zh / ja / en × 600 / 900 / 1400 × dark / light × free / bound × Watch / Take over, the desktop strip under a real agent lease, the window menu; controls = patched copies of style.css without the bar rules go RED), test-architecture §58 (every `UI_ICONS` / `FILE_ICONS` name resolves), test-contributions (the window menu row), test-window-binding (the bind button's words from its aria-label). Verifier r1: test-browser-live-ui ⑥ (the split floor — the window menu's act binds the view, a real divider drag to the clamp on 900 / 600 / 320 px windows, zh / ja-light / en × Watch / Take over: the toggle and the ⋯ inside the bar, no overflow, the whole census, the pane at ≥ its floor, the folded badge riding the ⋯; CONTROL: the floor removed at runtime ⇒ outside again), test-live-bar-layout (the fits:false branch stated, `floor` rows + the property "a bar as wide as its floor always fits", the split-floor rows over the verifier's measured widths beside the pre-fix table, a floor-without-⋯ mutant), test-window-binding-model (a pane floor is its track's minimum, capped; every grid write carries the pair's floors).

### Lane J — takeover clicks land where you click; while you drive, your keystrokes go only to the page

The owner, taking over the agent's browser from the live view: "接管浏览器的时候鼠标操作位置不对" — the mouse landed in the wrong place. The live view mapped every pointer by the size the stream's frames CLAIM — agent-browser's configured 1280×720 (0.32.0 and 0.38.1 alike) — while the page is 1280×577 headless and, headed on a big screen, e.g. 1265×1277 squeezed into a 713×720 picture. Measured on the real rung before the fix: a click on a grid cell landed 71 px off headless and 132 px off (or nowhere) on the owner's headed shape; after: on the cell, at DPR 2 and 1, UI scale 100 % and 125 %, a wide and a tall window.

- **Two sizes, never one.** The picture is letterboxed by its own size; the pointer is scaled to the page's real viewport, which the server now reads from the page itself (CDP layout metrics of the active tab — on the first frame, when the picture changes size, when another tab becomes active, and at every Take over) and tells every open live view. The stream's claim is used only where it matches the picture; otherwise the picture 1:1.
- **The agent's cursor** in the live view is placed through the same measurement as your clicks (it drifted the same way).
- **The action trace's "where it clicked" dot** was scaled by the same claim (too high on every thumbnail); it now uses the page's size.
- **No more "ephemeral → ephemeral".** Choosing the already-ticked row of the browser profile menu (the live view's title opens it) no longer tells the agent "browser profile changed: ephemeral (no profile) → ephemeral (no profile) (by user)"; a pin that moves nothing says nothing.
- The raw CDP address the server uses for the viewport read never reaches a live view (the daemon's `cdp_url` echo is dropped from the stream).
- Gates: test-browser-takeover (a PURE table of 4 page shapes × 2 window shapes × 2 zooms, the pre-fix formula as control, the bridge's viewport record, the CDP reader, the trace), test-browser-handles (the no-op pin + a patched-copy control that produces the owner's exact sentence), test-browser-live ⑤ (heavy: the whole stack on a real agent browser — headless and headed on its own 2560×1440 Xvfb — clicked from chrome emulated as the owner's Mac; the pre-fix belief in a patched copy is the control, through the same socket). Leg ④ now resolves the real binary the way the server does (it skipped whenever run inside a VibeSpace session) and the suite reaps the agent-browser daemons it starts.

**Lane J r2 — while you drive the agent's browser, your keystrokes go only to the page.**

The second naive-user study (2026-09-25, three operators on master 2.369.177, twelve collaboration scenarios) found that **every scenario where the person had to type inside the assistant's browser failed**: "接管后想在页面里打字 → 字消失，或跑进聊天输入框「tomsmithtomsmith…」" — typed text vanished, or landed in the CHAT COMPOSER, one Enter from sending a username (and, next, a password) to the agent. The live view forwarded keys only while its own element had focus, and every chat attach / reconnect put the caret back in the composer. Three more findings of the same study, fixed with it: "接管前助手排的审批卡 → 交回后还挂着，点 Allow 会跑旧计划" (an approval queued before a takeover ran a stale step after the hand back), "点击画面有没有送达的反馈：没有，所以分不清「画面卡了」还是「点丢了」", and "并排看时画面上下各三分之一黑边".

- **A takeover owns the keyboard.** While you drive, every key, every paste and every IME composition goes to the page — whatever has focus in the app. Nothing reaches a chat box or a terminal: the chat's attach / reconnect focus stands down, and a text box elsewhere that takes focus anyway gives it straight back ("Typing goes to the agent's browser while you drive it — press Hand back to type here"). The bar says **Typing goes to the browser** and the picture wears a focus ring. Only two chords stay the app's: Ctrl+\ (command mode) and Ctrl+Alt+←/→ (desktop switch). Esc goes to the page (pages close their own dialogs with it); handing back is the button. A paste arrives as its text (never a Ctrl+V into a browser whose clipboard is not yours); an IME composes in the view and the committed text is sent. The keyboard is released the moment you hand back, the socket drops, or the view is hidden (a desktop switch, a background tab) — typing blind into a page you cannot see is not driving.
- **Every click shows where it went.** A ripple at the page point the click was sent to, an "input sent · n" echo in the bar (or "not sent — …" when the view is disconnected), and a small marker where the page has your pointer (the screencast draws no cursor).
- **Stale approvals are answered, not left armed.** When you take over, the conversation's pending approval cards for browser page commands aimed at that browser are answered with a deny that names `browser_paused` ("…it did NOT run … wait for the handback message, which names the page they left, then re-plan"); the card says "Not run — you took over the browser, so this step went stale. The agent re-plans after you hand back." A card the agent queued while you drove goes the same way at the hand back. `vibespace-browser status`, a mention in an `echo`, a command on another attached profile are left alone (the CLI's own verb table decides). A deny opens no turn.
- **The picture fills the pane's width, top-aligned.** The spare room sits below the page, never a band above and below; the pointer, the ripple and both cursors use the same placement.
- **Verified on the real rung, not changed:** saucedemo's "Add to cart" is NOT a trusted-events site — after the login, Chrome's Password Manager raises its tab-modal "Change your password — found in a data breach" dialog (the public demo password), which swallows every input to the tab, CLI and live view alike, and is invisible to the screencast; a fresh navigation clears it (both the CLI click and the live-view click then add to the cart). The reCAPTCHA demo's "I'm not a robot" answers one live-view click by opening its image challenge (the click lands; the widget wants a human for the rest).
- Gates: test-browser-takeover ⑦ (fast: the ownership / key-route / focus / owner tables, text records, the top-aligned mapping with a centred-maths control, the stale verdict over the CLI's verb table, the REAL normalizer + claude adapter + the one permission answer under the takeover and handback sweep — a restart keeps the reason — with a patched-copy control that leaves the card pending, the one-answer census, the wiring pin), test-browser-live ⑥ (heavy, the real rung: the queued approval denied on the fake CLI's stdin at the first takeover; the band above the picture measured in pixels, the pre-fix centred CSS as the control; a form input clicked — ripple, echo, marker; the chat window attached and its composer focused by hand, then "tomsmith", an IME commit and a paste typed into the client ⇒ the page holds them and the composer is empty; CONTROL = the client rebuilt with the keyboard owner neutered ⇒ "tomsmith" lands in the chat composer).

### Integration (the four lanes on one tree)

- **The reaper reads a scratch root off the arguments the way lane H reads `--user-data-dir`:** lane N's `argvScratchRoots` is called by lane H's `scratchRootsOf` after the cwd and environment roots; a NUL-separated command line is read element by element (a root where an element starts with `/tmp/vs-…` or is a `<flag>=/tmp/vs-…` element), so a path merely mentioned inside another argument (`sh -c '…'`) roots nothing, and only a title-rewritten command line is read word by word. One `PRODUCT_ROOT_RE`; `Xtigervnc` on lane H's name list. test-ci-gate's controls (c)/(f) drop the argv reading too.
- **The live view's bar carries all four lanes:** the short badge (I) names a stopped / closed / failing browser (H) instead of "driving"; the "Typing goes to the browser" chip and the "input sent · n" echo (J) fold into ⋯ like every other item (the chip with bind/viewers/recording, the echo first; test-browser-live-ui's split-floor states now fold it, and its pre-fix-stylesheet control in Take over goes red on the Hand back toggle by name — the chip displaces the other labels); the one mode toggle (I) claims the keyboard through the `mode` answer (J); a desktop app on a paired machine keeps its machine chip in the folding strip (C + I).
- **A live view that opens after the stream did now knows it is connected.** Lane H's action recorder starts a browser's stream before anybody watches, so the live view always joined an open stream and never heard it open; lane J's takeover then never took the keyboard (keys went to the chat box). The bridge now tells a late viewer the stream is open.
- Every server a new suite boots gets its own Desktop display and port (`vncEnv()`, test-architecture §57); lane I's icon census is test-architecture §58.
- Suites that were red on their own lane and are fixed here: test-attach-rebuild (lane J moved the permission answer's live-feed site into `src/server/permission-answer.js`; the census follows it) and test-fixture-isolation (lane H's ephemeral leg in test-browser-live minted a fixture-family session id without being a transcript writer; it now uses a random id like the suite's other legs). The desktop-app install button's rule moved to `(0,2,0)` for lane I's cascade-tie census.

## 2.369.179 — the billing badge yields to the window title (lane G)

The owner, on a tab strip whose titles read "V.." and a six-letter stub beside a billing chip "≋ 全部 → UCI Max" and an inbox chip "⌸ 1": "这个全部->UCI Max占据了绝大部分空间，都看不到窗口标题了，你有什么好的解决方案吗？" The title wins now.

- **Three forms, one rule.** A window's billing chip (on a tab, and on a standalone title bar when space is short) takes the widest form that leaves the title readable: **full** ("≋ 全部 → UCI Max") only when the whole title fits beside it; else **compact** — the pool's glyph + the member's short name ("≋ UCI Max", a long name cut at 8 characters: "Northwi…") — when at least 6 characters of the title still show; else **icon** (the glyph and its colour, so a pooled window stays recognisable). API chips shorten the same way; a subscription chip, which never had a glyph, shows a crown only as an icon.
- **Nothing is lost.** The tooltip leads with the full words ("全部 → UCI Max · Pooled account · Click to switch billing"), and a click still opens the billing switcher, whose pool row names the pool and its member.
- **It follows the room.** Re-decided in one frame when the window is resized (one ResizeObserver per title bar, released when the window closes), when the title or the pool's member changes, on a tab switch, and when the owner dots or the inbox chip appear or go. Measured in layout px, so the UI scale never enters; the decision never reads the form currently shown, so it cannot flicker between two.
- **The inbox chip keeps its number** at its minimal width (never wider than "99+"; tighter padding on a tab).
- The phone layout is unchanged (it has no title bars), and so is the sidebar card (it has room).
- Gates: `scripts/test-title-chips.mjs` (fast — the rule's table at its exact boundaries, three patched-copy controls, the real `_fitChip` over a fake box with a label-only-room control, the wiring pins) and `scripts/test-title-chips-ui.mjs` (heavy, chrome — a pooled 3-tab chain at 640 px keeps every title readable: ≥ 6 characters beside a compact chip, ≥ 5 beside an icon — measured 7 under this box's Noto Sans and 6 under DejaVu Sans, the Actions runner's `system-ui`, which legs 1–5 also run under, the labels proven drawn in it; a 2-tab chain resized 1240 → 400 → 1240 px goes compact → icon → compact, one window at 1240 px shows every word; the control bundles an always-full rule and every title drops to ≤ 3 characters).

## 2.369.178 — desktop apps on paired machines: launch, stop, relaunch and watch a desktop app on another of your machines, and install xpra there from the dialog (lane C, docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless §3.5; owner D5–D8 2026-09-25)

The owner, after testing the desktop apps: "以及你要思考下整个app功能对于remote host的适配程度，自动seamless setup能力等等。" — how well does the whole app feature fit remote hosts, and can the setup happen by itself. Until now a desktop app could only run on the machine VibeSpace itself runs on; every other machine was refused by name. Now it can run on any paired Linux machine that runs the VibeSpace agent (D5), and xpra can be installed there from the launch dialog (D6).

- **Run on another machine.** The launch dialog has a "Run on" row: this machine plus every paired machine. Pick one and you see that machine's own app list and what it can run; the app starts there and the window's title says which machine it is on. A machine that cannot run apps is shown greyed with the reason in words (offline, its agent needs an upgrade, no X11 on macOS / Windows) — never hidden. Stop, Keep running, Scale ▸ and the window list work through that machine's agent.
- **The picture comes through VibeSpace.** The app's xpra port on the other machine is forwarded over the agent's own connection; your browser still talks only to VibeSpace, and seats, typing, the clipboard and the one-active-viewer rule are unchanged. Measured on a real paired box (dial pairing through a scratch hub): paired in 0.8 s, launch → ready 1.8 s, xpra round trip 7–8 ms on a 6–9 ms link, a key to its drawn echo 11–18 ms.
- **The apps live on their machine** (D8). Each paired machine keeps its own record (`~/.vibespace/desktop-apps.json`), so an app outlives a VibeSpace restart; the hub keeps its copy in `data/desktop-apps-hosts.json` (never mixed into this machine's store) and picks every machine's apps back up at boot, in the background. A machine that stops answering keeps its windows ("machine not answering" — the window reconnects when it returns) instead of closing them.
- **"Install xpra on <machine>…"** shows exactly what will run first (the distro's own xpra when it is 5 or newer, else xpra.org's repository pinned to 6.x), then runs it with passwordless sudo and streams the log into the dialog; without passwordless sudo you get the commands to copy. The install runs detached on the machine: a VibeSpace restart, a lost link or the agent's own restart never kills apt halfway, a second click follows the running install instead of starting another, and a lock held by the install itself (the kernel releases it when the install ends) makes sure there is only ever one. The fleet image installs xpra 6.x from xpra.org's bookworm repository, pinned (D7), so every machine speaks one xpra version.
- **One implementation on every machine.** The half of the desktop-app keeper that happens on the machine — starting X, xpra and the app, knowing which processes are the app's, stopping them, fitting the window, listing windows, the resource sample, the record — moved verbatim into the shared `src/desktop-serve.js`, which the agent bundles and answers as the `desktop-serve` op (nine ops, every answer `{ok, code, error}`, never a throw across the wire). VibeSpace keeps the policy (idle stop, the resource report, the viewer seats). `src/server/desktop-access.js` is the one way to reach a machine: in-process here, the op on a paired device (an ssh host gets the agent installed over ssh, as Add machine already does), an agent too old for the op refused by name before it is asked. Migration `2026-09-desktop-apps-host-key` stamps existing records `hostId: 'local'`; nothing changes for apps on this machine.
- **Routes:** `GET/POST /api/desktop/apps` take `host`; new `GET /api/desktop/machines`, `GET /api/desktop/install-plan`, `POST /api/desktop/install-xpra` (the log as NDJSON).
- **Five adversarial verify rounds**, every finding reproduced red first and fixed with a control that shows the old behaviour:
  - C2 verify: a click on a paired machine whose link drops mid-request answers at once, not after a 60 s timeout; a viewer that half-closes during setup releases its forward; a long install is waited out and named (never "exited 1", never killed).
  - r2: a viewer whose connection resets while the forward opens no longer takes the whole VibeSpace server down (an uncaught socket error — the agent browser's CDP mediator had the same shape and is fixed too); a streaming command whose link died is never left paused on the machine; the install became detached with its own pidfile.
  - r3: the install never follows a stale pid after a pid wrap; an orphaned command is never left paused by a log it cannot write; a browser lease revoked while its client was still connecting refuses that client instead of wiring it to the old browser.
  - r4: two simultaneous "Install" clicks could still both start (1–4 in 150) — the lock became `flock`, held by the running install itself on local storage, never broken by hand (40 + 20 trials of five simultaneous starts: one install every time).
  - r5 (four lows): a start in the same second as an earlier install's end runs instead of answering that old result (the recorded end time is nanoseconds now); the lock's directory is named by the user id (`/run/user/<uid>`, else a private `/tmp/vibespace-<uid>`), never by an environment variable two starters may not share; an install runner that did not get the lock is reported in ~0.2 s instead of after 10 s; the docs say who holds the lock — the install's shell and apt-get, never dpkg (apt-get closes inherited descriptors for dpkg; a dpkg that outlives both is held off by dpkg's own lock).
- Gates: new test-desktop-serve (fast, 196, ~16 s — the op table, the install plan, the hub's registry of a paired machine over a stub device, the bridge's endpoint, the routes, the install launcher under simultaneous, killed and squatted starts) and test-desktop-remote (heavy, 70, ~53 s — a real agent daemon from the built bundle as the paired machine: a real xpra session through VibeSpace's bridge, typed keys landing in the app, offline ⇒ 404, the daemon killed mid-install, the install's lock held while it runs); test-desktop-xpra-window §13 (real Chrome driving an app on a paired scratch daemon); test-migrations (the new row); test-architecture (desktop-serve.js in the shared set; §56: capabilities pinned by content); test-browser-mediation ③c; test-desktop-app-keeper, -apps, -viewers, test-xpra-client, test-browser-providers, test-opencode-remote re-pinned where a wiring line moved.

## 2.369.177 — seamless desktop-app windows: an app that draws its own title bar gets none of ours, and its header bar moves our window (round 3 lane B, docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless §3.3; owner D3 2026-09-25)

The owner, trying GNOME Calculator on the xpra rung: "if the inner window has full window controls (a close button …), the outer window should not show anything, for a seamless effect." A desktop app whose main window says `decorations: 0` (a GTK header bar) now shows NO VibeSpace title bar and NO status strip — they fold to 0 height; the 1 px frame and the resize handles stay.

- **The app's header bar moves the window.** xpra is the display's window manager and hands the app's move request to the client (`initiate-moveresize`); the VibeSpace window enters its title bar's own drag from that press (snap, shake bypass, tab merge, desktop-preview drop — one implementation, `WindowManager.beginDragFromPointer`), edges resize through the handles' own path (`beginResizeFromPointer`), a CANCEL puts it back. The X window stays at 0,0. Measured: a 120×64 drag moves the window by exactly 120/64; GTK4 sends its CANCEL on the button release, after the drop (a no-op).
- **The app's own ─ □ buttons work.** Measured: GTK 4.22 under xpra 6.5.3 paints minimize, maximize and close; maximize / restore / minimize now act on our window (set semantics), and restoring ours re-maps the app.
- **The bars come back** on a 250 ms hover of the top edge or while Alt is held — over the app, never resizing it; they linger 1.5 s after the pointer goes back into the app and fold when it leaves the window.
- **Paused** (the bars show) while an agent drives the app, in a tab group, on a phone, and while the picture is not connected.
- **Escape hatches:** the taskbar item's menu (Show window frame ▸ Auto / On / Off — per app, synced to every client — plus Scale ▸, Keep running, Stop app), the same under the revealed ⋯, and Settings → Window → Seamless desktop app windows = Off.
- **With the strip folded** the plain-http copy chip floats at the pane's bottom-right (gone after 10 s) and the idle stop's last minute is a toast.
- **Verifier r1, three fixes:** (1) dragging a MAXIMIZED seamless window off — by the app's header bar or by our title bar — now tells the app it is no longer maximized (window.js's drag un-maximize calls `onResize` like every other un-maximize; before, the app kept its restore glyph and its next click did nothing); (2) the floating copy chip moved from the pane's top-right, where it sat over the app's own ─ □ ✕ for 10 s, to the bottom-right; (3) the revealed bars sit UNDER the resize handles (z-index 9 / 8 < 10), so a press on the top edge after the 250 ms reveal is a resize again, not a drag.
- **Fixed on the way:** a click into an app's picture never activated its VibeSpace window (the pane cancels its pointerdown, so the window's mousedown focus never fired).
- Gates: test-desktop-seamless (new, fast: the verdict's 192-row matrix vs the formula + a pause-less control, the reveal transitions, the WindowManager seams over a fake DOM), test-xpra-client §2d/§2e, test-desktop-xpra-window §12 (heavy: every leg above on the real rung, CONTROL = a copy with the verdict forced false; §10/§11 now reveal the folded bars the user's way before clicking the outer ✕ / the ⋯ of a seamless calculator; r1: §12 (3b) drag off a maximized window + a live muted-onResize control, §12 (4) the revealed hit test at the top edge + a live z-index-25 control, §12 (9) the chip clear of the header bar + a live top-placement control; test-desktop-seamless §4 (e) + a mutant-copy control of window.js, §5 CSS pins).

## 2.369.176 — a browser desktop app changes its scale from the ⋯ menu like any other app, keeping its profile (owner 2026-09-25 "你不让我在这里调我怎么调？")

The Scale ▸ rows of a browser app (Chrome as a desktop app) were greyed out with "stop it and launch it again": a relaunch mints a new session with a new profile dir, and a browser started on an empty profile loses its logins and tabs. Now the keeper relaunches a browser in a different ORDER: the successor is recorded first (every refusal — the cap, a vanished binary — happens before anything stops), the old record names it, the old browser is stopped and, once every part is verified gone (a browser locks its profile dir), its profile dir is MOVED onto the successor's path, then the successor starts on it at the chosen scale. The picture reconnects in the same window; logins and tabs come back with the profile.

- What a "live" scale change would need does not exist on X11: GDK_SCALE / Xft.dpi are read once at the app's start, so a true scale change is always a restart. The confirm dialog for a browser says the profile is kept.
- Gates: test-desktop-apps (the PURE verdict no longer refuses a browser row); test-desktop-app-keeper §18 (c3) on the real xpra rung with the fake browser — the file the old browser wrote is in the successor's profile, the old dir is gone by a move (never `profileRemovedAt`), the successor process was started on the carried path, the old record names its successor in the same broadcast that shows it exited; CONTROL: a keeper without the carry starts the successor empty.

## 2.369.173 — two owner-reported bugs: codex sub-agents stay out of the Sessions list (the kind filter is per page, one classifier on every rung, the daemon snapshot child fixed), and a fork lands in its source's Task Groups (with the lock capture rebuilt on a PID witness — six adversarial rounds)

### Codex sub-agents stay out of the Sessions list: the agent-kind choice is a view of the page, and remote hosts classify sub-agents too

The owner (2026-09-25, a screenshot of the sidebar): "截图里这么多subagent啥情况，为啥没自动filter掉" — dozens of codex threads named Singer, Pasteur, Faraday … each with an orange "L". The "L" is the 12 px ↳ sub-agent icon, drawn only for a row already classified as a sub-agent: the classification was right (35 of this box's 48 September rollouts are v2 children, all marked). The list showed them because 2.369.32 PERSISTED an explicit ALL (or the ↳ tab) in localStorage — one click, and every later load was flooded.

- **The sidebar.** The ALL / kind tabs are now a choice for this page (sessionStorage); the old localStorage key is dropped at load, so every list opens primary-only again. A list that is not primary-only says so — "Sub-agent and review threads are listed too." with a **Main conversations only** link (zh/ja). Sub-agents stay reachable through the ↳ tab and the parent's View sub-agents (GET /api/subagents).
- **Remote hosts (the standing-sweep twin).** ssh and daemon discovery now classify a codex thread too: a new `SC` discovery line carries the thread's own `thread_source` / `parent_thread_id` / `agent_*` fields, read by the same classifier as the local listing (`classifyCodexThread`, src/discovery-facts.js). A remote sub-agent lists as a sub-agent under its parent, named by its nickname (it used to take the parent's first message as its name), and the Recent / History / cross-host search zones apply the same agent-kind filter.
- **One rule.** A thread is a sub-agent when its own session_meta says `source.subagent.thread_spawn` **or** the top-level `thread_source: "subagent"`; a user fork (`forked_from_id` only) stays a primary conversation; no role is invented from `agent_path` (codex writes `agent_role: null` on v2 children, so no role badge).
- **The daemon's discovery-snapshot child now runs.** It had crashed on every run since 2.288.0 (`os` used before its declaration), so each snapshot silently ran inline on the daemon's own loop instead.
- Fixture scripts/fixtures/codex-subagent-v2/ (the real v2 key shape, synthetic values); gate test-codex-subagents ④ (49 new asserts: listing, /api/subagents, daemon snapshot child, the real ssh script under sh, device ≡ ssh ≡ local, mutant-copy negative controls).

**Verifier round 1** — two findings from the adversarial verify of this change, both reproduced before the fix:

- **Remote hosts classified only the 30 newest codex threads.** The ssh script and the daemon snapshot list up to 100 rollouts, but the new classification (`SC` line) was read inside the loop that gathers cwd and name candidates for the 30 newest only. On the owner's real store 25 of 48 sub-agents still listed as primary, nameless conversations on a remote host. Every listed rollout now gets its classification (a 128 KiB head read past slot 30; the thread's own session_meta is its first line, ~22 KB). Measured on the same store after the fix: 48 of 48 on the daemon rung and on the ssh rung, equal to the local listing. **Still capped at 30, by design:** cwd and the first-message name — a primary thread older than the 30 newest lists without a name (a sub-agent is named by its nickname).
- **A sub-agent on a remote host could be hidden with no way to show it.** The ALL / ↳ tabs and the "listed too" hint counted local sessions only, so with a primary-only local list the remote zones filtered their sub-agents out and no tab appeared; a cross-host search for one answered "No sessions found". The tab census now spans every loaded remote list and is redrawn when one lands. A remote zone or search that the kind filter alone emptied says "{n} more on {host} hidden by the agent-kind filter." with **Show all agent types** (zh/ja).
- Gate: test-codex-subagents ④ grows to 109 — a generated 45-rollout store (40 sub-agents interleaved to positions 31–45) judged on every row by the local listing, the daemon snapshot child and the real ssh script under sh; mutants that re-cap the SC leg at 30 (daemon and ssh) go red; the real Sidebar prototype driven over a DOM stand-in (↳ tab, hint, search row, Show all), with a mutant whose census reads the local list alone going red. The suite now mints its fixture ids and re-homes its own process (HOME and os.homedir on a scratch home, cleaned on signals, the real ~/.claude/projects censused at the end): 109 asserts, and test-fixture-isolation is green with it (found by the integration's fast tier — the suite had started calling fixtureSid() without the isolation that census requires).

### A fork lands in its source's Task Groups

The owner: "fork的会话不会自动分配到和fork之前的会话相同的group里". `_doForkSession` spawned every fork with no `taskId`, so a branch of a conversation that sat in a Task Group arrived in none — no task context in the agent, no tag on the card; only folder auto-include carried over.

- A fork now inherits EVERY Task Group its source is explicitly tagged with: the first rides the spawn as `taskId` (the server's spawn group, so the agent's task context names it from the first turn), the others are bound once the fork's own id appears. Archived groups and the card's star are not inherited. One implementation for the card's Fork…, fork-at-message and the terminal-mode fork (PURE src/lib/fork-groups.js).
- The pending-bind queue holds a LIST per session and waits past the id a fork borrows from its parent — a claude/codex fork shows the parent's id until the harness announces its own, and binding then would have tagged the parent and dropped the fork's bind.
- A terminal-mode claude fork now learns its own id: terminal mode has no stream parser, and the local lock capture used to run only for a session with no id, so a fork kept its parent's id for life and its extra groups never bound. The capture is one module (src/claude-lock-capture.js) for the create chain and the boot re-arm, and it covers a pending terminal fork.
- A fork created right after its parent can no longer make the parent adopt the fork's lock: a fork's borrowed id is not a claim, and the capture stops once the stream has named the session.
- A local claude session's id is now taken only from the lock its OWN CLI wrote: the lock's pid must be alive and descend from the session's wrapper (the pid the wrapper records before it spawns the CLI). Picking by time swapped the ids of two sessions created together whenever the later one's CLI started first, and adopted a dead CLI's leftover lock or another same-cwd claude started a few seconds earlier — including on a restored fork, for good.
- The capture no longer gives up after about 17 seconds: a fork whose CLI is slow to start (a big parent transcript) used to keep its parent's id until a server restart. It keeps retrying, backing off to every 30 seconds, until the id is found or the session ends — after a restart too, for dtach and daemon pipe sessions alike.
- A chat fork's adoption now records that the fork is no longer pending, and a restart restores the pending flag only while the session still carries its source's id — a stale flag made the fork's own id look unclaimed to its neighbours.
- A server restart no longer kills the conversation a pending fork was made from. At boot, sessions that claim the same conversation are de-duplicated and the losers stopped; a fork still carrying its source's id counted as a claim, so the live PARENT was stopped as a "stale duplicate" (its CLI ended, its socket and metadata removed). This hit every restart inside a fork's start-up window and, because an older server left every terminal-mode fork with its parent's id for good, the update restart itself stopped the parent of each such fork. A fork's borrowed id is no longer a claim; two sessions that each own a conversation's id are still de-duplicated.
- The lock a session adopts must have been written by the process it names: its `procStart` matches the live process, or (a lock without one) that process is a claude. A stale lock whose pid number had been reused by a `sleep` or git child the CLI started was adopted before.
- A pending CHAT fork now adopts its own id after a restart: from its own lock when its first record arrived while the server was down, and from the stream when that record is the first line after the re-attach (dtach's clear-screen prefix used to be glued to it and the line was thrown away). A stream line that looks like a record and cannot be used is now logged and counted (`cli-unparsable-line`), never dropped silently. A fork re-opened on the device daemon keeps its pending flag too.
- A pending bind whose session died before its own id appeared is dropped at once instead of waiting for the 20-entry sweep. A remote terminal-mode claude fork still has no way to learn its own id and keeps its parent's key.
- A session restored from an older server's record can no longer take the id of a `claude` it runs from a tool. Every chat fork adopted before 2.369.134 kept `forkRequested: true` in its record with no source id, so it was read back as a pending fork and the capture looked past its own CLI's lock to a deeper one — a `claude -p` run from the session's Bash tool — and persisted that id. The capture now takes the nearest lock its wrapper's CLI wrote and answers nothing if that one is not usable, and such a record (its adoption left the source in `forkedFrom`) owns its id.
- A chat session ending on its own is no longer reported as a dropped record: dtach's `[EOF - dtach terminating]`, `[detached]`, `[got signal N - dying]`, `[read returned an error]` and `[select failed]` lines are transport output. A record-shaped line now means a JSON object or array prefix — that one test is the whole rule — and the telemetry for dropped lines is capped per session like the log.
- A session's CLI rewriting its own lock file can no longer hand the session the id of a `claude` it runs from a tool: a lock that cannot be read at that moment still counts as the nearest, and the capture waits for the next attempt instead of looking past it.
- New fast suite test-fork-groups (148): the plan and verdict tables, the real fork and pending-bind methods driven from source, a one-fork-create census, the terminal-mode fork end to end over real lock files and a real Task Group store, the parent/fork race with the locks in both orders, two sessions created together, stray and dead locks, a lock landing after the old window, real process trees over /proc (including a stale lock under a `sleep` child's pid), the boot de-duplication through the real code, the real chat stream consumer, the real daemon-pipe re-open, wiring pins that ignore comments, a real wrapper → claude → sh → claude tree, dtach's real exit bytes and all five of its banners through the consumer, a CLI lock torn mid-rewrite beside a nested claude's, twenty-two mutant-copy controls. New heavy suite test-fork-restore: a scratch server killed and rebooted beside two parents and three pending forks — no parent is stopped and every fork adopts its own id; a copy with the old de-duplication stops a parent. The fast suite re-homes its own process, so test-fixture-isolation is green again.

## 2.369.172 — exit forensics: a session's death names its actor — the CLI's exit signal, the wrapper's own signal and the socket's fate reach the journal line, and the wrapper meta is kept as a tomb

The 2026-09-24 08:11:33 UTC incident: three active chat sessions died in one 40 ms window and the journal held only `[session] exited <id> "<name>" mode=chat backend=claude` (B-3052).

- **The child's signal.** `chat-wrapper.js` now reads node's `(code, signal)` — a CLI killed by a signal used to be "code null" and nothing else — and `pty-wrapper.js` names node-pty's signal number (a signal death there is exitCode 0). Both write `childExitSignal` into the wrapper meta and log `Child exited with code <c> signal <s>`. Wrapper exit statuses are unchanged (a signal-killed child ⇒ 0, as before).
- **The wrapper's own signal.** All three wrappers (`chat-wrapper.js`, `pty-wrapper.js`, `codex-chat-wrapper.js`) now handle SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGINT with a synchronous record — `wrapper received <SIG> (child pid <p>, childDead=<b>)` in the log, `wrapperSignal`/`wrapperSignalAt` in the meta — and still die, with 143/129/130. The CLI is left exactly as before. SIGKILL is uncatchable and reads `wrapper=unfinalized`.
- **The line.** `[session] exited …` keeps every field and appends ` signal=<SIG>` (when there is one) ` wrapper=<signal:SIG|finalized|unfinalized> socket=<present|gone|none>`; the `session-exited` event carries the same facts and the `exited` broadcast the signal. One PURE reader, `src/exit-facts.js`.
- **The tomb.** The teardown keeps `data/exit-tombs/<id>.meta.json` (the wrapper meta + exitedAt/socketFate/wrapperFate) beside the existing `.tail`; the 7-day sweep removes both.
- **The record never creates a file.** The kill path unlinks `<id>.json`/`<id>.buf` in the same tick it SIGTERMs the dtach master, and the wrapper is SIGHUP'd a few ms later; the handler now writes only into files that still exist (`'r+'`), so a Terminate leaves no orphan pair (measured under real dtach).
- **The remote sentinel names the signal.** `vibespace-remote-keeper` and the daemon's pipe-session waiter add `signal` to `{"type":"_remote_exit"}` (`code` unchanged, `code ?? 0`); chat-wrapper and codex-chat-wrapper record it, so a CLI killed on the host reads `code=0 signal=SIGTERM` instead of a clean exit. A sentinel from an older keeper/daemon still says only `code=0`.
- **The child is handed nothing new**, pinned by the signals the child RECEIVES against the handler-less baseline, in the production shape: under dtach every kind (chat, pty, codex) receives exactly the kernel's SIGHUP — in the kill path and on a pkill of the wrapper alike, the same as before the change — so a chat CLI dies with its wrapper; it "receives nothing" only without a controlling terminal. The fake CLI counts what it receives, so a forwarded SIGHUP is caught too.
- **The codex wrapper.** `codex-chat-wrapper.js` wrote no exit record at all — every codex exit read `code=null wrapper=unfinalized` (the SIGKILL fate) and a codex app-server killed on a host a clean end. It now records `childExitCode`/`childExitSignal` (the keeper sentinel's `signal` included), logs `Child exited with code <c> signal <s>` and has the same record-then-die handler; exit statuses unchanged. A wrapper started before this build (dtach sessions survive the update) still writes no record until it is restarted.
- **The teardown waits for the wrapper's record.** In the incident's own order — the dtach master dies first — the server's exit handler and the wrapper's SIGHUP record are two consequences of one event, and the single read at exit usually lost (on the workspace's FUSE storage a read 3 ms after the socket closed could even parse a half-written meta, and the tomb then kept nothing but `metaMissing`). The teardown now reads at once as before unless the meta names a wrapper still running without a finished record; then it re-reads for at most 300 ms. A wrapper still alive after that reads `wrapper=running` (not the SIGKILL fate), a meta that never parses tombs as `metaUnreadable`, and the tomb records how long it waited. The wrappers write the record before anything else, and overwrite the meta in one space-padded write, so no instant of it is unreadable. Measured with the wrapper files on the FUSE workspace: 36/36 teardowns fed at the socket-close instant read `wrapper=signal:SIGHUP`.
- Gate: scripts/test-exit-forensics.mjs (fast, 285 — the three real wrappers against a fake CLI into the real teardown, the kill path and a wrapper pkill under real dtach, the real keeper's sentinel through both chat wrappers, the real teardown fed at the socket's close in the incident's order, a syscall-by-syscall read of the wrapper's record, with a patched-copy control per change — the keeper's via `scripts/mutant-copy.mjs`'s new `selfPath`, which keeps a self-spawning script's own `__filename`) + test-agentd-session (the pipe-session sentinel).

- **r1 (the Actions mirror's red, same version):** test-codex-p2-client failed on the 2-vCPU runner with `ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir /tmp/vs-cxfork-…` — the suite killed the wrapper and removed its scratch dir in the same tick, and the new signal handler's last act (the log append, which creates the log file) landed between rmSync's listing and its rmdir. Four fast suites had that shape with no exit wait (test-codex-p2-client, test-codex-0153, test-codex-effort-meta, test-codex-p2-wrapper). The ONE idiom is now scripts/scratch.mjs `stopWrapper(child, {dir})` (kill → await exit, SIGKILL after 3 s → rmSync with retries); test-architecture §55 is the grep-derived census (a suite that spawns a wrapper and removes a dir imports it or waits on `exit`), with a planted control. 不变量=a suite that starts a process that writes on its way out waits for the exit before removing the directory it writes into.

## 2.369.171 — a resource guard never stops an app a person or an agent is using: desktop apps and agent browsers are REPORTED, only the headless OpenCode serve is stopped; memory is measured as a footprint (PSS), never a sum of RSS

On 2026-09-25 00:03 UTC the owner launched Google Chrome as a desktop app; three seconds after it was ready the desktop-app keeper logged `RUNAWAY — … Google Chrome, 25 process(es) … RSS 2.0 GB (limit 2.0 GB)`, stopped it, deleted its profile directory and refused every Chrome launch for 60 minutes. The number was a SUM of VmRSS over processes that share their pages (the same box: 891 chrome pids ΣVmRSS 94.67 GB vs ΣPss 15.09 GB). The owner's ruling (00:12 UTC): "不是就算是单一内存2G也不好啊，chrome这么吃内存，完全可能超过这个量吧。这个keeper到底是干啥的，没必要别乱加会影响使用的feature" — a memory ceiling on an app a person is using is wrong even with an honest metric.

- **No kill.** The desktop-app keeper and the browser keeper no longer stop, park or refuse anything because of a resource sample. The `runawayParkedUntil` maps, the `runaway-parked` refusal (routes included), the `runaway` state transition and every "not launching X again for N min" sentence are gone. The headless OpenCode serve (which the product runs for itself, the 2.369.42 incident) keeps its stop and park, now on the honest metric, with `why` naming it ("memory (PSS) 5.0 GB (limit 2.0 GB)").
- **One verdict, two outcomes.** `src/runaway-guard.js` (PURE, new) is the ONE resource verdict (`resourceVerdict` → `over`); the three verbatim copies in desktop-apps.js, browser-profiles.js and opencode-serve.js are deleted. What a keeper does with `over` is its policy — the serve stops, apps and browsers report. `GUARD_RSS_BYTES` → `GUARD_MEM_BYTES` (same 2 GiB). test-architecture §54 keeps the comparison in that one file and keeps every keeper but the serve from stopping or parking for a resource — structurally: the report-only keepers' sampled block may write only its guard slot, live row and locals and call no stop, retire, kill or fs; every `stop(` names a reason from a closed list; the verdict is read nowhere else (eight planted spellings as controls).
- **Honest measurement.** Per pid, `/proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup` Pss (≈1.1 ms per pid; a 25-process app ≈27 ms per 60 s tick, read off the event loop), else RssAnon+RssShmem; a set is summed in the strongest metric EVERY member provides and names it (`memMetric`); a summed-RSS set is never judged, and neither is RssAnon+RssShmem over several processes (`anon-sum` — copy-on-write and shared pages counted per sharer, +51 % over ΣPss on 889 chrome pids); for ONE process it is judged and labelled "anon+shm". `rssBytes` stays in the payloads for one release (deprecated).
- **Reported, once, with your own lever.** Over the threshold, a session's live row carries the reading and the sentence, and a notice is filed when a crossing begins — "Google Chrome is using 6.2 GB (PSS) — Stop it from the Desktop panel if that is not what you expect" / "The agent browser of profile "Work" is using 4.0 GB (PSS) — Stop it from the Browser panel …" — and again only after three samples in a row under 90 % of the threshold, never within an hour of the previous notice for the same session (a reading hovering across the line had filed one every second sample: 5 notices in 10 minutes in review); a notice no browser tab received (a restart with nobody connected) is re-sent under the same key on the next sample still over; telemetry `desktop-app-resource` / `browser-resource`, once per crossing. The desktop-app window's chip and the Browser panel show memory with its metric ("412 MB (PSS)").
- **A profile goes only by your ending.** A desktop-app browser's profile is removed after Stop, a Scale ▸ relaunch or the browser's own exit — an idle-out (only when `desktop.idleTimeoutMin` is set — see below) keeps it and the record says why.
- **Idle-out is off by default** (owner, the same hour: "30分钟那个暂停也默认关掉！"). `desktop.idleTimeoutMin` now defaults to 0 (never); the setting stays for anyone who wants a stop after N minutes without input, and "Keep running" still exempts a window. An app a person opened is not stopped for sitting still.
- **Migration `2026-09-runaway-parks-void`** removes the park maps from data/desktop-apps.json and data/browser-profiles.json and rewrites the old guard's `stopped as a runaway: RSS …` errors to `stopped by the old resource guard (a per-process RSS sum — retired in 2.369.171)`, through the live keepers.
- Gates: test-runaway-guard (new; the oscillation fixture ⇒ one notice, delivery re-sends, two more scratch-copy controls), test-desktop-display §8, test-desktop-apps, test-browser-pin, test-browser-ephemeral, test-opencode-serve, test-migrations, test-architecture §54 (fast); test-desktop-app-keeper §5/§18 (heavy).

## 2.369.170 — the gate's reaper names every pid it kills; lane worktrees leave the scratch-root namespace (B-a965)

A stray `node scripts/ci.mjs --help` on 2026-09-24 ran the scratch-orphan sweep and killed 34 processes under 22 roots. One root was `/tmp/vs-work`, the directory the development lanes' worktrees lived in — their detached dev servers were orphaned by construction and older than the 10-minute floor, so the evidence-based rule fired correctly on the wrong thing, and the log named only the roots.

- `reapReport(list)` (PURE, exported) is the head line plus one `[ci]   pid <pid> (ppid <n>) <name>: <argv head> — root <dir> — <rule>` line per victim; both reapers (the fast tier's sync sweep and the heavy lanes' async twin) print it before the first SIGTERM. test-ci-gate §9 pins the report's shape, that every victim line carries its pid / root / rule / command head, and the wiring in both reapers.
- test-codex-pool R1 asserted the saved wait as the literal `2h`; the wall is stamped at world creation and the product measures from its own clock at the wall, so a second boundary under a loaded gate read `1h 59m` and blocked the 2.369.169 push. The assertion is a band (`2h` … `1h 50m`).
- Lane worktrees now live under `/tmp/vibespace-lanes/`, outside `SCRATCH_ROOT_RE` — a development checkout is never a suite's scratch dir. The product is unchanged by that half; the convention is recorded in kb-file-structure (ci.mjs) and kb-bugfix-invariants.

docs/design-user-inbox-reply.md (+ the zh twin). ## 2.369.168 — VibeSpace takes over the browser: agents use vibespace-browser only; agent-browser is not on their PATH; the three browser faces are renamed

The owner (2026-09-24): "那就选B吧 我还是觉得浏览器操作有点奇怪，另外建议vibespace完全接管浏览器工具，不要再给agent留agent-browser单独的入口了，也不要兼容agent直接操作agent-browser的行为。最好就是直接从系统path隐藏agent-browser，也修改一下web-access这个skill。" Design: docs/design-browser-takeover.zh.md (+ English).

**One CLI (T1).** `vibespace-browser` takes every page verb directly — `vibespace-browser open <url>`, `snapshot`, `click @e3`, `fill`, `get text`, `tab`, `batch` … — through ONE PURE router, `src/browser-verbs.js`: VibeSpace's own 12 words always win (the one collision with the browser CLI's census is `profiles`, reachable as `-- profiles`); raw CDP (`connect`, `get cdp-url`, `--cdp`, `--auto-connect`), identity flags (`--session`, `--namespace`, `--config`, `--state`, `--restore…`), launch flags (`--proxy`, `--headed`, `--args`, … — `--enable`/`--init-script` still pass beside `open`), the user's verbs (`confirm`/`deny`) and the verbs that are not the agent's (`auth`, `session`, `stream`, `inspect`, `install`, `upgrade`, `doctor`, `plugin`, `mcp`, `dashboard`, `chat`, `skills`) are refused LOCALLY — before any server call — with a typed code and a remedy; a `batch` is judged line by line and one refused line refuses it all, naming the line. Every page verb makes one `/resolve` call (lease, `profile_changed`, `browser_paused`), runs the real binary found on PATH behind the shim, and is audited — the ephemeral browser's commands too, which nothing recorded before. `use` only attaches (`--print` ⇒ `not_offered`), `new-child` prints only `export VIBESPACE_BROWSER=<child>`, `-- <verb>` stays as the valve for a verb newer than the table. On the shared rung `close --all` is refused `shared_browser`.

**The shim (T2).** `data/bin/agent-browser` answers one line — `agent-browser is driven by VibeSpace here — run: vibespace-browser <the same arguments>` — and exits 2; it never forwards. It ships to every remote host with the other tools, and the remote prelude now puts the tools dir on PATH AFTER the node finder (one of three hand-written copies ran it before, which put the real binary back in front); the three copies are one composition in src/remote-shell.js. The server's own probe and runtime resolve the real binary past the shim, so a server started from inside a session still reads the right version.

**The teaching (T4).** The Browsing line, the attachment-set line and the window line teach `vibespace-browser <verb>` and never name the hidden CLI; docs/agent/browser-manual.md is rewritten around the one tool; docs/agent/web-access-skill.md is the web-access skill rewritten for it (install it as ~/.claude/skills/web-access/SKILL.md). test-architecture §52 counts the name in the teaching, the agent manuals and the two CLIs' strings, and fails a static tool that does not ship.

Gates: test-browser-verbs (new, fast: the router table over the checked-in `--help` census, the shim with a forwarding-copy control, the CLI over a fake server), test-remote-shell (composition order, the zero-literal drift guard, a real `sh` resolving the shim over a fake nvm install — the pre-fix order as the control), test-architecture §52, and the browser suites that pinned `use --print` / the old wording.

**The managed ephemeral browser (T3).** A conversation's own browser is watched now. Its first page verb with no attachment makes VibeSpace record it (`(ephemeral) <session name>`, owned by the conversation, the same `vs-<browserKey>` identity the session already uses), start it — or pick up one already running — under the session's exact spawn settings, and audit every verb against it; the live view, the takeover and the action trace work on it exactly as before. It counts against the instance's ceiling of 6 running browsers, now shared with the running desktop apps: a conversation whose first verb would be the seventh is refused `browser_cap`, naming every holder and the way out, and nothing is queued. An idle stop is recorded as stopped (not an error) and the next verb starts it again; a runaway is parked like a profile's; a server restart adopts it; when the conversation ends it is stopped and its record removed by itself (a named profile never is). `vibespace-browser status` names it, `profiles` never lists it, and the Agent browser window (it was "Browser profiles" before the rename below) has an **Ephemeral browsers** section with a Stop button. Remote sessions and instances with per-session browsers off stay unmanaged, and the manual says so.

**The attach gap (T6).** A browser window the user launched from Desktop apps (Firefox, Chromium — the registry's `category: 'browser'` rows, or an ad-hoc launch of their executables) is theirs: `vibespace-window attach` (and snapshot, act, screenshot, watch) refuses it `browser_is_human` with the road to take (`vibespace-browser`), and `list` no longer shows it.

Gates (chunk 2): test-browser-ephemeral (new, fast: the record, the reuse, the idle restart, the live-view port parity, fork/child records, the reap with a named-profile control, the seventh conversation refused, runaway park, restart adoption — the real keeper, routes and CLI over a fake browser CLI), test-browser-mediation (raw CDP refused with zero server calls; a takeover pauses the ephemeral browser and an attachment alike), test-window-targets (both record shapes refused, an ordinary app still attaches), test-browser-housekeeping (the new section, zh + ja).

**Round 1 (after the adversarial verify, four reproduced findings).** ① `get --json cdp-url` — and `get -c cdp-url`, `get cdp-url --json`, the same line in a batch or after `--` — printed the raw CDP endpoint through `vibespace-browser`: the router took the word right after the verb as its noun, while the real 0.32.0 binary reads global flags anywhere. The noun is now the first non-flag word, and any `cdp-url` word of a `get` is refused. ② Every refused flag has an environment twin the real binary honours (`AGENT_BROWSER_CDP`, `_PROXY`, `_ARGS`, `_EXECUTABLE_PATH`, `_STATE`, `_PROFILE`, `_SESSION` …), and `vibespace-browser` passed the agent's shell straight through: `AGENT_BROWSER_CDP=1 vibespace-browser open …` connected where the variable said. The child environment is now built — every `AGENT_BROWSER_*` key of the shell dropped, the output-only ones kept, the session's own spawn pairs taken from the server (`/resolve` now answers `spawnEnv`, and `hostProfile` for a remote session's host-side scratch dir) — and a dropped key the agent added is named once on stderr (`[env_twin_dropped]`). ③ The attach refusal (T6) tested a `browser` field this branch's registry rows do not have, so a human-launched Chromium was still attachable; it now reads the rows' `category: 'browser'` too, proven against the real registry. ④ Route error strings still taught the hidden CLI — `switch_export_only` said to run `--state / --restore` on it, a failed profile start said "agent-browser open failed", the chromium provider was labelled "Chromium (agent-browser)"; they are reworded, and test-architecture §52b now counts the name in the route modules' strings. Gates: test-browser-verbs (the flag-ordered spellings, the env twins over a fake binary that dumps its env, a pre-fix patched copy as the control), test-browser-ephemeral (`spawnEnv` / `hostProfile`), test-window-targets (the real `DEFAULT_REGISTRY`, `gedit` the control), test-architecture §52b r1, test-browser-mediation-chrome ③ (heavy: the real binary answers the flag-ordered spelling and honours the CDP twin when run directly; through `vibespace-browser` the same shell lands on the lease's browser).

**Round 2 (after the second adversarial verify, four reproduced findings).** ① Round 1's "any `cdp-url` word of a `get`" refused legitimate reads — `get attr @e cdp-url` reads an attribute NAMED cdp-url and `get text cdp-url` an element of that name (the real 0.32.0 binary printed `zzz` and the element's text, never an endpoint). Only the NOUN decides now — but checking the proposed fix against the real binary showed the noun rule needed one more fact: a boolean global flag takes an optional `true`/`false` (`get --json true cdp-url` IS the raw endpoint; `get --json TRUE cdp-url` is "Unknown subcommand"), so a flag's `true`/`false` is skipped with it; every global value flag of the `--help` is in the router's table (a census fails on a missing one). (Round 1's `get -c cdp-url` never printed an endpoint: `-c` is a snapshot option, not a global flag — the binary answers "Unknown subcommand"; refusing it costs nothing.) ② The socket root was treated as an output setting: `export AGENT_BROWSER_SOCKET_DIR=/tmp/mine` (or `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`) reached the real binary, so the sanctioned command drove a daemon the keeper never launched, streams, traces or counts — or one the agent pre-started with any flag. The root is identity now: `/resolve` names the root the keeper's own runtime uses for that browser (`socketDir`, `runtimeDir`) and `vibespace-browser` sets it on the child last; a remote session (unmanaged) keeps only the short directory its host prelude exports (`hostSocketBase`, `<base>/vs-ab-<uid>`); the replaced variables are named once on stderr. ③ The attach refusal knew only the registry's firefox/chromium: a human's dialog-launched Chrome, Edge, Brave or flatpak Chromium was attachable. A browser is now recognised by name — the executable (`google-chrome-stable`, `microsoft-edge`, `brave-browser`, `x-www-browser` …), a flatpak / snap / env launcher's program, a reverse-DNS app id — and by the RUNNING app process's own executable (a wrapper the human typed execs into `chrome`); `chromium-thumbnailer`, GNU `infobrowser`, `gedit` stay attachable. ④ test-architecture §52b now scans every tracked `data/bin/vibespace-*` CLI (not two), the window-targets and browser-trace route/engine modules, and the agentd bundle (its only hits must be the user-only floor notice). Gates: test-browser-verbs (the noun and boolean-value legs, the `--help` global-option census, the socket-root legs over the fake binary, patched-copy controls for each), test-browser-ephemeral (per-kind `socketDir`, a decoy SOCKET_DIR through the shipped CLI lands on the keeper's root, the r1 table as the control), test-window-targets (a measured fixture of real browser executables, this machine's installed browsers, a wrapper decided by its running process, the r1 rule as the control), test-architecture §52b r2 (a planted name in a newly scanned module is the control), test-browser-mediation-chrome ③ (heavy: every spelling run through the real binary with the router held to its answer; another SOCKET_DIR is another daemon; through `vibespace-browser` the decoys stay empty; the heavy suite now removes its own daemon namespace directories).

**Round 3 (after the third adversarial verify, one major, one medium, two low and one informational finding — each reproduced first).** ① `vibespace-browser get --idle-timeout 5m cdp-url` printed the raw endpoint. `--idle-timeout` is a global value flag the real binary strips anywhere in the command, but its `--help` documents it only as an environment variable, so the round-2 census over the help's option sections never saw it and the router took its value `5m` for the noun. The router's flag tables are now **measured** off the binary itself (`scripts/browser-flag-census.mjs`: every flag-shaped string in the binary, run launch-free as `<flag> zzq9 session list` — 792 strings, 35 value flags, 19 booleans, checked in as `scripts/fixtures/browser-verbs/global-flags-0.32.0.json`; the heavy gate re-measures the installed binary and fails by name on a difference). `--idle-timeout` is also refused outright now (how long the browser lives is the keeper's decision, like its env twin). `get` passes only a noun it **reads** (text, html, value, attr, title, url, count, box, styles), so a value mistaken for the noun can never pass as a read, and a flag whose arity the table does not know is judged **both** ways — the command is refused if either reading reaches the endpoint or a refused verb. `get attr @e cdp-url` stays a read. ② A config **file** was the last twin of the refused launch flags: with no `AGENT_BROWSER_CONFIG` the binary searches `~/.agent-browser/config.json` and then `./agent-browser.json` in the directory the command runs from, and its launch keys ride every command — measured, a later `get title` from a directory holding `{"args":"--remote-debugging-port=41777"}` relaunched the running browser with that port open, and the rung-D generated config layered a session directory's `args` whole. Now the config is **named, never searched**: `/resolve` names the file the keeper runs that browser with (`config`: the browser's own generated config, else the keeper's `machine.json` / `machine-ephemeral.json`), every keeper call uses the same file, and `vibespace-browser` sets it last; where none is named (a session on another machine, an older server) the CLI composes one by the same rule into a private file and names it. The rule (`sanctionedConfig`): the machine's own `~/.agent-browser/config.json` is carried (the owner's `args`, proxy, executable, extensions, fence) minus `cdp` / `autoConnect` and minus every `--remote-debugging-*` / `--remote-allow-origins` / `--user-data-dir` / `--profile-directory` switch in `args`; an `agent-browser.json` in the agent's directory may only **narrow** the browser (`allowedDomains`, `actionPolicy`, `confirmActions`, `confirmInteractive`, `contentBoundaries`, `maxOutput`, and only where the machine's file sets none — it never replaces the owner's own fence) — its launch keys are dropped and said. ③ The §52b census of agent-facing route strings was a fixed list of nine modules; it is now every `src/routes/*.js` and every `src/server/{browser,window}-*.js` by glob, with its two user-only exceptions scoped to one function each. ④ A human's niche browser (surf, luakit, nyxt, dillo, netsurf, min, otter-browser, basilisk, icecat, cromite, zen, start-tor-browser, `firefox.real`) and `env -u NAME google-chrome` (the option's value was read as the program) are refused `browser_is_human` too; `arc` stays attachable — on Linux it is an archiver, the Arc browser has no Linux build. ⑤ On a remote session the CLI keeps the host prelude's short socket directory only when it is a real directory this user owns (lstat, as the prelude checks) — a planted symlink at the predictable name is dropped. Gates: test-browser-verbs (the measured tables, the noun allow-list, every-reading judgement, the config rule and the composed file, patched r2 copies as controls), test-browser-profiles (the generated config drops a project file's launch keys and every raw-debugging switch; the v2-r3 layering in a patched copy is the control), test-browser-ephemeral (the keeper launches with its named file, `/resolve` names the same one, a command from a directory with its own `agent-browser.json` runs with it; the pre-r3 keeper in a patched copy is the control), test-window-targets, test-architecture §52b r3, and test-browser-mediation-chrome (heavy: the installed binary re-measured; every measured flag fuzzed between `get` and `cdp-url` on a live daemon; a bare command from a directory with a hostile `agent-browser.json` runs its executable with its raw port while the same directory through `vibespace-browser` lands nothing; the suite's own runs no longer inherit the `AGENT_BROWSER_*` of the shell that starts them).

**Round 4 (after the fourth adversarial verify, one major, two medium, three low and one informational finding — each reproduced first).** ① Two page verbs printed exactly what `get cdp-url` is refused for. The real 0.32.0 binary launches EVERY browser with `--remote-debugging-port=0` (whatever the config says — round 3's rule only stripped a FIXED port), and `vibespace-browser open chrome://version` showed the browser's command line and profile directory, then `open file://<that directory>/DevToolsActivePort` its random port and browser GUID. A verb that navigates (`open` and the binary's own aliases `goto` / `navigate`, `tab new`, `window new`, `pushstate`, `diff url`, `read`, `vitals`, `record start`, any verb after `--`, every batch line) now goes to the web only: `file:`, `chrome:` / `chrome-*:`, `about:` other than `about:blank`, `view-source:`, `devtools:`, `javascript:`, `blob:`, `filesystem:`, a Chromium build's own `edge:` / `brave:` / `opera:` / `vivaldi:` pages and any other `x://` address are refused `local_scheme_refused` in every spelling the binary accepts (`FILE:`, `file:/x`, `file:x`, a tab inside the word), while a scheme-less host the binary makes `https://…` (`localhost:3000`) passes. Measured this round and fixed with it: `state load <file>` navigates to every origin its file lists, so a state file naming such an origin is refused too (the CLI reads the file the binary would). What remains is said plainly in the design and the manual: against an agent running as the same user, the rule restores only "the sanctioned road never prints it" — its own shell can still read the port off `ss -ltnp` or that file, which is the trust level the design already names; an `eval` navigation from a web page to `file://` is refused by the browser itself (measured). ② With `HOME` pointed elsewhere, an agent-written `~/.agent-browser/config.json` became "this machine's own configuration" wherever `/resolve` names no config (a remote session), and carried every launch key through the sanctioned road. The configuration is now the ACCOUNT's — its passwd home, never `$HOME` — and a `$HOME` that disagrees is refused `config_unavailable` naming both. ③ The stdin form of `batch` could never run: the binary reads stdin ONLY as a JSON array of string arrays, while the CLI judged it as shell lines — so the JSON form was refused and the plain form was the binary's `Invalid JSON input`. Both run now: JSON is judged element by element and handed over verbatim; plain lines are split, judged and handed over as the JSON of exactly those words. ④ An older server's answer (no spawn pairs, no config) no longer keeps the shell's `AGENT_BROWSER_CONFIG` — a config is composed. ⑤ `node scripts/browser-flag-census.mjs [<binary>]` works as documented (the positional binary was dropped without `--write`; a bare name is looked up on PATH, past the shim). ⑥ The flag table is trusted only on the version it was measured on: `vibespace-browser` reads the version off the binary it is about to run (launch-free, ~2 ms) and on any other build judges every flag both ways and says so once (`[flag_table_drift]`) — before any server call, so a refused command starts no browser. ⑦ The keeper names its own config file only while it is a regular file of this user with the content it wrote; a symlink or an edit swapped in is replaced. Gates: test-browser-verbs (every navigation spelling and its web controls, the state file, the stdin forms against a fake binary that — like the real one — reads only JSON, the passwd home with a `$HOME` that disagrees and once with no injection at all, the older-server config, the version gate, the census CLI; a patched round-3 copy is the control for each), test-browser-ephemeral (a symlink or an edit swapped in for the keeper's file is re-written; the round-3 check in a patched copy keeps naming the link), test-browser-mediation-chrome (heavy: bare, `chrome://version` + `file://…/DevToolsActivePort` and a crafted `state load` print the endpoint — the control — while every spelling through `vibespace-browser` is refused with no server call and the page never leaves the web; bare plain stdin lines are the binary's `Invalid JSON input` while both forms run through the CLI).

**The three browser faces are renamed (T5, direction B of docs/design-browser-faces.zh.md).** Three different things were all called "Browser" under one globe. Now each is named for who drives it: the toolbar's iframe is the **Web view** (网页视图 / ウェブビュー) and keeps the globe; the agent's browser is the **Agent browser** (Agent 浏览器 / エージェントブラウザ) everywhere it appears — the rail item, ⚙ Tools ▸ Agent browser…, its window and the "Agent browser (live)" views, the chat status-bar chip ("Agent browser · Shopping"), the session card's three commands, the Session Properties section and the Settings category — on the live view's window-with-a-dot glyph, defined once; a browser in the Apps catalog is sub-labelled **Browser app** (浏览器应用 / ブラウザアプリ), and the Apps dialog says the agent cannot reach an app you run. The phone's "+" sheet gains the two missing faces: Desktop app… and Agent browser (the current session's live view, or a pick of the sessions that hold a browser). Only names and icons changed — no window type, saved layout, settings key or rail id moved; rail items also gained an accessible name. The design, its mockups and their pixel verdicts come with it (docs/design-browser-faces.{zh.,}md, docs/mockups/browser-faces/).

Gates (chunk 3): test-browser-faces (new, fast: every face's label at its source with the ids pinned unchanged, the i18n census — every new key in zh and ja, no retired key orphaned —, the mockup-parity control 12/12 drawn with every shot's own control undrawn), the label pins in test-window-types / test-contributions / test-ax-paint / test-browser-housekeeping / test-profile-blindness (+ the heavy -chip leg) / test-mobile-gaps, and test-architecture §53 (the agent browser's glyph appears once in src/lib; a planted local copy is the control).

**Integration over 2.369.161–2.369.167.** Master's B-bfe6 (2.369.166, a browser as a desktop app) landed while the lane was open, and the two halves are now one rule: the window-targets engine refuses a desktop-app browser to agents at `open` (B-bfe6's registry-row / `url` / `keepProfile` refusal, now matching a row by `category: 'browser'` OR the `browser` kind) AND at `attach` / `snapshot` / `act` / `screenshot` / `watch` (T6 — by row, executable name, launcher program or running process); test-window-targets runs the real-registry leg on both row shapes (B-bfe6's rows carry the kind, the r1 miss was a category-only row) and puts the fake keeper's one launch id back after the open control (the browser it launched is the human's, so T6 rightly left it out of `list`). The Apps dialog keeps B-bfe6's **Browsers** section and its short dimmed reasons; the `Browser app ·` sub-label shows on a STARTABLE browser card only (design-browser-faces D7, decided at this merge), and the section's note now says "the Agent browser is separate" without the retired "(Browser profiles)" name (zh / ja and the heavy xpra-window pin follow). The lane's two census sections are renumbered after master's: the browser-takeover census is test-architecture §52 (§52a / §52b) and the one-glyph census §53. Master's §51 ("no suite writes a patched copy into the tree") judged `copyFileSync` by its SOURCE, so test-browser-verbs' controls — which copy `src/browser-verbs.js` OUT of the tree into a scratch dir — read as tree writes; the census now judges a write by its target (`writeFileSync`'s first argument, `copyFileSync`'s second), with a copy-out and a copy-in added to its negative control.
